senses.meaning_zh: 半脱位；关节或其他解剖结构未完全脱离正常位置的状态
senses.meaning_en: Partial dislocation of a joint or another anatomical structure.
senses.english_definition: A subluxation occurs when a joint or another anatomical structure moves partly, but not completely, out of its normal position.
senses.collocation_en: shoulder subluxation; joint subluxation
senses.collocation_zh: 肩关节半脱位；关节半脱位
senses.sentence_en: The scan showed a subluxation of the shoulder joint.
senses.sentence_zh: 扫描检查显示肩关节发生了半脱位。

etymology_story.zh: subluxation 来自新拉丁语 subluxatio，由 sub- 和表示“脱位”的 luxatio 构成，后者与拉丁语 luxare“使脱位”有关。这里的 sub- 表示程度不完全，因此整个词指部分脱位。
etymology_story.en: Subluxation comes from New Latin subluxatio, combining sub- with luxatio ‘dislocation’, related to Latin luxare ‘to dislocate’. Here sub- indicates an incomplete degree, giving the meaning ‘partial dislocation’.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：sub-（部分、不完全）＋luxation（脱位）→ subluxation；也可联系动词 subluxate 与名词后缀 -ion 理解。主要词族：subluxate（使半脱位；发生半脱位）、subluxates、subluxated、subluxating、subluxations；相关基础词有 luxate（使脱位）和 luxation（脱位）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: sub- ‘partial, incomplete’ + luxation ‘dislocation’ → subluxation; it can also be understood alongside the verb subluxate and the noun suffix -ion. Principal family forms are subluxate, subluxates, subluxated, subluxating, and subluxations; related base words are luxate and luxation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: partial dislocation（部分脱位）是最直接的同义表达；dislocation（脱位）在与 subluxation 对比时通常指完全脱位；instability（不稳定）指关节容易异常移位的状态，并不表示已经发生半脱位。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Partial dislocation is the closest equivalent; dislocation usually means complete displacement when contrasted with subluxation; instability describes a tendency toward abnormal movement and does not establish that a subluxation has occurred.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sub- 表示“不完全”：脱位了一部分，就是半脱位。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sub- signals incompleteness: displaced part of the way means subluxation.

meaning: 未加发酵剂的；未发酵的

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；音标按现代 IPA 排写。

forms: 形容词，无复数变化；通常不用比较级。
family: leaven 发酵剂；leavened 加发酵剂的

morphology.text: un-（未；不） + leaven（使面团发酵） + -ed → unleavened（未发酵的）。

etymology.text: 英语由 un- 和 leavened 构成；leaven 经古法语 levain 追溯到拉丁语表示“使升起”的词。没有使面团鼓起的发酵剂，就联想到薄平的饼。

usage_note: 常修饰 bread 或 dough；强调不用发酵剂，不等于没烤熟。

senses.meaning_zh: 未被幽默等因素调剂的；缺少轻松或活泼成分的
senses.meaning_en: Lacking a quality that would make something lighter or more enjoyable.
senses.english_definition: If something serious is unleavened by humour or another pleasant quality, it has none of that quality to make it lighter or more enjoyable.

etymology_story.zh: unleavened 由否定前缀 un- 加 leavened 构成；leaven 经古法语 levain 源于拉丁语 levamen，原有“使变轻之物”的意思，与 levare“举起、使变轻”有关。面团没有被“发起”的具体含义，进一步引申为严肃内容没有被幽默等因素调剂。
etymology_story.en: Unleavened combines negative un- with leavened; leaven came through Old French levain from Latin levamen ‘a means of lightening’, related to levare ‘to raise or lighten’. The literal absence of something that raises dough also supports the figurative meaning of lacking something that lightens serious material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：un-（不、未）＋leaven（使面团发起；调剂）＋-ed（分词形容词形式）→ unleavened。主要词族：leaven（发酵剂；使发起；调剂）、leavens、leavened、leavening（发酵剂；使发起的过程）、unleavened；本词的常用词性为形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: un- ‘not’ + leaven ‘make dough rise; lighten’ + -ed, forming a participial adjective → unleavened. Principal family forms are leaven, leavens, leavened, leavening, and unleavened. Unleavened is commonly used as an adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: yeast-free（不含酵母的）只排除酵母，仍可能使用其他膨松剂；unraised（未发起的）强调面团没有膨起的结果；unrelieved（未经调剂的）可对应比喻义，强调单调、严肃或不愉快的状态持续不变。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Yeast-free excludes yeast but may allow other raising agents; unraised emphasizes the result that dough has not risen; unrelieved overlaps with the figurative sense by describing seriousness, monotony, or unpleasantness without a moderating interruption.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: leaven 让面团发起，也让气氛轻松；un- 去掉它：饼不发，内容也少了调剂。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Leaven raises dough and lightens a mood; un- removes it, leaving bread unraised or serious material without relief.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；音标按现代 IPA 排写。

usage_note: 神话语境中与 nectar“神饮”相对；美式英语也指一种水果甜点，本课只考神食义。

senses.meaning_zh: 安布罗西亚水果沙拉；通常含橙子和椰丝的美式甜味水果沙拉
senses.meaning_en: an American sweet fruit salad typically containing oranges and coconut
senses.english_definition: Ambrosia is a sweet fruit salad, popular in the United States, that usually contains oranges and coconut and may also contain cream or marshmallows.

etymology_story.zh: 经拉丁语借自希腊语 ambrosia，意为“神食”，与 ambrotos“不朽的”有关，其历史构词包含表示否定的 a- 和表示“会死的”的成分。英语后来把它用于极其美味的食物，并用作一种美式水果沙拉的名称。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed through Latin from Greek ambrosia, meaning the food of the gods, the word is related to ambrotos, “immortal,” historically formed from a negative a- and an element meaning “mortal.” English later extended it to exceptionally delicious food and to a particular American fruit salad.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 ambrosia 是整体借入的名词，不宜把历史希腊语成分当作能自由组合的英语词缀。主要派生词：ambrosia 去掉末尾 a，再加 -al → ambrosial（美味如神食的；芳香宜人的）；ambrosial + -ly → ambrosially（美味如神食地；芳香宜人地）；常见组合有 ambrosia salad（安布罗西亚水果沙拉）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ambrosia is a borrowed noun treated as a whole base; its historical Greek elements are not freely productive English affixes. Principal derivatives are ambrosia minus final a + -al → ambrosial, “divinely delicious or fragrant,” and ambrosial + -ly → ambrosially; a common combination is ambrosia salad.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: delicacy 指珍馐或精致美食，不一定强调味道绝佳；nectar 原指神饮，形容美味时尤其用于饮料；heavenly food 是“天赐美味”的描述性近义表达，缺少 ambrosia 特有的古典神话色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Delicacy emphasizes a prized or special food rather than necessarily an exquisite taste; nectar originally denotes the gods’ drink and especially suits delicious liquids; heavenly food is a descriptive near-equivalent without ambrosia’s specific classical association.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “不朽”关联“不朽众神的食物”：神食 → 人间至味 → 以美味命名的水果沙拉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect “immortal” with the immortals’ food: divine food → extraordinary deliciousness → a fruit salad named for that deliciousness.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；音标按现代 IPA 排写。

forms: 本课为形容词，无复数变化；名词用法的复数为 anthropoids。
family: anthropoidal 似人的；anthropology 人类学

morphology.text: anthrop-（人，anthropo- 在元音前省去 o） + -oid（像……的） → anthropoid（似人的）。

etymology.text: 来自希腊语表示“像人、具有人形”的词，包含 anthrōpos“人”和表示形态相似的成分。看见人的轮廓就容易记住。

usage_note: 较正式，可用于人形、动物形态等描述；名词另可指高级灵长类，本课只学形容词。

senses.meaning_zh: 似人的；具有人形的；（动物学）猿猴类的
senses.meaning_en: humanlike in form; relating to the primate group containing monkeys, apes, and humans

senses.meaning_en: an ape; technically, a member of the primate group containing monkeys, apes, and humans
senses.english_definition: An anthropoid is an ape, or, in zoological classification, any member of the group that includes monkeys, apes, and humans.
senses.collocation_en: early anthropoids; the evolution of anthropoids
senses.collocation_zh: 早期猿猴类动物；猿猴类动物的演化
senses.sentence_en: The researchers compared the teeth of early anthropoids.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员比较了早期猿猴类动物的牙齿。

etymology_story.zh: 源自希腊语 anthrōpoeidēs“形似人的”，由 anthrōpos“人”和与 eidos“形态”有关的成分构成。英语既保留了“似人的”这一描述义，也把它用于灵长类动物的分类。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Greek anthrōpoeidēs, “human-shaped,” combining anthrōpos, “human,” with an element related to eidos, “form.” English retained the descriptive meaning “humanlike” and also adopted the word for primate classification.

morphology_enriched.zh: anthrop-（人；anthropo- 在元音开头的 -oid 前的形式）+ -oid（形似……的）→ anthropoid；形容词可直接转作名词，名词复数为 anthropoids。派生形容词 anthropoidal 表示“似人的；猿猴类的”，较少见；同根词包括 anthropology（人类学）、anthropologist（人类学家）、anthropological（人类学的）、anthropocentric（以人类为中心的）和 anthropomorphic（拟人的），它们并非都由 anthropoid 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Anthrop-—the form of anthropo-, “human,” before vowel-initial -oid—combines with -oid, “resembling,” to form anthropoid. The adjective also functions as a noun, with plural anthropoids; the derivative anthropoidal is uncommon. Related root-family words include anthropology, anthropologist, anthropological, anthropocentric, and anthropomorphic, though these are not all direct derivatives of anthropoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: humanlike 泛指外形或行为像人；humanoid 通常强调身体结构或轮廓像人，常用于机器人或虚构生物；simian 表示“猴或猿的”，与 anthropoid 的动物学含义接近，但不突出“似人”的直观意义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Humanlike broadly covers resemblance in appearance or behavior; humanoid usually emphasizes a human body plan, especially in robots or fictional beings; simian concerns monkeys and apes and approaches anthropoid’s zoological meaning without foregrounding human resemblance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: anthrop-＝人，-oid＝像：像人的 → 似人的猿；动物学中还可指包含猴、猿和人的整个类群。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anthrop- means “human” and -oid means “resembling”: human-shaped → humanlike apes, with a broader zoological use covering monkeys, apes, and humans.

usage_note: 不是牙齿，也不是真正的骨头；传统 whalebone 常指这种角质材料。

senses.meaning_zh: 鲸须；须鲸上颌垂下、用于滤食的角质板
senses.meaning_en: the keratin plates in a baleen whale’s mouth that filter food from water
senses.english_definition: Baleen consists of flexible plates hanging from a whale’s upper jaw that allow it to strain small animals from seawater.
senses.collocation_en: baleen plates; baleen whales
senses.collocation_zh: 鲸须板；须鲸

senses.sentence_zh: 鲸把水从鲸须间排出，将微小动物留在口中。

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语和古法语 baleine、balaine 等形式，追溯至拉丁语 balaena“鲸”。原本表示鲸的词在英语中专指鲸口中的滤食角质板；这种材料过去也用于制作紧身胸衣等物品。
etymology_story.en: Through Middle English and Old French forms such as baleine and balaine, baleen traces back to Latin balaena, “whale.” In English, the name became specialized for the filtering plates in a whale’s mouth, a material formerly used in items such as corsets.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 baleen 是不可再作常规词缀拆分的整体词，通常作不可数名词。相关形式有 baleened（有鲸须的）以及组合词 baleen whale（须鲸）、baleen plate（鲸须板）和 baleen-bearing（具有鲸须的）；baleen whale 中的 baleen 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern baleen is a whole lexical base without a productive prefix–root–suffix division and is normally uncountable. Related formations include baleened, “having baleen,” baleen whale, baleen plate, and baleen-bearing; in baleen whale, baleen is a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: whalebone 是鲸须的传统同义词，虽然含 bone，却不是真正的骨；baleen plates 强调一片片具体的鲸须板；filter plates 是说明其功能的描述性近义表达，本身并不专指鲸须。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Whalebone is the traditional synonym, although the material is not actual bone; baleen plates emphasizes the individual structures; filter plates is a descriptive near-equivalent that explains their function but is not specific to whales.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把历史词义“鲸”连接到鲸口中的“滤网”：鲸须是角质滤板。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical meaning “whale” with the whale’s mouth filter: baleen is its set of keratin filtering plates.

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 basso“低的；低音”，后者源于晚期拉丁语 bassus“低的”。表示高度低的词被用于音高，并进一步指低音声部和演唱这一声部的歌手。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian basso, “low; bass,” which descends from Late Latin bassus, “low.” A word for low height came to describe low pitch, then the bass part and the singer who performs it.

morphology_enriched.zh: basso 是整体借入的意大利语词，在现代英语中不宜把 -o 当作能产后缀；指歌手时复数可为 bassos 或 bassi。主要相关组合有 basso buffo（喜剧男低音歌手）、basso cantante（歌唱性男低音）、basso profondo 或英语化拼法 basso profundo（深沉男低音）和 basso continuo（通奏低音）；bass（低音；男低音）是同源词。
morphology_enriched.en: Basso is borrowed as a whole from Italian; its final -o is not a productive English suffix. For singers, the plural is bassos or bassi. Principal related expressions include basso buffo, “comic bass,” basso cantante, “singing or lyrical bass,” basso profondo or the anglicized basso profundo, “deep bass,” and basso continuo, “continuous bass”; bass is a cognate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bass 是现代英语中更通用的说法，还可表示低音乐器或低频声音；bass singer 明确指男低音歌手；basso profondo 指特别深沉的男低音类型，范围比 basso 窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bass is the more general modern English term and can also denote low instruments or low-frequency sound; bass singer explicitly identifies the vocalist; basso profondo denotes a particularly deep bass category and is narrower than basso.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: basso 的历史核心是“低”：音高低 → 低音声部 → 男低音歌手。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical core is “low”: low pitch → the bass part → the singer with that voice.

etymology_story.zh: 源自西班牙语 castañeta，常经法语 castagnette 传入英语；castañeta 是 castaña“栗子”的小称。响板圆润的外形使人联想到小栗子，因此获得这一名称。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Spanish castañeta, commonly transmitted through French castagnette; castañeta is a diminutive of castaña, “chestnut.” The instrument’s rounded shape suggested a little chestnut and supplied its name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 castanet 是整体借入的名词，不能把 -net 当作英语后缀；castanet + -s → castanets（响板，通常使用的复数形式）。常见组合有 castanet player（响板演奏者）和 castanet playing（响板演奏）；西班牙语 castañ- + -eta“小称”解释的是历史来源，不是现代英语构词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, castanet is a borrowed noun treated as a whole base; -net is not an English suffix here. Castanet + -s forms castanets, the usual plural. Common combinations include castanet player and castanet playing; Spanish castañ- + diminutive -eta explains the historical formation rather than modern English morphology.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clappers 是相互碰击发声器具的上位词，可涵盖响板；Spanish clappers 是响板的描述性近义表达；bones 指夹在手指间演奏的骨板类乐器，与响板相近，但形制不同，不能完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clappers is a broader term for instruments whose parts strike together; Spanish clappers is a descriptive near-synonym for castanets; bones names a related instrument held between the fingers, but its different shape prevents full interchangeability.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “小栗子”般的外形，加上两片碰击的咔嗒声：小栗子 → 响板。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture two little chestnut-shaped shells clicking together: little chestnuts → castanets.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自意大利语 contessa，即 conte“伯爵”的阴性形式，历史上可追溯至中世纪拉丁语 comitissa“女伯爵；伯爵夫人”。其称号最终与拉丁语 comes“同伴；随从”有关，该词后来发展为官职和贵族头衔。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian contessa, the feminine counterpart of conte, meaning “count,” historically traceable to Medieval Latin comitissa, meaning “countess.” The title ultimately belongs to the family of Latin comes, meaning “companion” or “attendant,” which developed into an official and noble title.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，contessa 是整体借入的名词，没有能产的英语词缀拆分；在意大利语内部可分析为 cont-（conte“伯爵”的词干）+ -essa（女性称谓后缀）。英语复数为 contessas，意大利语复数为 contesse；相关称谓有 conte“意大利伯爵”、count“伯爵”和 countess“女伯爵；伯爵夫人”，但它们不是由英语 contessa 派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, contessa is a borrowed noun with no productive English affix structure; within Italian, it can be analyzed as cont-, the stem of conte, meaning “count,” plus the feminine-title suffix -essa. The English plural is contessas, while the Italian plural is contesse; related titles include conte, count, and countess, but these are not English derivatives of contessa.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: countess“女伯爵；伯爵夫人”是最直接的英语对应词，不限定意大利背景；noblewoman“贵族女性”涵盖各种贵族等级；aristocrat“贵族成员”范围更广，也不限定性别。contessa 特指意大利称谓。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Countess is the closest English equivalent and does not require an Italian context; noblewoman covers women of various noble ranks; aristocrat is broader still and is not restricted to women. Contessa specifically identifies the Italian title.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: conte 是“伯爵”，意大利语女性称谓后缀 -essa 把它变成“女伯爵或伯爵夫人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with conte, “count”; the Italian feminine-title suffix -essa gives “countess.”

morphology.text: dis-（逆转；解除） + inter（埋葬） → disinter（掘出已埋葬的遗体）。

etymology.text: 来自法语 désenterrer，由表示逆转的成分和“埋葬”组成；“埋进去”的动作被倒过来，就成为“掘出来”。

usage_note: 较正式，通常用于已埋葬遗体；也有发掘旧资料的比喻义，本课只学本义。

senses.meaning_zh: 掘出已埋葬的遗体；起掘

senses.meaning_en: To bring something forgotten or hidden back to light.
senses.english_definition: If you disinter an old fact, document, or idea, you find it and bring it to people's attention again after it has been forgotten or hidden.

etymology_story.zh: disinter 由表示逆转的 dis- 与 inter“埋葬”构成；inter 经法语追溯至中世纪拉丁语 interrare，字面意思是“放入土中”，其中 terra 意为“土地”。“把埋葬的东西挖出来”后来引申为“重新发掘被遗忘的资料或往事”。
etymology_story.en: Disinter combines reversative dis- with inter, meaning “bury”; inter came through French from Medieval Latin interrare, literally “put into the earth,” from terra, meaning “earth.” The physical act of digging something up later supplied the figurative meaning of recovering forgotten material or events.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dis-（逆转）+ inter（埋葬）→ disinter。屈折形式为 disinters、disinterred、disinterring，派生名词为 disinterment“起掘；掘出”；相关词族包括 inter“埋葬”、interment“埋葬”、reinter“重新安葬”和 reinterment“重新安葬”。过去式和现在分词分别双写 r 后加 -ed、-ing。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: dis-, expressing reversal, + inter, meaning “bury,” → disinter. Inflected forms are disinters, disinterred, and disinterring; the derived noun is disinterment. Related family members include inter, interment, reinter, and reinterment. The final r is doubled before -ed and -ing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: exhume“掘出遗体”是字面义最接近的正式对应词；unearth“挖出；发现”适用范围更广，可指文物、事实或证据；uncover“揭露；发现”强调使隐藏的事物显现，不一定涉及挖掘。disinter 的比喻义通常带有“从久被遗忘的状态中重新带出”的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Exhume is the closest formal equivalent for removing a buried body; unearth applies more broadly to objects, facts, or evidence; uncover emphasizes revealing something hidden without necessarily suggesting digging. Figurative disinter particularly suggests bringing something back from long neglect or oblivion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: inter 是“埋进去”，dis- 把动作倒转：从土里掘出，也从遗忘中翻出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Inter puts something into the earth; dis- reverses it: dig it out of a grave or out of oblivion.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；音标按现代 IPA 排写。

morphology.text: fluor-（来自 fluor-spar“萤石”的词干） + -ine（化学元素名称后缀） → fluorine（氟）。

etymology.text: 19世纪由矿物名称 fluor-spar“萤石”加化学后缀 -ine 命名；名称根部与拉丁语表示“流动”的 fluor 有关。

usage_note: 指元素氟；fluoride 指氟化物，不能把牙膏中的氟化物说成装有游离氟。

senses.meaning_zh: 氟：元素符号为 F、原子序数为 9 的化学元素，其单质为淡黄色、反应性极强的气体
senses.meaning_en: The chemical element F, atomic number 9, whose elemental form is a highly reactive, pale-yellow gas.

etymology_story.zh: fluorine 于19世纪以 fluor“萤石”的名称成分加元素名称后缀 -ine 构成。fluor 最终与拉丁语 fluere“流动”有关，因为萤石曾用作冶炼助熔剂，帮助物料熔化流动。
etymology_story.en: Fluorine was formed in the nineteenth century from fluor, referring to fluorspar, plus the element-name suffix -ine. Fluor ultimately connects with Latin fluere, meaning “flow,” because fluorspar was used as a flux to help materials melt and flow during smelting.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：fluor-（与氟及萤石有关的词干）+ -ine（见于若干元素名称的后缀）→ fluorine。现代科学词汇使用结合形式 fluoro-；常用词族包括 fluoride“氟化物；氟离子”、fluorite“萤石”、fluorinate“使氟化”、fluorination“氟化”、fluorinated“经氟化的”、fluoridate“向……添加氟化物”、fluoridation“加氟化物处理”、fluorocarbon“氟碳化合物”和 hydrofluoric acid“氢氟酸”。这些词属于共同词根的词族，并非都由 fluorine 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Morphological analysis: fluor-, a stem associated with fluorine and fluorspar, + -ine, a suffix found in several element names, → fluorine. Modern scientific vocabulary uses the combining form fluoro-; common family members include fluoride, fluorite, fluorinate, fluorination, fluorinated, fluoridate, fluoridation, fluorocarbon, and hydrofluoric acid. These share a root family rather than all being direct derivatives of fluorine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该元素名称没有严格的普通词汇同义词。elemental fluorine“单质氟”明确指未与其他元素化合的氟；fluorine gas“氟气”特指气态单质 F₂；F 是元素符号。fluoride“氟化物；氟离子”表示另一类化学实体，不能与 fluorine 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no strict everyday lexical synonym for this element name. Elemental fluorine explicitly means fluorine uncombined with other elements; fluorine gas specifies gaseous F₂; F is the element symbol. Fluoride denotes a different class of chemical entities and is not interchangeable with fluorine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“助熔流动”记 fluor-：萤石帮助熔物流动，氟的名称由此而来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link fluor- with flow: fluorspar helped molten material flow and supplied fluorine's name.

pronunciation.note: 按英式非卷舌读音排写；美式有卷舌读法，词尾重读 /liː/。

forms: 通常不可数；美式拼写 hypercholesterolemia。
family: hypercholesterolaemic 高胆固醇血症的；cholesterol 胆固醇

etymology.text: 现代医学用希腊语来源的 hyper-“过高”、cholesterol“胆固醇”和 -aemia“血液状态”组合命名。字面线索就是血中胆固醇过高。

usage_note: 这是英式拼写，美式用 hypercholesterolemia；指胆固醇水平过高，不等于泛指任何血脂异常。

senses.meaning_zh: 高胆固醇血症：血液中的胆固醇水平异常升高
senses.meaning_en: An abnormally high level of cholesterol in the blood.
senses.english_definition: Hypercholesterolaemia is a condition in which the level of cholesterol in a person's blood is abnormally high.
senses.collocation_en: familial hypercholesterolaemia; severe hypercholesterolaemia

senses.sentence_zh: 血液检查显示她患有高胆固醇血症。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学术语，由希腊语来源的 hyper-“过高”、cholesterol“胆固醇”和 -aemia“血液状态”组合而成。cholesterol 的名称包含表示“胆汁”和“固体”的希腊语词根，因为这种物质早期从胆结石中得到研究；整个术语因此表示“血中胆固醇过高”。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term combines Greek-derived hyper-, meaning “excessive,” cholesterol, and -aemia, referring to a blood condition. Cholesterol contains Greek roots meaning “bile” and “solid,” reflecting early study of the substance in gallstones; the complete term therefore denotes excessive cholesterol in the blood.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hyper-（过高）+ cholesterol（胆固醇）+ -aemia（血液状态）→ hypercholesterolaemia。cholesterol 内部可进一步识别 chol(e)-“胆汁”、ster-“固体”和 -ol“醇”；-aemia 源自希腊语 haima“血液”。常用词族包括 cholesterol“胆固醇”、cholesterolaemia“血中胆固醇的存在或水平”、hypercholesterolaemic“高胆固醇血症的”和 hypocholesterolaemia“低胆固醇血症”；美式拼写为 hypercholesterolemia，相应形容词为 hypercholesterolemic。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hyper-, meaning “excessive,” + cholesterol + -aemia, indicating a blood condition, → hypercholesterolaemia. Cholesterol can be further analyzed into chol(e)-, “bile,” ster-, “solid,” and -ol, “alcohol”; -aemia comes from Greek haima, “blood.” Common family members include cholesterol, cholesterolaemia, hypercholesterolaemic, and hypocholesterolaemia. The American spelling is hypercholesterolemia, with the adjective hypercholesterolemic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: high blood cholesterol“血胆固醇过高”是最接近的日常表达；hyperlipidaemia“高脂血症”范围更广，包括胆固醇和甘油三酯等血脂升高；dyslipidaemia“血脂异常”还涵盖某些血脂过低或比例异常。因此后两者是相关的上位概念，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: High blood cholesterol is the closest everyday equivalent; hyperlipidaemia is broader and includes elevated blood lipids such as cholesterol or triglycerides; dyslipidaemia also covers certain low lipid levels or abnormal lipid patterns. The latter two are related broader terms rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hyper-＝过高，cholesterol＝胆固醇，-aemia＝血液状态：血中胆固醇过高。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hyper- means too high, cholesterol names the substance, and -aemia points to blood: too much cholesterol in the blood.

meaning: 无知的人；不学无术的人

pronunciation.note: 采用英式读音；音标按现代 IPA 排写。

forms: 可数名词，复数 ignoramuses；不用 ignorami。
family: ignorant 无知的；ignorance 无知

morphology.text: ignor-（拉丁语 ignorare“不知道”的词干） + -amus（第一人称复数动词词尾） → ignoramus（原意“我们不知道”）；现代英语作为独立名词记忆。

etymology.text: 借自拉丁语 ignoramus“我们不知道”，曾用于法律文书。17世纪戏剧把它用作无知人物的名字，后来成为“无知的人”的称呼。

usage_note: 带侮辱性，避免用来随意称呼别人；通常强调知识欠缺。

senses.meaning_zh: 无知的人；不学无术的人，带贬义或侮辱意味
senses.meaning_en: An ignorant or poorly informed person, used disapprovingly or insultingly.
senses.english_definition: If you call someone an ignoramus, you mean that they know very little, and you are expressing disapproval or insulting them.
senses.collocation_en: a complete ignoramus; an utter ignoramus
senses.collocation_zh: 一个十足的无知之徒；一个彻头彻尾的无知之徒
senses.sentence_en: I felt like a complete ignoramus when everyone started discussing classical music.
senses.sentence_zh: 大家开始讨论古典音乐时，我觉得自己简直一无所知。

etymology_story.zh: ignoramus 是拉丁语“我们不知道”，曾是英国大陪审团在认为起诉证据不足时所作的批注。该词后来成为对无知者的称呼，乔治·拉格尔1615年的拉丁语喜剧《Ignoramus》以此为无知律师命名，进一步传播了这一用法。
etymology_story.en: Ignoramus is Latin for “we do not know” and was once an endorsement used by English grand juries when they found insufficient grounds for an indictment. It later became a label for an ignorant person, and George Ruggle's 1615 Latin comedy Ignoramus, featuring an ignorant lawyer with that name, helped popularize the usage.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，ignoramus 是整体使用的可数名词，不按英语词缀进行能产拆分，标准复数为 ignoramuses。历史拉丁语分析为 ignor-（ignorare“不知道”的词干）+ -amus（此处表示现在时第一人称复数的词尾）；相关词根家族包括 ignore“忽视”、ignorance“无知”、ignorant“无知的”和 ignorantly“无知地”，但它们不是由英语名词 ignoramus 派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ignoramus is a count noun treated as a whole, with the standard plural ignoramuses and no productive English affix breakdown. Historically, Latin ignor- is the stem of ignorare, “not know,” and -amus here marks the first-person plural present tense. Related root-family words include ignore, ignorance, ignorant, and ignorantly, but these are not derivatives of the English noun ignoramus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dunce“笨学生；迟钝的人”侧重学习或理解困难；fool“傻瓜”更常批评判断和行为愚蠢；know-nothing“无知之徒”直接贬斥知识匮乏。ignoramus 尤其强调缺乏知识或见识，语气通常带嘲讽或侮辱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dunce emphasizes difficulty learning or understanding; fool more often criticizes poor judgment or foolish behavior; know-nothing directly disparages a lack of knowledge. Ignoramus particularly targets someone's lack of knowledge or understanding and usually sounds mocking or insulting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语“我们不知道”变成人物标签：一个什么都不知道的“无知之徒”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Turn the Latin “we do not know” into a label for a person: an ignoramus is someone who knows very little.

meaning: 言外行为的；与说话所实施的行为有关的

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

forms: 形容词；通常不用比较级。
family: illocution 言外行为；locution 表达方式

morphology.text: in-（在……之中，变为 il-）+ locution（说话）+ -ary（有关的）→ illocutionary（与说话所实施的行为有关的）。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语语言哲学中的造词，以拉丁语来源的 locution（说话）配合 in- 构成；想象一句话本身就在完成请求、承诺或警告。

usage_note: 用于语言学和语言哲学。illocutionary force 是一句话所具有的请求、承诺等行为力量；不等于说话造成的实际后果。

senses.meaning_zh: 言外行为的；与通过说话实施请求、承诺、警告等行为有关的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to an act performed in speaking, such as requesting, promising, or warning.
senses.english_definition: The illocutionary force of an utterance is the act a speaker performs by saying it, such as making a request or giving a warning.
senses.collocation_en: illocutionary act; illocutionary force
senses.collocation_zh: 言外行为；言外之力
senses.sentence_en: In this context, the question has the illocutionary force of a request.
senses.sentence_zh: 在这一语境中，这个问句具有提出请求的言外之力。

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于20世纪的言语行为理论，以表示“在……之中”的 in- 的变体 il- 与源自拉丁语的 locution（说话）为基础构成。其核心是人们“在说话中”实施的行为，如承诺或警告。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/illocutionary)
etymology_story.en: The word arose in twentieth-century speech-act theory, combining il-, a form of in- meaning 'in', with the Latin-derived locution, meaning speaking. It concerns acts performed in speaking, such as promising or warning. [Etymology reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/illocutionary)

morphology_enriched.zh: 共时构词可分析为 illocution（言外行为）+ -ary（……的）；历史构词涉及 il- + locution，而 il- 在这里不表示否定。主要词族：illocution（言外行为）、illocutionary（言外行为的）、illocutionarily（以言外行为的方式，较少见）；相关术语：locutionary（言内行为的）、perlocutionary（言后行为的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Synchronically, illocutionary can be analyzed as illocution + -ary, meaning 'relating to'; its historical formation involves il- + locution, with il- meaning 'in', not 'not'. Principal family members are illocution, illocutionary, and the less common adverb illocutionarily; related technical terms include locutionary and perlocutionary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全对应的常用近义词。相关词 pragmatic（语用的）范围更广，涉及语言在语境中的使用；performative（施为的）强调话语本身实施某种行为；communicative（交际的）泛指传递意义或进行交流。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym. Pragmatic broadly concerns language in context; performative emphasizes an utterance's performance of an act; communicative generally concerns conveying meaning or interacting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“在说中做”：说出“I promise”，就是在实施承诺。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember 'doing in saying': saying 'I promise' performs the act of promising.

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

forms: 常作不可数名词；指多次分裂可用 mitoses。
family: mitotic 有丝分裂的；mitotically 以有丝分裂方式

morphology.text: mit-（线）+ -osis（过程）→ mitosis（有丝分裂）；这是借入的科学术语，可联想分裂时可见的丝状结构。

etymology.text: 英语借自德语 Mitosis，由希腊语 mitos（线）与表示过程的 -osis 构成；名称抓住了细胞分裂时染色体呈丝状的画面。

usage_note: 生物学术语，侧重细胞核分裂。不要与产生生殖细胞时涉及的 meiosis（减数分裂）混淆。

senses.sentence_en: Many cells in growing tissues reproduce by mitosis.
senses.sentence_zh: 生长中的组织里，许多细胞通过有丝分裂增殖。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自德语 Mitosis，该术语由生物学家瓦尔特·弗莱明于1882年使用希腊语 mitos（线）和 -osis（过程）构成。名称指向分裂过程中可观察到的线状染色体结构。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/mitosis)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed German Mitosis, a term introduced by biologist Walther Flemming in 1882 using Greek mitos, 'thread', and -osis, a process suffix. The name refers to the threadlike chromosome structures visible during division. [Etymology reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/mitosis)

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词：mit-（线）+ -osis（过程）→ mitosis；不是普通英语自由词根与后缀的日常组合。主要词族：mitosis（有丝分裂）、mitoses（复数，/maɪˈtoʊsiːz/）、mitotic（有丝分裂的）、mitotically（通过有丝分裂地）、antimitotic（抑制有丝分裂的；有丝分裂抑制剂）、endomitosis（核内有丝分裂）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific formation: mit-, 'thread', + -osis, 'process', rather than an everyday combination of a free English root and suffix. Principal family members include mitosis, plural mitoses /maɪˈtoʊsiːz/, mitotic, mitotically, antimitotic, meaning inhibiting mitosis or an agent that does so, and endomitosis, nuclear division without ordinary completion of cell division.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关术语并非完全同义：cell division（细胞分裂）范围更广；karyokinesis（核分裂）强调细胞核的分裂；meiosis（减数分裂）通常使染色体数目减半，不能替代 mitosis。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms are not exact synonyms: cell division is broader; karyokinesis emphasizes division of the nucleus; meiosis normally halves the chromosome number and cannot replace mitosis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mit- 是“线”：染色体像线一样分开，两边各得一套。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mit- means 'thread': picture chromosome threads separating into two matching sets.

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

forms: 物质名词，通常不可数。
family: actomyosin 肌动球蛋白；actin 肌动蛋白（相关蛋白）

morphology.text: my-（肌肉）+ -ose + -in（物质名词后缀）→ myosin（肌球蛋白）；这是科学命名中的组合，词尾拼写合并。

etymology.text: 国际科学词汇，以希腊语来源的肌肉词根 my- 配合科学命名后缀组成；把它与肌肉中工作的蛋白质联系起来。

usage_note: 蛋白质名称。myosin 是肌球蛋白，actin 是肌动蛋白；两者名称和角色不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 肌球蛋白：利用 ATP 提供的能量沿肌动蛋白运动、参与肌肉收缩等过程的一类马达蛋白
senses.meaning_en: A family of motor proteins that use ATP to move along actin, contributing to muscle contraction and other cellular movements.
senses.english_definition: Myosin is a type of protein that uses energy from ATP to move along actin filaments, helping muscles contract and materials move inside cells.
senses.collocation_en: myosin heavy chain; myosin filaments
senses.collocation_zh: 肌球蛋白重链；肌球蛋白丝
senses.sentence_en: Myosin uses energy from ATP to pull on actin filaments during muscle contraction.
senses.sentence_zh: 肌肉收缩时，肌球蛋白利用 ATP 提供的能量牵拉肌动蛋白丝。

etymology_story.zh: 该名称属于国际科学词汇，以源自希腊语 mys（肌肉）的 my- 与科学命名成分 -ose、-in 构成。名称反映了它与肌肉的早期联系，而现代 myosin 也包括在非肌肉细胞中起作用的蛋白质。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/myosin)
etymology_story.en: The name belongs to international scientific vocabulary and combines my-, from Greek mys meaning 'muscle', with the scientific naming elements -ose and -in. It reflects an early association with muscle, although modern myosin also includes proteins functioning in nonmuscle cells. [Etymology reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/myosin)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代使用中通常把 myosin 作为完整的蛋白质名称；历史分析为 my-（肌肉）+ -ose + -in（物质名称后缀），中间的 e 在结合时脱落。主要相关构词：myosins（多种肌球蛋白）、actomyosin（肌动球蛋白复合物）、tropomyosin（原肌球蛋白）、paramyosin（副肌球蛋白）、nonmuscle myosin（非肌肉肌球蛋白）；这些名称不全指同一种蛋白质。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern use, myosin is normally treated as a complete protein name; its historical analysis is my-, 'muscle', + -ose + -in, a substance suffix, with the intermediate e dropped. Principal related formations include myosins, actomyosin, an actin–myosin complex, tropomyosin, a regulatory protein, paramyosin, a structural protein, and nonmuscle myosin; these names do not all denote the same protein.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格同义的常用名称。motor protein（马达蛋白）是上位类别；actin（肌动蛋白）形成供肌球蛋白相互作用的丝状结构；actomyosin（肌动球蛋白）指肌动蛋白与肌球蛋白形成的复合物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym. Motor protein is the broader category; actin forms filaments with which myosin interacts; actomyosin is a complex containing actin and myosin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: my- 联结“肌肉”：把肌球蛋白想成沿肌动蛋白轨道工作的微型马达。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect my- with muscle: picture myosin as a tiny motor working along an actin track.

senses.english_definition: The naira is the money used in Nigeria, and one naira is a basic unit of that money.

etymology_story.zh: naira 是20世纪由国名 Nigeria（尼日利亚）变形而来的货币名称。这个经过改造的国名后来成为该国基本货币单位的名称。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/naira)
etymology_story.en: Naira is a twentieth-century currency name formed by altering Nigeria. This reshaped country name became the name of the country's basic monetary unit. [Etymology reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/naira)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可进一步按常用词缀拆分的单纯词。复数为 naira 或 nairas，金额后常用不变形式，如 five hundred naira（五百奈拉）；常见复合形式为 naira-denominated（以奈拉计价的）。没有常用的独立动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, naira is a simple word without a productive internal affix breakdown. Its plurals are naira and nairas, with the unchanged form common after amounts, as in five hundred naira; a common compound is naira-denominated, meaning expressed in naira. It has no common independent verb or adjective derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Nigerian currency（尼日利亚货币）是语境中的释义表达；currency（货币）泛指一国或地区使用的货币；money（钱）范围更广。三者都不能在精确金额中直接替代计量单位 naira。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nigerian currency is a contextual paraphrase; currency refers generally to a monetary system or its money; money is broader still. None directly replaces naira as the unit in a precise amount.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Nigeria → naira：国家名称变形，记住“尼日利亚的钱”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nigeria → naira: a reshaped country name identifies Nigeria's money.

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

etymology.text: 经新拉丁语、拉丁语传入英语，源头是希腊语 oryx，曾指羚羊等长角动物；可联想它醒目的长角。

usage_note: 可数动物名。剑羚属于羚羊类，不是鹿；不要把所有羚羊都叫 oryx。

senses.meaning_en: A large antelope of the genus Oryx, native to Africa or Arabia and having long, slender horns.
senses.english_definition: An oryx is a large antelope from Africa or Arabia that has long, narrow horns and usually a pale coat with contrasting markings.
senses.collocation_en: Arabian oryx; scimitar-horned oryx
senses.collocation_zh: 阿拉伯剑羚；弯角剑羚

senses.sentence_zh: 一只阿拉伯剑羚站在沙丘上，长角的轮廓映衬在天空中。

etymology_story.zh: 英语经新拉丁语和拉丁语承接希腊语 oryx，这个古老名称曾用于指某些羚羊等动物，并与表示“挖掘”的希腊语动词有关。现代动物学将它用于剑羚属及其动物。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/oryx)
etymology_story.en: English received the word through New Latin and Latin from Greek oryx, an ancient name applied to certain antelopes and other animals and related to a Greek verb meaning 'dig'. Modern zoological usage applies it to the genus Oryx and its animals. [Etymology reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/oryx)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为单纯借词，不宜拆成具有现代英语意义的词根和词缀。复数为 oryx 或 oryxes；可按需构成 oryx-like（像剑羚的），但它不是常用固定派生词。Arabian oryx（阿拉伯剑羚）和 scimitar-horned oryx（弯角剑羚）属于物种名称组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, oryx is a simple loanword without a useful English root-and-affix division. Its plurals are oryx and oryxes; oryx-like, meaning resembling an oryx, is a possible productive formation rather than a common established derivative. Arabian oryx and scimitar-horned oryx are species-name combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: antelope（羚羊）是上位词；gemsbok（南非剑羚）指一种具体的剑羚；gazelle（瞪羚）通常指体形较纤细的另一类羚羊，并非 oryx 的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Antelope is the broader term; gemsbok names a particular species of oryx; gazelle usually denotes a different, more lightly built kind of antelope and is not a synonym of oryx.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词配图记忆：浅色大羚羊，头顶两支长角；不要硬拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Learn the whole word with an image: a large pale antelope with two long horns, without forcing an English root breakdown.

senses.sentence_en: Her cheeks were pinking with embarrassment.

senses.meaning_en: Abnormal engine combustion accompanied by a metallic knocking sound.
senses.english_definition: Pinking is a metallic knocking sound caused by abnormal combustion in a petrol engine.
senses.collocation_en: engine pinking; pinking under load

senses.pos: v. 动词（现在分词；英式英语，汽车技术）
senses.meaning_zh: 发动机正在爆震并发出金属敲击声
senses.meaning_en: Producing metallic knocking sounds through abnormal engine combustion.
senses.english_definition: If an engine is pinking, abnormal combustion is making it produce a metallic knocking sound.

senses.collocation_zh: 加速时发生爆震；负荷下发生爆震

etymology_story.zh: 剪裁义 pink 可追溯到中古英语中表示刺孔或切出装饰性花纹的用法，其更早来源并不确定。颜色义由石竹花的名称发展而来，发动机义则源于模仿金属敲击声的另一个 pink，因此这些意义不能归为同一条已证实的词源。
etymology_story.en: The cutting verb pink goes back to Middle English uses involving piercing or cutting decorative patterns, but its earlier origin is uncertain. The colour sense developed from the flower name pink, whereas the engine sense comes from a sound-imitating verb, so these meanings do not share one established origin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：pink + -ing，构成动作名词或现在分词；不同义项分别对应剪裁、颜色变化和发动机爆震。相关形式：pink、pinks、pinked、pinking；颜色词族另有 pinkish（略带粉红的）、pinkness（粉红的状态）、pinker／pinkest（更粉红／最粉红）；pinking shears 中 pinking 作前置修饰语，不必另立形容词词性。CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方逐词定级；未核实具体考试词表收录。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: pink + -ing, forming an action noun or present participle; the different senses belong to cutting, colour change, and engine knocking. Related forms are pink, pinks, pinked, and pinking; the colour family also includes pinkish, pinkness, and the comparative and superlative pinker and pinkest. In pinking shears, pinking is a premodifier and does not require a separate adjective classification. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level rating; inclusion in specific examination lists has not been verified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: notching（切出缺口）强调逐个缺口；zigzag cutting（锯齿状剪裁）强调边缘形状；knocking（发动机爆震）对应汽车义，不能替换剪裁义或颜色义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Notching emphasizes making individual cuts; zigzag cutting emphasizes the resulting edge pattern; knocking corresponds to the engine sense and cannot replace the cutting or colour senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先认语境：剪刀旁是“锯齿裁边”，脸颊旁是“泛粉红”，发动机旁是“爆震”；-ing 表示过程或正在发生。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the context: scissors mean notched edges, cheeks mean turning pink, and an engine means knocking; -ing presents the process or ongoing action.

senses.meaning_zh: 菱形肌；位于上背部、连接脊柱与肩胛骨的肌肉

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语追溯到希腊语 rhomboeidēs，意为“像菱形的”，由 rhombos（菱形）和表示“形似”的成分组成。它后来也用于命名轮廓近似菱形的背部肌肉。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Latin from Greek rhomboeidēs, meaning 'resembling a rhombus', formed from rhombos and an element meaning 'having the form of'. It was also applied to back muscles with a roughly diamond-shaped outline.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：rhomb-（菱形）+ -oid（形似……的）；相关词包括 rhomboidal（菱形的）、rhomboidally（呈菱形地）、rhombus（菱形，复数 rhombuses 或 rhombi）和 rhombic（菱形的）。rhomboid 的复数为 rhomboids；解剖名称包括 rhomboid major（大菱形肌）和 rhomboid minor（小菱形肌）。CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方逐词定级；未核实具体考试词表收录。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: rhomb- 'rhombus' + -oid 'resembling'. Related words include rhomboidal, rhomboidally, rhombus, with plurals rhombuses or rhombi, and rhombic. The plural of rhomboid is rhomboids; anatomical names include rhomboid major and rhomboid minor. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level rating; inclusion in specific examination lists has not been verified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: parallelogram（平行四边形）是范围更大的类别；rhombus（菱形）要求四边等长，与传统严格意义的 rhomboid 有别；diamond-shaped（菱形的）是较宽泛的外形描述，不保证满足特定几何条件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Parallelogram names the broader category; rhombus requires four equal sides and differs from rhomboid in its traditional strict sense; diamond-shaped is an informal description that does not guarantee particular geometric properties.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: rhomb- 是“菱形”，-oid 是“像”：记住“像菱形的轮廓”，再联想到同形的背部肌肉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rhomb- points to a rhombus and -oid means 'resembling': picture the slanting outline, then the similarly shaped back muscles.

morphology.text: rictus 作为独立词素记忆；派生：rictus + -like → rictus-like（像僵硬咧嘴表情的）。

etymology.text: 英语借自新拉丁语 rictus，沿用拉丁语“张开的嘴”的意思，相关动词 ringi 意为张嘴；由张嘴的形状联想到僵住的笑容。

usage_note: 偏书面、文学用语。常说 a rictus of fear 或 a fixed rictus；并不表示愉快自然的微笑。

senses.meaning_zh: 僵硬的咧嘴表情；露齿的僵笑
senses.meaning_en: A fixed, unnatural grin or grimace, often exposing the teeth.
senses.english_definition: A rictus is a stiff, unnatural expression in which someone's mouth is stretched into a grin, often because of fear or pain.
senses.collocation_en: a fixed rictus; a rictus of pain
senses.collocation_zh: 僵住的咧嘴表情；痛苦造成的龇牙表情
senses.sentence_en: His mouth was drawn into a rictus of pain.
senses.sentence_zh: 他的嘴因疼痛而扭成了僵硬的龇牙表情。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用拉丁语 rictus，原指张开的嘴或口裂，与 ringī（龇牙、张嘴咆哮）有关。英语常用义由张口露齿的外形发展为因痛苦、恐惧等形成的僵硬咧嘴表情。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin rictus, meaning an open mouth or gape, related to ringī, 'to bare the teeth or snarl'. The usual English sense developed from that exposed-mouth shape into a fixed grin or grimace associated with pain, fear, or similar emotions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 rictus 作为整体词基处理，不宜强行拆成常见英语词根和后缀；复数可用 rictuses，也可保留 rictus。相关形式包括专业形容词 rictal（口裂的）和描述性复合词 rictus-like（像僵硬咧嘴表情的），没有丰富的常用派生词族。CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方逐词定级；未核实具体考试词表收录。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, rictus is best treated as an unanalyzed base rather than divided into familiar English roots and suffixes; its plural can be rictuses or unchanged rictus. Related forms include the technical adjective rictal, referring to a gape, and the descriptive compound rictus-like; there is no extensive common derivative family. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level rating; inclusion in specific examination lists has not been verified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grin（咧嘴笑）本身未必僵硬或痛苦；grimace（扭曲的表情）范围较广，常表示疼痛或厌恶；rictus 特别突出嘴部僵住、拉开的不自然状态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A grin need not be stiff or painful; a grimace is a broader facial distortion expressing pain or disgust; rictus specifically emphasizes an unnaturally stretched, fixed mouth.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住拉丁语“张开的嘴”：嘴咧开又僵住，就是 rictus。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep the Latin image of an open mouth: stretch it into a grin and freeze it to picture a rictus.

senses.pos: v. 动词（古体第三人称单数现在时）
senses.meaning_zh: 说；says 的古体形式，现见于古典引文、宗教文体或仿古表达
senses.meaning_en: An archaic form of says, used in older texts and deliberately archaic language.
senses.english_definition: Saith is an old form of says that you find in religious or literary texts and in language that imitates them.

etymology_story.zh: saith 是本土英语动词 say 的历史屈折形式，所属词系可追溯到古英语 secgan（说）。它在中古英语时期形成，与带旧式第三人称单数词尾的较完整形式有关，后来在普通现代英语中被 says 取代，但保留于宗教和文学语言。
etymology_story.en: Saith is a historical inflected form of the native English verb say, whose ancestry goes back to Old English secgan. It developed in Middle English alongside fuller forms with the older third-person singular ending and was later replaced by says in ordinary English, while surviving in religious and literary language.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史形态上，saith 是 say 的缩合式第三人称单数现在时，与 sayeth 及旧式词尾 -(e)th 有关；它不是现代英语中可自由套用的派生形式。所属词族和屈折形式包括 say、says、said、saying（也可作名词，意为格言或说法）、sayer（说话者）及复合词 soothsayer（预言者）、naysayer（惯于反对者）。CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方逐词定级；未核实具体考试词表收录。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, saith is a contracted third-person singular present form of say, related to sayeth and the older ending -(e)th; it is not a freely productive modern derivative. The family and inflected forms include say, says, said, saying, also a noun meaning a proverb or expression, sayer, and compounds such as soothsayer and naysayer. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level rating; inclusion in specific examination lists has not been verified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: says（说）是现代英语中的直接对应形式；declares（宣告）语气更郑重；states（陈述）强调明确表达内容，后两者都不像 saith 那样自带古体色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Says is the direct modern equivalent; declares suggests a more emphatic or formal announcement; states emphasizes explicit expression, and neither of the latter inherently carries the archaic tone of saith.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 saith，就把旧词尾换成现代的 -s：he saith = he says。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Replace the old ending with modern -s: he saith means he says.

etymology_story.zh: subtend 源自拉丁语 subtendere，由 sub-（在下面）和 tendere（伸展）组成，原有“在下方伸展”的意思。几何义把这种空间关系用于角及其对边或对应弧，植物学义则保留了位于另一结构下方的关系。
etymology_story.en: Subtend comes from Latin subtendere, formed from sub- 'under' and tendere 'to stretch', giving the idea of stretching beneath. Geometry applies this spatial relationship to an angle and its opposite side or corresponding arc, while botany retains the relationship of lying below another structure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 词源及形态分析：sub-（在下面）+ -tend（伸展，拉丁来源的词根，并非“照料”义 tend）；屈折形式为 subtends、subtended、subtending，相关名词为 subtension（张角关系；张角）。同源词包括 extend（延伸）、distend（使膨胀）和 tension（张力），它们属于较大的同源词群，并非都由 subtend 直接派生。CEFR-C2 为学习难度估计，并非已核实的官方逐词定级；未核实具体考试词表收录。
morphology_enriched.en: Etymological and morphological analysis: sub- 'under' + -tend 'stretch', a Latin-derived root distinct from tend meaning 'care for'. Inflected forms are subtends, subtended, and subtending; the related noun is subtension. Extend, distend, and tension belong to the wider etymological family rather than being direct derivatives of subtend. CEFR-C2 is an estimated learning level, not a verified official word-level rating; inclusion in specific examination lists has not been verified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: lie opposite（位于对面）强调边与角的相对位置；form an angle at（在某点形成角）解释从指定点观察到的几何关系；underlie（位于下方）接近植物学义，但不能精确替代几何术语 subtend。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Lie opposite emphasizes the position of a side relative to an angle; form an angle at explains the geometry from a specified point; underlie approaches the botanical sense but is not an exact substitute for the geometric term subtend.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sub- 在下，-tend 伸展：想象三角形底边在顶角对面展开；植物学中则想象花下的一片苞片。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sub- means 'under' and -tend means 'stretch': picture a triangle's base stretching opposite its top angle, or a bract sitting below a flower.

meaning: 圣餐变体论；天主教关于饼酒实体转变的教义
aliases: 饼酒实体转变的圣餐教义

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

morphology.text: trans-（转变）+ substanti-（实体）+ -ation（过程或概念）→ transubstantiation（实体转变的教义）。

usage_note: 宗教术语，特指天主教圣餐教义；不宜泛指任何物质的变化，也不等于仅作象征解释。

senses.meaning_zh: 圣餐变体；圣餐中饼酒的实体转变为基督身体和血、而外在形态不变的教义
senses.meaning_en: The change of the substance of Eucharistic bread and wine into Christ's body and blood while their outward appearances remain unchanged.
senses.english_definition: Transubstantiation is the change which, according to Roman Catholic teaching, makes the bread and wine in the Eucharist become Christ's body and blood while keeping their outward appearances.
senses.collocation_en: the doctrine of transubstantiation; belief in transubstantiation
senses.collocation_zh: 圣餐变体教义；对圣餐变体的信仰
senses.sentence_en: The priest explained the doctrine of transubstantiation to the class.
senses.sentence_zh: 神父向班上的学生解释了圣餐变体教义。

etymology_story.zh: 英语经中古英语借入相关词形，源头是中世纪拉丁语 transubstantiatio，相关动词 transubstantiare 由 trans-（转变、越过）和 substantia（实体）构成。其神学含义强调饼酒的实体发生转变，而可感知的外在形态保持不变。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Middle English from medieval Latin transubstantiatio, related to transubstantiare, formed from trans- indicating change and substantia meaning substance. Its theological meaning concerns a change of substance while the perceptible outward appearances remain unchanged.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 transubstantiate（使实体转变）去掉词尾 -e，再加 -ion，形成 transubstantiation（实体转变；圣餐变体）；词干内部可辨认 trans-（转变）和 substanti-（实体）。词族包括 transubstantiate（使发生圣餐变体）、transubstantiated（其过去式和过去分词）、transubstantiating（其现在分词）、transubstantiational（圣餐变体的）和 transubstantiationist（圣餐变体论信奉者）；后两者较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is transubstantiate minus final -e plus -ion, producing transubstantiation; the stem contains recognizable trans- indicating change and substanti- meaning substance. The family includes transubstantiate, transubstantiated, transubstantiating, transubstantiational meaning relating to transubstantiation, and transubstantiationist meaning an adherent of the doctrine; the last two are uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的普通近义词：transformation（转变）泛指形态或性质变化；transmutation（质变）强调一种东西变成另一种；conversion（转化）范围更广，在宗教语境中还可指皈依。这些词都不能单独准确替代这一特定教义名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym: transformation broadly describes a change in form or character; transmutation emphasizes one thing becoming another; conversion is broader and can also mean adopting a religion. None alone precisely names this particular doctrine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: trans- 转变 + substance 实体：改变的是“实体”，外观仍是饼和酒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect trans- with change and substance with underlying reality: the substance changes while the appearances remain.

meaning: 外来的；偶然附加而非本来固有的

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

family: adventitiously 偶然地；adventitiousness 偶生性

morphology.text: advent-（到来）+ -itious（形容词后缀）→ adventitious（外来附加的）；词义不是“爱冒险的”。

etymology.text: 借自拉丁语 adventicius（从外面来的），相关动词 advenire 意为来到；把它想成后来从外部加入的东西。

usage_note: 较正式，常修饰 influences、factors 等。本课教外来附加义；植物学中的 adventitious roots 是不定根。

senses.meaning_zh: 外来的；非固有的；偶然附加的
senses.meaning_en: Coming from outside or arising incidentally rather than being inherent.
senses.english_definition: Something adventitious comes from an outside source or happens incidentally, rather than being a natural or essential part of something.
senses.collocation_en: adventitious contamination; adventitious factors
senses.collocation_zh: 外源性污染；偶然介入的因素
senses.sentence_en: The analysis distinguished the material's original components from adventitious contamination.

senses.meaning_zh: 不定的；从非通常部位生长出来的
senses.meaning_en: Developing in an unusual position, especially of plant roots or buds.
senses.english_definition: Adventitious roots or buds grow from parts of a plant where roots or buds do not usually develop.
senses.collocation_en: adventitious roots; adventitious buds
senses.collocation_zh: 不定根；不定芽
senses.sentence_en: The cutting developed adventitious roots along its stem.
senses.sentence_zh: 这根插条沿着茎长出了不定根。

etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 adventicius 或 adventitius，意为外来的、从外部加入的，最终与 advenire（来到）有关。由“后来从外面到来”发展出“非固有、偶然附加”的意思，植物学又将其用于出现在非通常部位的根和芽。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin adventicius or adventitius, meaning foreign or coming from outside, ultimately related to advenire, meaning to arrive. The idea of something arriving from elsewhere developed into the sense of being incidental or nonessential, with a botanical extension to roots and buds arising in unusual places.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析可记为 adventiti-（拉丁语来源的借入词干）+ -ous（形容词后缀），不宜把它误拆成表示“冒险”的词。直接词族：adventitious（外来的；不定的）、adventitiously（偶然地；以不定方式）、adventitiousness（外来性；偶然附加性）；advent（到来）与其有历史词源联系，但不是它的现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: A practical modern analysis is adventiti-, a borrowed Latin stem, plus the adjective ending -ous; the word does not mean adventurous. Its direct family is adventitious, adventitiously, and adventitiousness; advent shares a historical source but is not a modern derivative of adventitious.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: extrinsic（外在的）强调来自事物本身之外；incidental（附带的）强调不是主要或必需部分；accidental（偶然的）强调未经计划。adventitious 可兼有外来和偶然附加之意，但这些普通词不能替代其植物学术语义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Extrinsic emphasizes an origin outside the thing itself; incidental emphasizes a secondary or nonessential role; accidental emphasizes lack of intention or planning. Adventitious can combine external origin with incidental addition, but these ordinary synonyms do not replace its technical botanical meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 后来“到来”的，不是原来固有的；根长到非常规位置，就是不定根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Something that arrives later is not inherent; a root appearing in an unexpected place is adventitious.

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

forms: 介词，无屈折变化；常保留法语重音拼写 après。

morphology.text: apres 作为独立词素记忆；复合：apres + ski → apres-ski（滑雪后的活动）；规范法语式拼写为 après-ski。

etymology.text: 借自法语 après，追溯到古法语 apres 与晚期拉丁语 ad pressum（靠近）；由紧接在后联想到“在……之后”。

usage_note: 英语中的法语借词，常写 après，多用于休闲社交或复合修饰语；普通日常表达用 after 更常见。本卡保留无重音拼写 apres。

etymology_story.zh: apres 是法语 après 的无重音符号写法；法语词经古法语 apres 追溯到拉丁语 ad pressum，原有“靠近、紧接”的意思，后来发展为时间上的“在……之后”。英语中表示滑雪后娱乐的名词用法，则是 après-ski 的缩略形式。
etymology_story.en: Apres is an unaccented spelling of French après, which developed through Old French apres from Latin ad pressum, conveying closeness and later temporal succession. The English noun referring to social activity after skiing is a shortening of après-ski.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 après／apres 视为不可再拆的借词；après + ski 构成 après-ski（滑雪后的娱乐活动），再截短为名词 après。常见相关形式有 après-ski、après ski 和 apres-ski；这些主要是复合形式或拼写变体，没有常用的后缀派生词族；après drinks 中的 après 是名词作前置修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats après or apres as an unanalyzed borrowing; après plus ski forms après-ski, which can then be shortened to the noun après. Related forms include après-ski, après ski, and apres-ski, chiefly compounds or spelling variants rather than a productive suffix-based family; in après drinks, après is a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 介词义近 after（在……之后），但 after 是日常中性表达，après 带有明显法语或风格化色彩；名词义近 après-ski（滑雪后的娱乐活动），这是较完整的表达；post-ski socializing（滑雪后社交）是说明性短语，不是同样固定的词项。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the preposition, after is the neutral everyday equivalent, while après has a distinctly French or stylistic flavor. For the noun, après-ski is the fuller equivalent; post-ski socializing explains the activity without being the same established lexical item.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 après-ski 记成“滑雪之后”；省去 ski，仍可指滑雪后的聚会。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember après-ski as after skiing; drop ski and après can still mean the socializing afterward.

etymology_story.zh: 源于希腊语 archaios（古老的），并与 archē（开端）有关，英语在十九世纪将其用于极古老地层和地质时期的命名。随着地质年代体系的发展，Archaean 成为太古宙的名称之一，Archean 是另一种通行拼写。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Greek archaios, meaning ancient, related to archē, meaning beginning, and entered nineteenth-century geological terminology for very ancient rocks and time. As geological classification developed, Archaean became a name for the eon also commonly spelled Archean.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可识别为 archae-（古老）+ -an（属于……的），形成形容词 Archaean；形容词名词化后，the Archaean 指太古宙。直接相关形式包括拼写变体 Archean，以及分期名称 Eoarchaean（始太古代）、Palaeoarchaean（古太古代）、Mesoarchaean（中太古代）和 Neoarchaean（新太古代）；相应的 -archean 拼写也通行。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be recognized as archae- meaning ancient plus -an meaning relating to; nominal use produces the Archaean, the name of the eon. Related forms include the spelling variant Archean and the subdivision names Eoarchaean, Palaeoarchaean, Mesoarchaean, and Neoarchaean; corresponding spellings with -archean are also used.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Archean 是同义拼写变体；ancient（古老的）只是宽泛描述，不能精确指定地质年代；Precambrian（前寒武纪的／前寒武纪）范围更大，涵盖太古宙及其他前寒武纪地质时期。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Archean is an equivalent spelling; ancient is a broad description that does not specify a geological interval; Precambrian covers a much broader span that includes the Archaean and other geological time before the Cambrian.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: archae- 表示“古老”：Archaean 就是地球极古老历史中的太古宙。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link archae- with ancient: the Archaean belongs to Earth's very ancient history.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学由拉丁语来源成分组合而成的词：cerebro- 来自 cerebrum（脑），vascular 最终来自 vasculum（小容器）。词义由两个成分直接组合，专指与脑部血管及供血有关的事物。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical compound combines Latin-derived cerebro-, from cerebrum meaning brain, with vascular, ultimately from vasculum meaning a small vessel. The combined meaning specifically concerns the brain's blood vessels and blood supply.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词公式为 cerebro-（脑）+ vascular（血管的）；vascular 内部可分析为 vascul-（小血管、容器）+ -ar（……的）。直接相关名词为 cerebrovasculature（脑血管系统）；构词成分的常见词族包括 cerebrum（大脑）、cerebral（大脑的）、vascular（血管的）、vasculature（血管系统）、vascularity（血管分布或丰富程度）和 vascularization（血管形成）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is cerebro- meaning brain plus vascular meaning relating to blood vessels; vascular contains vascul- meaning a small vessel and -ar meaning relating to. A directly related noun is cerebrovasculature, the brain's vascular system; component families include cerebrum, cerebral, vascular, vasculature, vascularity, and vascularization.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的单词近义词：cerebral（脑的）范围更广，不限于血管；vascular（血管的）可用于全身任何部位；neurovascular（神经血管的）涉及神经系统与血管的关系，也不限于脑部。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact single-word synonym: cerebral concerns the brain generally, rather than specifically its vessels; vascular concerns blood vessels anywhere in the body; neurovascular concerns relationships between nerves or the nervous system and blood vessels, extending beyond the brain.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cerebro- 脑 + vascular 血管的：把“脑”和“供血管道”连在一起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cerebro- means brain and vascular means blood-vessel-related: picture the brain and its supply pipes.

usage_note: 正式用语，常说 exculpate someone 或 exculpate someone from blame；不是证明其有罪。

senses.meaning_zh: 证明某人无罪或无过错；为某人开脱罪责
senses.meaning_en: to clear someone of blame or establish their innocence
senses.english_definition: If evidence exculpates someone, it shows that they are not guilty of an offence or responsible for something wrong.

etymology_story.zh: 源自中世纪拉丁语 exculpare，通常经其过去分词形式 exculpatus 解释，由 ex-（除去）和 culpa（过错、罪责）构成。其核心意义是“除去罪责”，既可指证明法律上的清白，也可指解除一般的过错责任。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Medieval Latin exculpare, commonly traced through its past participle exculpatus, combining ex- meaning 'away' with culpa meaning 'fault or blame.' Its central idea of removing blame applies both to legal innocence and to freedom from responsibility for wrongdoing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：ex-（除去）+ culp（过错、罪责）+ -ate（动词后缀）。主要词族：exculpates（第三人称单数）、exculpated（过去式及过去分词）、exculpating（现在分词）、exculpation（免责；证明无罪）、exculpatory（证明无罪的；开脱罪责的）；同根相关词包括 culpable（应受责备的）、culpability（罪责）和 inculpate（归罪于；牵连入罪）。
morphology_enriched.en: Morphological analysis: ex- 'away' + culp 'fault or blame' + the verb-forming suffix -ate. The main family includes exculpates, exculpated, exculpating, exculpation, and exculpatory; related words sharing the Latin root include culpable, culpability, and inculpate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: exonerate（使免于罪责）强调正式解除指控或责任；absolve（赦免；免除责任）还可涉及道德或宗教上的宽恕；vindicate（证明正确或清白）范围更广，也可指证明某人的判断或行为有理。exculpate 较正式，尤其强调证明某人不应承担罪责。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Exonerate emphasizes formally clearing someone of an accusation or responsibility; absolve can also involve moral or religious forgiveness; vindicate is broader and can establish that a person's judgment or actions were justified. Exculpate is formal and particularly emphasizes establishing freedom from blame.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ex- 向外 + culp 罪责：把罪责从某人身上移走。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ex- takes culp, or blame, away: remove the blame from someone.

etymology_story.zh: 由拉丁语来源的 extra-（在……之外）与 mural（墙的）构成，后者源于拉丁语 murus（墙）。字面上的“墙外”逐渐引申为大学等机构边界之外，并用于校外教学、研究及资助等语境。
etymology_story.en: The word combines Latin-derived extra- 'outside' with mural 'relating to walls,' ultimately from Latin murus 'wall.' The literal idea of being outside the walls developed into being beyond an institution's boundaries, including in education, research, and funding.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：extra-（在……之外）+ mural（与墙有关的）；mural 内部可联系 mur-（墙）+ -al（形容词后缀）。主要派生词：extramurally（在机构外；以校外方式）；相关词包括 mural（壁画；墙的）、intramural（机构内部的；校内的）和 intramurally（在机构内部）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: extra- 'outside' + mural 'relating to walls'; mural can further be connected with mur- 'wall' and the adjective suffix -al. The principal derivative is extramurally; related words include mural, intramural, and intramurally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: external（外部的）用途最广，不限于机构边界；off-campus（校外的）主要强调地点不在校园内；extension（大学推广教育的，作名词定语）常指面向社会的大学课程。extramural 更正式，强调超出机构的常规范围；它不等于表示课外活动的 extracurricular。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: External is the broadest term and is not limited to institutional boundaries; off-campus chiefly identifies a location outside a campus; extension, used attributively, often describes university teaching offered to the wider community. Extramural is more formal and emphasizes activity beyond an institution's regular scope; it is distinct from extracurricular.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: extra- 在外 + mur 墙：走出机构的围墙。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Extra- means outside and mur means wall: go beyond the institution's walls.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代技术词，由 hydro-（水，源于希腊语 hydōr）与 foil（能产生升力的翼面）组成。它既用于指水下的升力装置，也用于指装有这种装置的船，后来还形成了水上运动中的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: This modern technical formation combines hydro- 'water,' from Greek hydōr, with foil in the sense of a lifting surface. It names both the underwater lifting device and a vessel fitted with it, and later developed a verb use in water sports.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hydro-（水）+ foil（翼面）。主要词族：hydrofoils（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、hydrofoiled（过去式及过去分词）、hydrofoiling（现在分词；水翼滑行运动）、hydrofoiler（水翼运动参与者或使用水翼的艇）；常见复合表达包括 hydrofoil boat（水翼艇）和 hydrofoil board（水翼板）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hydro- 'water' + foil 'lifting surface.' The main family includes hydrofoils, hydrofoiled, hydrofoiling, and hydrofoiler; common compounds include hydrofoil boat and hydrofoil board.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: foiling（水翼滑行）在水上运动语境中常与动词 hydrofoil 对应；ferry（渡船）强调载客或载车往返的用途，只有部分渡船是水翼艇；speedboat（快艇）强调速度，通常并不依靠水翼。后两者是相关船型称谓，并非 hydrofoil 的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Foiling commonly corresponds to the verb hydrofoil in water-sport contexts; ferry describes a vessel's passenger or vehicle transport function, and only some ferries are hydrofoils; speedboat emphasizes speed and usually does not imply hydrofoil support. The latter two are related vessel terms rather than exact synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hydro 水 + foil 翼面：水下的翼把船或板托起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hydro is water and foil is a wing: an underwater wing lifts the boat or board.

senses.meaning_zh: 焦耳；能量、功和热量的国际单位制单位，符号为 J
senses.meaning_en: the SI unit of energy, work, and heat, symbol J
senses.english_definition: A joule is a unit of energy equal to the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one metre in the direction of the force.
senses.collocation_en: energy measured in joules; one joule per second
senses.collocation_zh: 以焦耳计量的能量；每秒一焦耳
senses.sentence_en: A device operating at one watt transfers one joule of energy every second.
senses.sentence_zh: 以一瓦功率运行的装置每秒传递一焦耳能量。

etymology_story.zh: 该单位以英国物理学家詹姆斯·普雷斯科特·焦耳的姓氏命名，以纪念他在热与机械功关系方面的研究。人名转化为单位名称后，英文全称写作小写 joule，而单位符号写作大写 J。
etymology_story.en: The unit is named after the British physicist James Prescott Joule in recognition of his work on the relationship between heat and mechanical work. As a unit name it is written joule with a lowercase initial, while its symbol is the capital letter J.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是由姓氏转来的单纯词，不应拆成词根和后缀。主要相关形式：joules（复数）、millijoule（毫焦耳，mJ）、kilojoule（千焦耳，kJ）、megajoule（兆焦耳，MJ）、gigajoule（吉焦耳，GJ）、joulemeter（焦耳计）；Joule heating（焦耳热）和 Joule effect（焦耳效应）保留人名的大写形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, joule is a simple word derived from a surname and has no productive internal root-and-suffix division. Principal related forms include joules, millijoule (mJ), kilojoule (kJ), megajoule (MJ), gigajoule (GJ), and joulemeter; Joule heating and Joule effect retain the capitalized surname.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: watt-second（瓦秒）与焦耳在能量计量上完全等值；newton-metre（牛顿米）在表示功时也与焦耳等值，但表示力矩时通常保留牛顿米这一名称；calorie（卡路里）是另一种能量单位，热化学卡为 4.184 焦耳。这些是等值表达或相关单位，不能把它们的数值直接视为相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Watt-second is exactly equivalent to joule as an energy unit; newton-metre is also equivalent when expressing work, but the name newton-metre is normally retained for torque; calorie is a different energy unit, with one thermochemical calorie equal to 4.184 joules. These are equivalent expressions or related units, rather than interchangeable numerical values.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 焦耳研究热与功：用他的名字记能量单位；1 J = 1 N·m = 1 W·s。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Joule studied heat and work, so his name measures energy: 1 J = 1 N·m = 1 W·s.

etymology_story.zh: 由 mega-（极大，源于希腊语 megas）与 store（商店）在现代英语中组合而成，用来突出零售店的庞大规模。store 的早期意义与储备和供应有关，后来发展出存放及出售商品的场所这一含义。
etymology_story.en: This modern English formation combines mega- 'very large,' ultimately from Greek megas, with store to emphasize the scale of a retail outlet. Store earlier referred to supplies or provisions and later developed the sense of a place where goods are kept and sold.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：mega-（巨大；此处不表示精确的“一百万”）+ store（商店）。主要词族：megastores（复数）；相关构词包括 superstore（大型综合商店）和 megamall（超大型购物中心），相关基础词包括 store（商店；储存）、stores（商店的复数或动词第三人称单数）、stored（已储存的）、storing（储存）和 storage（储存；储藏空间）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: mega- 'very large,' without the precise numerical meaning 'one million' here, + store 'shop.' The principal inflection is megastores; related formations include superstore and megamall, while the base family includes store, stores, stored, storing, and storage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: superstore（大型商店）与 megastore 最接近，但 megastore 往往更突出规模特别大；hypermarket（大卖场）通常同时销售食品和大量非食品商品；department store（百货商店）强调按商品类别分设部门，而不是单纯强调面积。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Superstore is the closest synonym, although megastore often puts stronger emphasis on exceptional size; hypermarket usually combines groceries with a large range of non-food goods; department store emphasizes organization into separate merchandise departments rather than size alone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mega 巨大 + store 商店：把普通商店放大很多倍。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mega means huge: picture an ordinary store enlarged many times.

usage_note: 通常写 Platonist；本课指哲学立场，不是 platonic friendship 中的“纯精神友谊”。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古拉丁语 Platonista 传入英语，以柏拉图名字的词干 Platon- 加表示信奉者的后缀构成。它最初指柏拉图哲学的追随者，后来也用于主张数等抽象对象独立存在的人。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through Medieval Latin Platonista, formed from Platon-, the stem of Plato's name, with a suffix denoting a follower. It originally identified followers of Plato and later also described believers in the independent existence of abstract objects such as numbers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 Platon-（柏拉图）+ -ist（信奉者；具有某种思想倾向的），兼作名词和形容词。主要词族：Plato（柏拉图）、Platonism（柏拉图主义）、Platonic（柏拉图哲学的；指关系时也表示纯精神的）、Platonically（以柏拉图哲学的方式；以纯精神关系的方式）、Platonistic（柏拉图主义的）、Neoplatonism（新柏拉图主义）、Neoplatonist（新柏拉图主义者；新柏拉图主义的）；名词复数为 Platonists。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern analysis is Platon- (Plato) + -ist (a follower or someone associated with a doctrine), with both noun and adjective uses. The principal family includes Plato, Platonism (the doctrine), Platonic (relating to Plato; also describing a nonsexual relationship), Platonically (in a Platonic or nonsexual manner), Platonistic (relating to Platonism), Neoplatonism (a later philosophical tradition), and Neoplatonist (its follower or an adjective describing it); the noun plural is Platonists.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: follower of Plato（柏拉图的追随者）是最直接的释义；idealist（唯心主义者）范围更广，并非都接受柏拉图的理论；realist about abstract objects（抽象对象实在论者）接近现代哲学中的相关含义，但不必认同柏拉图的全部哲学。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Follower of Plato is the closest plain-language equivalent; idealist is broader and does not necessarily imply acceptance of Plato's theories; realist about abstract objects captures the relevant modern philosophical position without implying agreement with Plato's entire philosophy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Platon- 指柏拉图，-ist 指信奉者：把柏拉图的思想当作立场的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Platon- names Plato; -ist marks a follower: someone who takes a Platonic position.

morphology.text: poly-（多）+ math（学习，希腊语来源）→ polymath（在多个领域有学问的人）；这里的 math 不只指数学。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于希腊语 polymathēs，意为“学识广博的”，由表示“多”的 poly- 和与“学习”有关的成分构成。英语将其用作名词，指在多个知识领域都有深厚学养的人。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Greek polymathēs, meaning 'much learned', combining poly- ('much' or 'many') with an element connected with learning. English uses it as a noun for a person with substantial learning across several fields.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按希腊语来源成分理解为 poly-（多）+ -math（学习、学识）；这里的 -math 不是现代英语 mathematics 的缩写。主要词族：polymathy（博学）、polymathic（博学的；涉及多个知识领域的）、polymathical（博学的，较少用）；复数为 polymaths。
morphology_enriched.en: Its Greek-derived components are poly- (many) + -math (learning); -math here is not the modern abbreviation of mathematics. The principal family includes polymathy (wide learning), polymathic (widely learned or spanning several fields), and the less common polymathical (widely learned); the plural is polymaths.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Renaissance person（多才多艺的博学者）强调跨领域的知识与才能；polyhistor（博学者）含义接近，但更书面且少见；generalist（通才）强调涉猎范围广，不一定具有 polymath 所暗示的深厚学识。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Renaissance person emphasizes knowledge and accomplishments across fields; polyhistor is a close but rarer, more literary equivalent; generalist emphasizes breadth without necessarily implying the depth of learning associated with polymath.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: poly-＝多，-math＝学：多门学问都懂的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Poly- means many and -math points to learning: a person learned in many subjects.

etymology.text: 植物学名词借自拉丁语 scapus（杆、茎）；可以联想从植株基部直立向上的一根无叶花梗。

usage_note: 本课只教植物的花葶，不是 landscape 的缩略或古体 escape。花葶本身无叶。

senses.sentence_zh: 这只蚂蚁较长的柄节构成了其膝状触角的第一段。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自拉丁语 scapus，意为“杆、茎”，更早与希腊语 skapos 相联系。杆状的基本意象体现在植物的花葶和昆虫触角的柄节等专业用法中。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from Latin scapus, meaning a shaft or stalk, ultimately connected with Greek skapos. Its shaft-like image appears in technical uses for a plant's flower stalk and the basal segment of an insect's antenna.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 scape 是不可再作常规前后缀切分的基础名词。主要相关形式：scapes（复数）、scapeless（无花葶的）、scapose（具花葶的）、scapal（触角柄节的）；scape 与 landscape、soundscape 中表示“景观、整体环境”的 -scape 不应混为同一构词成分。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, scape is a base noun without a productive internal prefix-and-suffix division. Principal related forms include scapes (plural), scapeless (without a scape), scapose (having a scape), and scapal (relating to an antennal scape); it should be distinguished from -scape meaning a scene or environment in landscape and soundscape.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flower stalk（花梗）是较宽泛的日常说法，不一定无叶或从基部长出；peduncle（花序梗、总花梗）是较宽的植物学术语，scape 是其中一种；basal antennal segment（触角基节）可解释昆虫学义，与植物学义不可互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flower stalk is a broader everyday term and need not imply a leafless stalk arising from the base; peduncle is a broader botanical term of which a scape is one type; basal antennal segment explains the entomological sense and is not interchangeable with the botanical terms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“一根基部支杆”：植物用它托花，昆虫用它连接触角。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a basal supporting shaft: it carries flowers in a plant and anchors an antenna in an insect.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 soffite 来自意大利语 soffitto，意为“天花板”，其历史来源与拉丁语 suffigere（从下面固定）有关。英语将它用于建筑构件朝下的底面，尤其是屋檐和拱的底面。
etymology_story.en: The word came through French soffite from Italian soffitto, meaning a ceiling, historically related to Latin suffigere, 'to fasten underneath'. In English it denotes the downward-facing surface of an architectural feature, especially an eave or arch.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 soffit 作为整体词根记忆，不宜拆成看似熟悉的英语小词。主要相关形式：soffits（复数）、soffited（设有底面或底面覆板的）、soffiting（底面覆板材料；安装底面覆板的作业）；常见复合词有 soffit board（檐底板）和 soffit vent（檐底通风口）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, soffit is treated as a whole base rather than divided into familiar-looking English words. Principal related forms include soffits (plural), soffited (provided with a soffit or soffit lining), and soffiting (soffit lining material or the work of installing it); common compounds include soffit board and soffit vent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: underside（底面）是最宽泛的对应词，不限建筑；intrados（拱腹面）专指拱或拱顶的内凹面；ceiling（天花板）通常指室内上方的表面，不专指突出构件的底面。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Underside is the broadest equivalent and is not restricted to architecture; intrados specifically denotes the inner curved surface of an arch or vault; ceiling usually means the overhead interior surface of a room rather than specifically the underside of a projecting feature.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从下方固定、朝下可见：站在屋檐下抬头看的那一面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fastened underneath and visible from below: the surface you see when looking up beneath an eave.

senses.english_definition: If someone has a strop or is in a strop, they behave angrily or sulk because they are annoyed.
senses.collocation_en: throw a strop; be in a strop
senses.collocation_zh: 大发脾气；正在闹情绪
senses.sentence_en: He threw a strop when he was told he could not use the car.
senses.sentence_zh: 听说自己不能用车，他便大发脾气。

senses.meaning_zh: 发脾气；气冲冲地行动，尤用于英国口语
senses.meaning_en: to behave or move in a bad-tempered way, especially in informal British English
senses.english_definition: If someone strops, they show that they are annoyed by behaving or moving in a bad-tempered way.
senses.collocation_en: strop off; strop around
senses.collocation_zh: 气冲冲地离开；带着怒气四处走动或闹情绪
senses.sentence_en: She stropped off upstairs when the discussion ended.
senses.sentence_zh: 讨论结束时，她气冲冲地上楼去了。

etymology_story.zh: 表示带子的 strop 可追溯到古英语 stropp，源自拉丁语 stroppus，并最终与希腊语表示“绞成的带子或绳索”的词有关；strap 与它有历史联系。磨刀带义和吊索义保留了“带、环”的意象，而“发脾气”是较晚出现、与 stroppy（脾气暴躁的）相关的英国口语用法。
etymology_story.en: Strop in the sense of a band goes back to Old English stropp, from Latin stroppus, ultimately connected with a Greek word for a twisted band or cord; strap is historically related. The blade-finishing and lifting senses retain this band-like image, while the bad-temper sense is a later British colloquial use associated with stroppy.

morphology_enriched.zh: strop 是基础词，磨刀义动词由名词直接转化而来。屈折形式：strops、stropped、stropping；加 -ed、-ing 时双写 p。相关词族包括 stroppy（易怒的；爱顶撞的）、stroppily（暴躁地；顶撞地）、stroppiness（暴躁；爱顶撞的性情）；strap（带子）是历史相关词，不是现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Strop is a base word, with the blade-finishing verb formed by conversion from the noun. Inflected forms are strops, stropped, and stropping, with p doubled before -ed and -ing. Related family members include stroppy (irritable or argumentative), stroppily (in an irritable or argumentative way), and stroppiness (that quality); strap is historically related rather than a modern derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hone（磨利、珩磨）通常涉及磨石或其他磨削工具，而 strop 强调用带子进行刃口修整；sling（吊索）与吊装义接近，但结构和适用范围更广；tantrum（大发脾气）接近情绪义，通常更强调明显的失控表现。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hone usually involves a stone or another abrasive tool, whereas strop specifies finishing an edge on a strip; sling is close to the lifting sense but covers a broader range of supporting arrangements; tantrum is close to the emotional sense but usually suggests a more conspicuous loss of control.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 实物义抓住“一条带”：磨刀或吊物；口语义连到 stroppy：一阵坏脾气。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the physical senses, picture a band that finishes a blade or lifts a load; for the colloquial sense, connect it with stroppy and bad temper.

usage_note: 可数动物名，指有短而灵活鼻部的貘；不是食蚁兽，也不是小象。

senses.meaning_zh: 貘：鼻吻短而能伸动的大型食草哺乳动物
senses.meaning_en: A large plant-eating mammal with a short, flexible snout.
senses.english_definition: A tapir is a large mammal with a short, flexible snout that lives in tropical forests and eats plants.
senses.collocation_en: a Malayan tapir; a Brazilian tapir
senses.collocation_zh: 一只马来貘；一只巴西貘
senses.sentence_en: The tapir used its flexible snout to pull leaves from a low branch.
senses.sentence_zh: 那只貘用能灵活伸动的鼻吻从低矮的树枝上扯下树叶。

etymology_story.zh: tapir 最终源于南美洲图皮语中的动物名称 tapi'ira，经法语等欧洲语言传入英语。它原本用于指称南美洲的貘，后来也用于包括马来貘在内的其他貘类。
etymology_story.en: Tapir ultimately comes from the Tupi animal name tapi'ira and reached English through European languages, including French. Originally associated with South American tapirs, the name also came to cover other tapirs, including the Malayan tapir.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tapir 是不可再作常用词根、词缀拆分的借词。屈折形式：tapirs（复数）；相关构词：tapir-like（像貘的），tapirid（貘科动物；貘科的，动物学用语）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tapir is a borrowed base without a productive root-and-affix breakdown. Its plural is tapirs; related formations include tapir-like and the zoological term tapirid, meaning a member of the tapir family or relating to that family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的精确同义词。ungulate（有蹄类动物）和 mammal（哺乳动物）都是范围更大的上位词，不能在需要准确指明貘时替换 tapir。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Ungulate and mammal are broader category terms and cannot replace tapir when the particular animal must be identified.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 tapir 与“短鼻吻、食树叶的貘”这一形象整体绑定；它是借来的动物名称，无须硬拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link tapir directly to a leaf-eating animal with a short, flexible snout; learn the borrowed animal name as a whole.

senses.meaning_zh: 尺骨：前臂两骨中位于小指一侧的骨
senses.meaning_en: The forearm bone on the little-finger side.
senses.english_definition: Your ulna is the long bone on the little-finger side of your forearm when your palm faces forward.

etymology_story.zh: ulna 借自拉丁语 ulna，原有“肘、前臂”等含义，也曾表示以前臂长度为基础的长度单位。解剖学用法将这个名称专门用于前臂小指侧的那根骨头。
etymology_story.en: Ulna was borrowed from Latin ulna, meaning the elbow or forearm and also a measure based on forearm length. Anatomical usage specialized the name to the bone on the little-finger side of the forearm.

morphology_enriched.zh: ulna 是借入的基本词；构词时常用词干 uln- 或结合形式 ulno-。复数为 ulnae 或 ulnas；uln- + -ar → ulnar（尺骨的）；相关复合词包括 radioulnar（桡尺骨的）和 ulnocarpal（尺腕的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Ulna is a borrowed base; related formations commonly use the stem uln- or combining form ulno-. Its plurals are ulnae and ulnas; uln- + -ar forms ulnar. Related compounds include radioulnar and ulnocarpal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ulnar bone（尺骨）是解释性的同义表达；forearm bone（前臂骨）范围较广，也可能指桡骨。radius（桡骨）是与尺骨配对的另一根骨头，属于对照词，不能当作同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ulnar bone is an explanatory equivalent, while forearm bone is broader and may also refer to the radius. Radius names the other forearm bone and is a contrasting term, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ulna 对应小指侧，radius 对应拇指侧；记住这对位置，便能定位尺骨。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair ulna with the little-finger side and radius with the thumb side to locate the two forearm bones.

etymology.text: 现代医学英语仿法语 vaso-constriction 构成；vaso- 与 constriction 均有拉丁语背景，合起来就是血管变窄。

usage_note: 指血管管腔变窄这一过程；与 vasodilation（血管舒张）相反。本课学习术语含义。
