senses.meaning_zh: 血管收缩：血管壁肌肉收缩引起的管腔变窄
senses.meaning_en: Narrowing of blood vessels caused by contraction of their muscular walls.
senses.english_definition: Vasoconstriction is the narrowing of blood vessels when the muscles in their walls tighten.
senses.collocation_en: peripheral vasoconstriction; cause vasoconstriction
senses.collocation_zh: 外周血管收缩；引起血管收缩
senses.sentence_en: Exposure to cold causes vasoconstriction in the skin, helping to reduce heat loss.
senses.sentence_zh: 暴露于寒冷环境会引起皮肤血管收缩，有助于减少热量散失。

etymology_story.zh: vasoconstriction 是现代医学术语，由 vaso-（血管，最终源于拉丁语 vas，意为“容器、管道”）与 constriction（收紧、缩窄）组合而成。名称把“容器”的古义具体化为血管，并直接描述血管管腔变窄的过程。
etymology_story.en: Vasoconstriction is a modern medical formation combining vaso-, ultimately from Latin vas meaning a vessel or container, with constriction, meaning tightening or narrowing. The older idea of a vessel is applied specifically to blood vessels and their narrowing.

morphology_enriched.zh: vaso-（血管）+ constriction（收缩）；constriction 与 constrict（使收缩）+ -ion（过程名词后缀）相联系。主要词族：vasoconstrict（使血管收缩）、vasoconstriction（血管收缩）、vasoconstrictor（血管收缩剂；使血管收缩的）、vasoconstrictive（使血管收缩的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Vaso- means blood vessel, and constriction denotes narrowing; constriction is related to constrict plus the process-noun suffix -ion. The principal word family includes vasoconstrict, vasoconstriction, vasoconstrictor, and vasoconstrictive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vascular constriction（血管收缩）是近义表达；blood vessel narrowing（血管变窄）更通俗，但范围更广。vasospasm（血管痉挛）强调突然或异常的血管收缩，不能用于替换所有正常生理性收缩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vascular constriction is a close equivalent; blood vessel narrowing is plainer but broader. Vasospasm emphasizes sudden or abnormal contraction and does not cover every instance of normal physiological vasoconstriction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: vaso- 是“血管”，constrict 是“收紧”：血管一收紧，管腔就变窄。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Vaso- supplies the blood vessel, and constrict supplies the tightening: tighten the vessel wall and the opening narrows.

aliases: 结合树木与作物或牧业的土地经营

morphology.text: agro-（农业）+ forestry（林业）→ agroforestry（农林复合经营）。

etymology.text: 现代英语把希腊语来源的 agro-（田地、农业）与 forestry 组合；名称体现树木与作物或牧场共同经营。

usage_note: 不是把农业与林业各做各的简单并列，强调同一土地系统中结合树木与作物或牧业。

senses.meaning_zh: 农林复合经营：在同一土地经营系统中结合树木与农作物或畜牧业
senses.meaning_en: Land management that deliberately combines trees with crops or livestock.
senses.english_definition: Agroforestry is a way of managing land in which trees are deliberately grown together with crops or used as part of a livestock farming system.
senses.collocation_en: agroforestry systems; agroforestry practices
senses.collocation_zh: 农林复合经营系统；农林复合经营措施
senses.sentence_en: The farmers adopted agroforestry by planting fruit trees among their crops.
senses.sentence_zh: 农民们在作物之间栽种果树，采用了农林复合经营方式。

etymology_story.zh: agroforestry 是现代英语将 agro-（农业，最终源于希腊语 agros，意为“田地”）与 forestry（林业）组合形成的词。它为树木与作物或牲畜相结合的土地经营方式提供了统一名称，而这类实践本身远早于该术语。
etymology_story.en: Agroforestry is a modern English formation combining agro-, ultimately from Greek agros meaning a field, with forestry. It provides a collective name for land-use practices combining trees with crops or livestock, although those practices long predate the term.

morphology_enriched.zh: agro-（农业）+ forestry（林业）→ agroforestry。相关词族：agroforester（农林复合经营从业者或专家），复数 agroforesters；基础词族包括 forest（森林；造林）、forester（林业工作者）和 forestry（林业）。
morphology_enriched.en: Agro- meaning agricultural + forestry forms agroforestry. Related vocabulary includes agroforester, a practitioner or specialist, and its plural agroforesters; the underlying family includes forest, forester, and forestry.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: farm forestry（农场林业）与之有重叠，但未必强调树木与农牧活动的整合；agrosilviculture（农林间作）特指树木与农作物结合；silvopasture（林牧复合经营）特指树木、牧草与放牧牲畜结合，后两者均是 agroforestry 的具体形式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Farm forestry overlaps with agroforestry but need not emphasize integration with other farming activities. Agrosilviculture specifically combines trees and crops, while silvopasture combines trees, forage, and grazing livestock; both are forms of agroforestry.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: agro- 想“农业”，forestry 想“林业”：让农田或牧场与树木共同经营。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read agro- as farming and forestry as trees: manage trees together with crops or livestock.

senses.meaning_zh: 笨蛋；傻瓜（非正式、贬义，尤用于英式英语）

etymology_story.zh: dipstick 由英语 dip（浸入）和 stick（杆、条）复合而成，原义直接描述把标尺浸入液体测量液位的操作。后来该词也用于浸液检测试条，并发展出称人为“笨蛋”的俚语用法；医疗动词用法则由检测工具名转化而来。
etymology_story.en: Dipstick combines dip and stick, originally describing a rod dipped into liquid to measure its level. It later also named a liquid-testing strip and acquired a slang sense meaning a foolish person; the clinical verb developed from the testing-tool noun.

morphology_enriched.zh: dip（浸入）+ stick（杆、条）→ dipstick，是复合词。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 dipsticks；动词过去式、过去分词为 dipsticked，现在分词或动名词为 dipsticking；常见组合为 dipstick test（试条检测）和 dipstick testing（试条检测法）。
morphology_enriched.en: Dip + stick forms the compound dipstick. Dipsticks is both the noun plural and the third-person singular verb form; the past tense and past participle are dipsticked, and the present participle or gerund is dipsticking. Common combinations include dipstick test and dipstick testing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gauge（测量仪表）比量液位的 dipstick 范围更广；test strip（检测试条）对应化学检测义，通常不指量油尺；fool（傻瓜）对应骂人义，比 dipstick 更普遍，较少带英式口语色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gauge is broader than dipstick as a liquid-level measuring device. Test strip matches the chemical-testing sense but normally does not mean an oil-level rod. Fool matches the insulting sense and is more general and less distinctly British.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dip 是“浸”，stick 是“杆或条”：浸进去，取出来，看液位或颜色；“笨蛋”义另外记作口语引申。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dip the stick, pull it out, and read the level or colour; remember the informal insult as a separate extended sense.

etymology.text: 经中古英语、法语追溯到古意大利语 ducato，相关 duca 指公爵或总督；名称与刻有统治者像的钱币相连。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语等途径传入英语，最终源自意大利语 ducato，原义为“公国”，与 duca（公爵）同源。钱币名称与威尼斯金币上提及公国的拉丁文铭文有关，后来又产生“钱”和“入场券”等俚语义。
etymology_story.en: The word reached English through French and ultimately comes from Italian ducato, meaning 'duchy', related to duca, 'duke'. Its use as a coin name is associated with a Latin inscription referring to the duchy on Venetian gold coins; slang senses later developed for money and tickets.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作常规拆分的借词 ducat；复数为 ducats。没有常用的标准派生词族；gold ducat（金达克特）和 Venetian ducat（威尼斯达克特）是名词短语，不是派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ducat is an unanalyzed loanword; its plural is ducats. It has no established common family of derived words; gold ducat and Venetian ducat are noun phrases rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: coin（硬币）是上位词，不限定年代或币种；gold piece（金币）只说明材质，不说明具体货币制度；ticket（入场券）仅对应 ducat 的美国俚语义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Coin is a broader term that does not specify a historical currency; gold piece identifies the material without identifying the currency; ticket matches only the American slang sense of ducat.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“公国的钱币”记起：ducat 先指旧币，再可借指钱或门票。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'a duchy's coin': ducat names an old coin and can extend to money or a ticket.

senses.meaning_zh: 龙胆；龙胆属植物，常开蓝色喇叭状花
senses.meaning_en: a plant of the genus Gentiana, often bearing blue trumpet-shaped flowers

senses.collocation_zh: 龙胆根；龙胆提取物
senses.sentence_en: The drink gets its bitter flavour from gentian.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语和法语源自拉丁语 gentiana。古代传统将这一植物名称与伊利里亚国王 Gentius 联系起来，称他发现了它的药用价值，但这种说法属于历史传说，不能视为已证实的发现史。
etymology_story.en: The word comes through Middle English and French from Latin gentiana. Ancient tradition connected the plant's name with Gentius, an Illyrian king credited with discovering its medicinal properties, though that account is traditional rather than an established discovery history.

morphology_enriched.zh: gentian 是现代英语中不作常规词根词缀拆分的植物借名；可数植物义的复数为 gentians，药材义通常不可数。相关词包括 Gentiana（龙胆属的学名）、Gentianaceae（龙胆科）和 gentianaceous（龙胆科的）；gentian root（龙胆根）与 gentian violet（龙胆紫，一种合成染料）是复合表达，后者并非龙胆植物提取物。
morphology_enriched.en: Gentian is a borrowed plant name without a productive modern root-and-affix breakdown; the countable plant sense has the plural gentians, while the herbal-material sense is usually uncountable. Related botanical forms include Gentiana, the genus name, Gentianaceae, the family name, and gentianaceous, meaning 'belonging to the gentian family'; gentian root and gentian violet are compound expressions, and the latter names a synthetic dye rather than a plant extract.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gentian plant（龙胆植物）近乎等义，但不指药材；gentian root（龙胆根）只指植物根部及相关药材；bitter herb（苦味草药）范围更广，并非龙胆的专名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gentian plant is nearly equivalent in the botanical sense but excludes the prepared herbal material; gentian root specifies the root and its preparations; bitter herb is a broader description rather than an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 蓝花认植物，苦根认用途：gentian 把龙胆花与龙胆根连在一起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Blue flowers identify the plant; bitter roots identify its use: gentian connects both.

senses.meaning_en: orbiting above the equator so as to remain over the same point on Earth
senses.english_definition: A geostationary satellite moves around Earth above the equator at the same angular speed as Earth rotates, so it stays above the same place.
senses.collocation_en: a geostationary satellite; geostationary orbit
senses.collocation_zh: 地球静止卫星；地球静止轨道
senses.sentence_en: The antenna points at a geostationary satellite above the equator.
senses.sentence_zh: 这副天线对准赤道上空的一颗地球静止卫星。

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代航天英语中由 geo-（地球）与 stationary（静止的）构成的术语；geo- 源自希腊语表示“大地”的词，stationary 最终与拉丁语表示“站立”的词有关。其“静止”指相对地面的表观位置不变，而卫星本身仍在绕地球运动。
etymology_story.en: This modern spaceflight term combines geo-, 'Earth', from Greek, with stationary, ultimately related to Latin words for standing. Its 'stationary' element describes an unchanged position relative to the ground while the satellite continues to orbit Earth.

morphology_enriched.zh: geo-（地球）+ stationary（静止的）→ geostationary。相关词有 stationary（静止的）、stationarity（平稳性；静止性）和专业名词 geostationarity（地球静止状态）；geosynchronous（地球同步的）是相关术语，意义范围更广。
morphology_enriched.en: Geo- ('Earth') + stationary ('remaining in one position') forms geostationary. Related forms include stationary, stationarity, and the specialist noun geostationarity; geosynchronous is a related term with a broader meaning.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: geosynchronous（地球同步的）只要求轨道周期与地球自转周期相同，不保证相对地面位置固定；stationary（静止的）是一般用语，不包含赤道轨道等条件。geostationary 特指顺行、赤道面内的圆形地球同步轨道所具有的性质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Geosynchronous requires an orbital period matching Earth's rotation but does not guarantee a fixed position in the sky; stationary is a general word without orbital conditions. Geostationary specifically describes the fixed-ground-position property of a prograde, circular, equatorial geosynchronous orbit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo- 是地球，stationary 是位置不变：跟着地球同速转，地面看来停一点。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Geo- means Earth and stationary means staying in place: match Earth's rotation and appear fixed above one point.

senses.meaning_zh: （语音学）声门音；在声门处发出的辅音

senses.english_definition: A glottal is a consonant whose place of articulation is the glottis.

senses.collocation_zh: 声门音与咽音；声门音 /h/

etymology_story.zh: glottal 由 glottis（声门）的词干加形容词后缀 -al 构成；glottis 经拉丁语源自希腊语 glōttis，与表示“舌头”的 glōtta 有关。该词先描述声门部位及其活动，也用于描述在那里形成的语音，并可名词化表示声门音。
etymology_story.en: Glottal was formed from the stem of glottis with the adjective suffix -al; glottis came through Latin from Greek glōttis, related to glōtta, 'tongue'. The word describes the glottis and sounds produced there, and it can also function as a noun for such a consonant.

morphology_enriched.zh: glottis（声门）去掉词尾 -is，取词干 glott-，加 -al → glottal；glottal + -ly → glottally（在声门处；以声门方式）。常见专业词族包括 glottalize/glottalise（使声门化）、glottalized/glottalised（声门化的）及 glottalization/glottalisation（声门化）；相关形容词还有 glottic（声门的）和 glottalic（声门气流机制的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Remove the ending -is from glottis to obtain glott-, then add -al to form glottal; adding -ly gives glottally. The established technical family includes glottalize/glottalise, glottalized/glottalised, and glottalization/glottalisation; related adjectives include glottic and glottalic, the latter especially referring to a glottalic airstream mechanism.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: glottic（声门的）在解剖学语境中意义接近；laryngeal（喉的）涵盖整个喉部，范围更广；guttural（喉部发出的；喉音的）常是较宽泛的听觉描述，不能精确替代语音学中的 glottal。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Glottic is close in anatomical contexts; laryngeal concerns the whole larynx and is broader; guttural is often a loose description of a throaty sound and cannot precisely replace glottal in phonetics.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: glottis 是声门，-al 表“有关的”：气流在声门处受控制，就是 glottal 的核心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Glottis names the opening and -al means 'relating to': think of airflow controlled at the glottis.

senses.meaning_zh: （非正式）跑腿办杂事的雇员；打杂助手
senses.meaning_en: an employee or assistant who runs errands and does routine minor jobs
senses.english_definition: A gofer is someone whose job is to fetch things and do small tasks for other people.
senses.collocation_en: work as a gofer; a production gofer
senses.collocation_zh: 做跑腿打杂的工作；制作团队的打杂助手
senses.sentence_en: She started as a gofer on a film set and later became a producer.
senses.sentence_zh: 她起初在电影片场跑腿打杂，后来成为了制片人。

etymology_story.zh: 该词产生于20世纪的美国英语，是 go for（去拿、去取）的谐音式拼写。它把别人反复吩咐“去拿这个、去取那个”的工作内容变成了这类助手的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word arose in twentieth-century American English as a respelling of go for, meaning to fetch something. Repeated instructions to 'go for' things became a name for the assistant carrying out those errands.

morphology_enriched.zh: go for（去拿）→ gofer，是短语按读音融合并重新拼写形成的名词，不宜机械分析为 go + 施事后缀 -er。复数为 gofers，另有拼写 go-fer；没有常用的标准派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Go for ('fetch') becomes gofer through phonetic fusion and respelling; it is not straightforwardly formed from go plus the agent suffix -er. The plural is gofers, the spelling go-fer also occurs, and there is no established common family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: errand runner（跑腿者）最直接强调取送和外出办事；assistant（助手）范围更广，也可能承担专业职责；lackey（听差；跟班）含明显贬义，强调卑躬屈膝，而 gofer 主要强调工作琐碎、职位较低。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Errand runner most directly emphasizes fetching, delivering, and outside errands; assistant is broader and may involve skilled responsibilities; lackey is distinctly disparaging and suggests servility, while gofer mainly emphasizes minor duties and low status.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 总被叫去“go for coffee”的人，就是 gofer。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The person repeatedly told to 'go for coffee' is the gofer.

meaning: 极其复杂难解的；棘手的

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

morphology.text: Gordius（人名，去掉 -us）+ -an（有关的）→ Gordian（与戈耳迪俄斯有关的，引申为极难解的）。

etymology.text: 来自古代弗里吉亚国王 Gordius 的名字；与传说中极难解开的戈耳迪结相连，后来用来比喻难题。

usage_note: 通常在 Gordian knot 中大写 Gordian，指盘根错节的难题；不是 ordinary knot 的通用替代词。

senses.meaning_zh: 极其复杂难解的；棘手的，尤用于 Gordian knot
senses.meaning_en: Extremely complicated or difficult to resolve, especially in the expression Gordian knot.
senses.english_definition: A Gordian knot is a problem that is extremely complicated and difficult to solve.
senses.collocation_en: a Gordian knot; cut the Gordian knot
senses.collocation_zh: 错综复杂的难题；快刀斩乱麻
senses.sentence_en: The negotiations had become a Gordian knot of conflicting demands.
senses.sentence_zh: 由于各方要求相互冲突，谈判已陷入错综复杂、难以化解的困局。

etymology_story.zh: 源自古代弗里吉亚国王 Gordius（戈耳迪俄斯）的名字；传说他的车轭上系着一个无人能解开的结。亚历山大挥剑斩结的故事，使 Gordian knot 成为复杂难题的比喻，而 cut the Gordian knot 则表示以果断办法解决难题。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the name of Gordius, a legendary king of Phrygia whose wagon yoke was secured with a seemingly impossible knot. The story of Alexander cutting it with his sword made Gordian knot a metaphor for a complex problem and cut the Gordian knot an expression for resolving one decisively.

morphology_enriched.zh: 人名构词：Gordius 的词干 Gordi- + -an（与……有关的）→ Gordian。现代英语通常把它作为整体的人名派生形容词使用，首字母大写；没有常用的进一步派生词，核心固定表达为 Gordian knot 和 cut the Gordian knot。
morphology_enriched.en: Name-based formation: Gordi-, the stem of Gordius, + -an, meaning 'relating to,' → Gordian. Modern English generally treats it as an established adjective derived from a proper name and retains the capital letter; it has no common further derivatives, and its central expressions are Gordian knot and cut the Gordian knot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intricate（错综复杂的）强调细节或关系交织；intractable（难以处理的）强调难以解决或控制；convoluted（盘根错节的）常暗示结构或解释过度复杂。Gordian 带有典故色彩，最常通过 Gordian knot 描绘难以理清的困局。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Intricate emphasizes interwoven details or relationships; intractable emphasizes resistance to solution or control; convoluted often suggests excessive complexity in structure or explanation. Gordian is literary and allusive, most often describing an apparently insoluble situation through Gordian knot.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Gordius 的结难解，亚历山大一剑斩开：Gordian knot＝复杂难题，cut the knot＝果断破局。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture Gordius's impossible knot and Alexander's sword: the Gordian knot is the tangled problem; cutting it is the decisive solution.

pronunciation.note: 采用常用英式读法；ˈ 标记后一个音节的主重音，ˌ 标记后一个音节的次重音。

morphology.text: kilo-（千）+ byte（字节）→ kilobyte（千字节）。

usage_note: 可指1000字节，传统计算机语境也可能指1024字节；读容量说明时看约定。字节 byte 与位 bit 不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 千字节：按十进制为1000字节；传统计算机用法中也指1024字节
senses.meaning_en: A unit of digital information equal to 1,000 bytes, also traditionally used for 1,024 bytes.
senses.english_definition: A kilobyte is a unit used to measure digital information and means 1,000 bytes, although some computing uses mean 1,024 bytes.

etymology_story.zh: 由 kilo-（千）与计算机术语 byte（字节）组合而成；kilo- 最终源自希腊语 khilioi，意为“一千”。由于1024是接近1000的二次幂，计算机领域曾广泛用 kilobyte 表示1024字节；后来引入 kibibyte，专门明确表示1024字节。
etymology_story.en: Kilobyte combines kilo-, ultimately from Greek khilioi meaning 'a thousand,' with the computing term byte. Because 1,024 is a power of two close to 1,000, computing usage also adopted kilobyte for 1,024 bytes; kibibyte was later introduced as an unambiguous name for that binary quantity.

morphology_enriched.zh: kilo-（千）+ byte（字节）→ kilobyte；复数为 kilobytes，十进制单位符号为 kB。相关单位词有 byte、megabyte（兆字节）、gigabyte（吉字节）和 kibibyte（二进制千字节，KiB，1024字节）；kilobit（千比特）使用相同前缀，但不是 kilobyte 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: kilo- ('thousand') + byte → kilobyte; the plural is kilobytes, and the decimal unit symbol is kB. Related unit terms include byte, megabyte, gigabyte, and kibibyte, abbreviated KiB and equal to 1,024 bytes; kilobit shares the prefix but is not a derivative of kilobyte.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kB 是十进制千字节的规范符号；KB 是常见写法，但在不同语境中可能表示1000或1024字节；kibibyte（KiB）严格表示1024字节。因此这些形式并非在所有语境中都能互换，kilobit 更不能与 kilobyte 混用，因为1字节等于8比特。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: kB is the standard symbol for the decimal kilobyte; KB is common but may mean either 1,000 or 1,024 bytes depending on context; kibibyte, or KiB, means exactly 1,024 bytes. These forms are therefore not universally interchangeable, and kilobit must not be confused with kilobyte because one byte contains eight bits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: kilo- 表示“千”：kilobyte 就是“千个字节”；看到 KiB，则准确想到1024字节。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Kilo- means 'thousand,' so a kilobyte is a thousand bytes; KiB specifically signals 1,024 bytes.

etymology_story.zh: 由希腊语来源的 kilo-（千）与 ton（吨）组合而成。随着核技术的发展，该词也用于表示爆炸能量，以一千公吨TNT所对应的约定能量作为一个单位。
etymology_story.en: Kiloton combines the Greek-derived prefix kilo-, meaning 'thousand,' with ton. With the development of nuclear technology, it also became a unit of explosive energy based on the conventional energy equivalent of one thousand metric tons of TNT.

morphology_enriched.zh: kilo-（千）+ ton（吨）→ kiloton；复数为 kilotons。kilotonne 明确以公吨 tonne 为基础；相关单位词有 ton、tonne 和 megaton（百万吨；百万吨TNT当量）。ten-kiloton 等形式可作前置复合修饰语，其中 kiloton 保持单数形式，并不因此成为独立的常用形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: kilo- ('thousand') + ton → kiloton; the plural is kilotons. Kilotonne explicitly uses the metric tonne as its base; related unit words include ton, tonne, and megaton. Forms such as ten-kiloton function as compound modifiers before nouns, with kiloton remaining singular; this does not establish a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kilotonne（千公吨）明确表示1000公吨；thousand tons（千吨）是质量义的普通表达，但同样需要明确吨制；kiloton of TNT equivalent（千吨TNT当量）表示能量而非实际炸药重量。megaton 是更大的同类单位，并非同义词，等于1000 kilotons。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kilotonne explicitly means 1,000 metric tons; thousand tons is a plain-language equivalent for mass but still requires the ton convention to be clear; kiloton of TNT equivalent specifies energy rather than an actual weight of explosive. Megaton is a larger related unit, not a synonym, and equals 1,000 kilotons.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Kilo- means 'thousand' and ton supplies the base: material is measured in thousands of tons, while explosions are measured in thousands of tons of TNT equivalent.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 lapidarius，意为“与石头有关的”，其中 lapid- 是 lapis（石头）的词干；英语早期用它指从事宝石加工的人。形容文字的用法则让人联想到石刻铭文的简洁庄重，以及精心雕琢的表达。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin lapidarius, meaning 'relating to stone,' built on lapid-, the stem of lapis, 'stone'; early English used it for a worker in gemstones. Its literary sense evokes the concise dignity of inscriptions carved in stone and the care of finely worked expression.

morphology_enriched.zh: 词源形态为 lapid-（石头）+ -ary（与……有关的；相关从业者）→ lapidary；现代英语中 lapid- 是黏着词根，不能单独使用。名词复数为 lapidaries；形容词仍为 lapidary。同根词还有较少见的 lapidate（用石头砸）和 lapidation（投石行为），它们是同源词，并非直接由现代英语 lapidary 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned structure is lapid- ('stone') + -ary ('relating to' or 'a person concerned with') → lapidary; lapid- is a bound root in modern English. The noun plural is lapidaries, while the adjective remains lapidary. Less common relatives include lapidate, 'to pelt with stones,' and lapidation, 'stoning'; these are related formations rather than direct derivatives of modern English lapidary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gem cutter（宝石切磨匠）是名词义的直白近义表达，jeweler（珠宝商；珠宝匠）的工作范围更广，未必亲自切磨宝石。形容文风时，terse（简短的）强调字少，有时略显生硬；lapidary 则突出精心雕琢、凝练而有分量。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gem cutter is a straightforward equivalent for the noun, while jeweler has a broader scope and does not necessarily imply cutting stones. For writing, terse emphasizes brevity and can suggest abruptness; lapidary emphasizes carefully polished wording with precision and weight.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lapid-＝石头：磨石成宝，也把语言磨成像碑铭一样精练的句子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lapid- means 'stone': a lapidary polishes stones, and lapidary prose sounds polished enough to carve into stone.

etymology_story.zh: 源自阿拉伯语 lūf，即这种植物的名称；英语还有 luffa 这一拼写，它也用于植物属名 Luffa。成熟果实内部的纤维网络干燥后可用于擦洗，因此植物名称也转指由它制成的浴擦。
etymology_story.en: Loofah comes from Arabic lūf, the name of the plant; English also has the spelling luffa, which is used in the botanical genus name Luffa. Because the mature fruit's dried fiber network can be used for scrubbing, the plant's name also came to denote the resulting washing sponge.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 loofah 是不可再作实用拆分的借词，不宜把 loo- 或 -fah 当作英语词根词缀。复数为 loofahs，变体拼写为 luffa、loofa；loofah sponge（丝瓜络浴擦）和 loofah plant（丝瓜植株）是名词复合结构，loofah-like（像丝瓜络的）是可按需构成的形容词，后者不是常见固定派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, loofah is an unanalyzable loanword; loo- and -fah should not be treated as English roots or affixes. Its plural is loofahs, and variant spellings include luffa and loofa. Loofah sponge and loofah plant are noun compounds; loofah-like is a possible productive adjective rather than a common established derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bath sponge（洗浴海绵）按用途命名，材料未必是丝瓜络；body scrubber（身体搓洗工具）泛指各种搓洗用品；sponge gourd（丝瓜）主要指植物或果实。Loofah 既可指植物，也常特指由其成熟果实纤维制成的擦洗用品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bath sponge describes an item by its use and does not specify loofah fiber; body scrubber covers many kinds of washing tools; sponge gourd mainly names the plant or fruit. Loofah can name the plant but commonly refers specifically to a scrubber made from its mature fruit fibers.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一根丝瓜，两种用途：嫩时做菜，老后留络做浴擦。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One gourd, two uses: eat it young; dry its mature fibers into a scrubber.

cloze: I felt like a _____ when I found my glasses on my head.

teaching.contrast: 非正式、带贬义或戏谑色彩；可以自嘲，直接用来称呼别人可能冒犯。它说的是愚笨，不是善良。
teaching.sentence: Only a ninny would ignore such a clear warning.
teaching.translation: 只有傻瓜才会无视这样明确的警告。

comprehension_check.sentence: Only a ninny would ignore such a clear warning.
comprehension_check.question: 句中目标词表示哪一种意思？
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: ninny 贬称愚笨的人；句中无视明确警告是愚蠢行为，不是聪明的表现。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（傻瓜／聪明人）
fields.wrong_reason: ninny 贬称愚笨的人；句中无视明确警告是愚蠢行为，不是聪明的表现。

senses.meaning_zh: 傻瓜；笨蛋（非正式、略显过时，常带轻微责怪或戏谑意味）
senses.meaning_en: A foolish or silly person; informal and somewhat old-fashioned, often mildly reproachful or teasing.
senses.english_definition: If you call someone a ninny, you mean that they are being silly or foolish.
senses.collocation_en: a silly ninny; don't be a ninny
senses.collocation_zh: 一个傻乎乎的人；别犯傻
senses.sentence_en: Don't be such a ninny—the spider is tiny.
senses.sentence_zh: 别这么傻乎乎地大惊小怪了——那只蜘蛛小得很。

etymology_story.zh: ninny 至少在十六世纪末已见于英语，可能是 innocent 的变形或缩略形式，其中 innocent 曾可指天真无知的人。这一来源尚不确定，不能把两者的联系当作已经证实的构词规则。
etymology_story.en: Ninny is recorded in English by the late sixteenth century and may be an alteration or shortening of innocent, which could describe a simple or unsuspecting person. This origin remains uncertain and should not be treated as an established word-formation rule.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作有效拆分的词干 ninny；复数为 ninnies，即辅音字母后的 y 变为 -ies。词族很小，罕用派生词 ninnyish = ninny + -ish，意为“傻乎乎的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ninny is best treated as an unanalyzed stem; its plural is ninnies, with consonant + y changing to -ies. Its small word family includes the rare adjective ninnyish, formed from ninny + -ish and meaning foolish or silly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fool（傻瓜）意义最宽泛，责备程度因语境而异；simpleton（头脑简单的人）强调理解力或判断力不足；nincompoop（笨蛋）与 ninny 一样略显过时，但往往更滑稽、更具夸张色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fool is the broadest term, with its harshness depending on context; simpleton emphasizes limited understanding or judgment; nincompoop, like ninny, sounds somewhat old-fashioned but is often more comic and exaggerated.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用可能的历史联系记忆：innocent 的“天真”过了头，就成了 ninny 的“傻气”；这只是记忆线索，并非确定词源。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the possible historical link as a hook: innocence carried too far becomes foolishness—a ninny. This is a memory aid, not a certain etymology.

forms: 可数名词；复数 perorations。
family: perorate 长篇大论地讲话；perorational 结束演说的。
usage_note: 正式修辞用语，本课只学演讲的收尾部分；也可指辞藻华丽、冗长的讲话。与开场 introduction 区分。
sentence: In her peroration, the speaker called for everyone to act.
translation: 在结束语中，演讲者呼吁大家行动起来。
collocation:
a stirring peroration 激动人心的结束语（公众演讲）
the peroration of a closing argument 结案陈词的收尾部分（法庭辩论）
context_hint: Focus on the final part of a speech.
scenario: 一场演讲即将结束，演讲者在最后一段发出行动呼吁。
hint: Focus on the final part of a speech.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 /reɪ/；-tion 读 /ʃən/。

morphology.text: perorat-（结束演说的词干）+ -ion（名词后缀）→ peroration（演讲的结束部分）；对应动词 perorate。

etymology.text: 拉丁语 peroratio 经中古英语 peroracyon 传入英语；它来自 perorare，原指把一场演说讲到收尾。想象演讲者在最后一段集中发力。

sources.label: Merriam-Webster

cloze: In her _____, the speaker called for everyone to act.

teaching.contrast: 正式修辞用语，本课只学演讲的收尾部分；也可指辞藻华丽、冗长的讲话。与开场 introduction 区分。
teaching.sentence: The lawyer saved his strongest appeal for the peroration.
teaching.translation: 律师把最有力的呼吁留到了结束语。

comprehension_check.sentence: The lawyer saved his strongest appeal for the peroration.
comprehension_check.question: 句中目标词表示哪一种意思？
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: peroration 是演讲的结束部分；把最强的呼吁留到这里，表示最后收束，而不是开场。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（演讲的结束语／演讲的开场白）
fields.wrong_reason: peroration 是演讲的结束部分；把最强的呼吁留到这里，表示最后收束，而不是开场。

senses.meaning_zh: 演说的结束部分；尤指总结论点、激发感情的结语（正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: The concluding part of a speech, especially an emphatic summary or emotional appeal; formal.
senses.english_definition: The peroration of a speech is its final part, in which the speaker often sums up the argument or appeals strongly to the audience's feelings.
senses.collocation_en: a stirring peroration; deliver a peroration
senses.collocation_zh: 激动人心的演说结语；发表演说的结束陈词
senses.sentence_en: In her peroration, she urged the audience to turn sympathy into action.
senses.sentence_zh: 在结束陈词中，她敦促听众把同情化为行动。

senses.meaning_zh: 冗长而夸夸其谈的讲话（常含贬义）
senses.meaning_en: A lengthy, pompous or grandiloquent speech; often disapproving.
senses.english_definition: If you describe someone's speech as a peroration, you often mean that it is long and uses language that sounds too grand or self-important.
senses.collocation_en: a lengthy peroration; launch into a peroration
senses.collocation_zh: 冗长的高谈阔论；开始滔滔不绝地发表宏论
senses.sentence_en: He launched into a lengthy peroration about the decline of good manners.
senses.sentence_zh: 他开始长篇大论地谈论礼貌风尚的衰退。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语和拉丁语传统进入英语，源自拉丁语 peroratio，后者来自动词 perorare，意为“讲完、结束演说”，由 per-（贯彻到底）与 orare（讲话、申辩）构成。它原指演说的收尾部分，后来也可带讽刺意味地指冗长浮夸的讲话。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through the French and Latin rhetorical tradition, ultimately from Latin peroratio, derived from perorare, 'to speak to the end,' combining per-, 'through,' and orare, 'to speak or plead.' Its original sense of a speech's conclusion later developed a sometimes mocking use for a lengthy, grandiose speech.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族可按 perorate 去掉词尾 -e，再加 -ion，构成 peroration；不宜把整个词当作由常用英语独立词根自由拼成。相关形式包括 perorate（作结束陈词；高谈阔论）、perorates、perorated、perorating，以及较少见的 perorator（作结束陈词或长篇演说的人）。
morphology_enriched.en: Within the modern word family, peroration corresponds to perorate with final -e removed and -ion added; it is not a freely assembled combination of ordinary English roots. Related forms include perorate, perorates, perorated, perorating, and the less common agent noun perorator.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: conclusion（结尾）是最中性的统称；summation（总结陈词）强调归纳论点，尤其常见于法律语境；harangue（长篇训斥）强调咄咄逼人或说教，与 peroration 的贬义用法部分重合，但不专指演说结尾。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Conclusion is the neutral general term for an ending; summation emphasizes bringing arguments together, especially in legal contexts; harangue suggests an aggressive or lecturing speech and overlaps with the disapproving sense of peroration without specifically meaning a conclusion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史构词逻辑：per-“到底”＋orare“讲话”＝把话讲到最后，落在演说的收尾重音上。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the historical logic: per-, 'through to the end,' plus orare, 'speak'—the speech reaches its final emphatic passage.

forms: 可数名词；复数 petards。本课不使用动词形式。
family: petardier 操作攻城爆炸装置的士兵。
usage_note: 历史军事用语，指用来炸开门墙的装置；习语 hoist with your own petard 表示害人反害己，但本课考实物义。
sentence: The drawing shows a petard fixed to the fortress gate.
translation: 图中画着一个固定在要塞大门上的破门爆炸装置。
collocation:
a petard at the gate 门上的破门爆炸装置（历史围城图）
a museum petard exhibit 博物馆的攻城爆炸装置展品（文物展览）
context_hint: The object is attached to a fortress gate.
scenario: 看历史围城示意图，辨认大门上标出的装置。
hint: The object is attached to a fortress gate.

pronunciation.note: 重音在第二音节；英式读音中的 r 不卷舌。

morphology.text: petard 作为独立词素记忆；petard + -ier → petardier（操作这类装置的士兵），-ier 构成人员名称。

etymology.text: 借自中古法语 pétard，与 péter（放屁、发出爆裂声）有关。这个略带滑稽的名字抓住了装置爆炸时的巨响。

sources.label: Merriam-Webster

cloze: The drawing shows a _____ fixed to the fortress gate.

teaching.contrast: 历史军事用语，指用来炸开门墙的装置；习语 hoist with your own petard 表示害人反害己，但本课考实物义。
teaching.sentence: The museum displayed a petard recovered from the ruined fort.
teaching.translation: 博物馆展出了一件从要塞遗址发现的破门爆炸装置。

comprehension_check.sentence: The museum displayed a petard recovered from the ruined fort.
comprehension_check.question: 句中目标词表示哪一种意思？
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: petard 用爆炸破坏门墙，功能是破门；不是用来保护或加固门的装置。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（破门用的爆炸装置／加固城门的防护装置）
fields.wrong_reason: petard 用爆炸破坏门墙，功能是破门；不是用来保护或加固门的装置。

senses.meaning_zh: 用于炸开城门、墙壁等的爆炸装置（历史用语）
senses.meaning_en: A historical explosive device used to breach gates, walls or other defenses.
senses.english_definition: A petard was an explosive device that soldiers placed against a gate or wall to blow an opening in it.
senses.collocation_en: attach a petard to a gate; explode a petard
senses.collocation_zh: 把破门炸药装置固定在城门上；引爆破门炸药装置
senses.sentence_en: The soldiers fixed a petard to the gate and withdrew before it exploded.
senses.sentence_zh: 士兵们把破门炸药装置固定在城门上，并在爆炸前撤离。

senses.pos: n. 名词（固定习语用法）
senses.meaning_zh: 在 be hoist with/by one's own petard 中表示“害人反害己；自食其果”
senses.meaning_en: In be hoist with/by one's own petard: to be harmed by one's own scheme against someone else.
senses.english_definition: If someone is hoist with their own petard, a plan they intended to use against someone else ends up harming them instead.
senses.collocation_en: be hoist with one's own petard; be hoist by one's own petard
senses.collocation_zh: 搬起石头砸自己的脚；因自己的害人计策而自食其果
senses.sentence_en: He was hoist with his own petard when the rule he introduced was used to remove him.
senses.sentence_zh: 他自食其果了：他自己推出的那条规定被用来将他免职。

etymology_story.zh: petard 借自法语 pétard，与 péter（放屁、发出爆裂声）有关，以爆响为这种装置命名。莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》中“被自己的炸药炸起”的意象，使相关习语成为“害人反害己”的著名表达。
etymology_story.en: Petard was borrowed from French pétard, related to péter, 'to fart or make an explosive report,' naming the device after its blast. The image of being blown up by one's own explosive in Shakespeare's Hamlet helped establish the familiar idiom for being undone by one's own scheme.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 petard 作为借入的完整词干记忆，不按英语常用词缀拆分；复数为 petards。历史上的相关人员名词为 petardier，指放置或操作破门炸药装置的士兵，属于罕见历史词汇。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, petard is a borrowed whole stem rather than a combination of productive English affixes; its plural is petards. The historical agent noun petardier denotes a soldier who placed or operated such devices and is rare historical vocabulary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: explosive charge（炸药包、装药）是较宽泛的装药名称；breaching charge（破障装药）强调炸开障碍的用途，是现代功能上较接近的表达；bomb（炸弹）范围更广，不限于贴附在城门或墙壁上的破障装置。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Explosive charge is a broader term for a quantity of explosive prepared for use; breaching charge is the closest modern functional expression, emphasizing opening a barrier; bomb is much broader and does not specifically denote a device attached to a gate or wall.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住一个画面：自己的破门炸药反把自己炸飞——于是记住“自食其果”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture your own gate-blasting explosive blowing you up: your scheme becomes your undoing.

forms: 形容词；比较程度通常用 more / most puissant。
family: puissance 力量；权势；puissantly 强有力地。
usage_note: 文学或古雅用词，日常通常用 powerful。可说强大的君主或势力；不是精确的官职名称。
sentence: The tale describes a puissant king who ruled a vast realm.
translation: 故事描写了一位统治辽阔国土的强大君王。
collocation:
a puissant ruler 强大的统治者（历史叙事）
a puissant force of nature 强大的自然力量（文学描写）
context_hint: Look at the size of the realm under the king.
scenario: 阅读一段古雅的王国故事，描写君王的权势。
hint: Look at the size of the realm under the king.

pronunciation.note: 此处用三音节读法；另有 /ˈpwɪsənt/ 等读法。

morphology.text: puissant 作为独立词素记忆；puissant + -ly → puissantly（强有力地），-ly 构成副词。

etymology.text: 十五世纪借自盎格鲁法语 pussant（有能力的、强有力的），更早联系到拉丁语 posse（能够）。它和 power、potent 有共同的历史亲缘。

sources.label: Merriam-Webster

cloze: The tale describes a _____ king who ruled a vast realm.

teaching.contrast: 文学或古雅用词，日常通常用 powerful。可说强大的君主或势力；不是精确的官职名称。
teaching.sentence: The poet praised the puissant force of the sea.
teaching.translation: 诗人赞颂了大海强大的力量。

comprehension_check.sentence: The poet praised the puissant force of the sea.
comprehension_check.question: 句中目标词表示哪一种意思？
comprehension_check.wrong_reason: puissant 表示强大；统治辽阔国土或赞叹海洋力量，都指向力量强盛，而非弱小。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（强大的／弱小的）
fields.wrong_reason: puissant 表示强大；统治辽阔国土或赞叹海洋力量，都指向力量强盛，而非弱小。

senses.meaning_zh: 强大的；有权势的；强有力的（文学或古雅用语）
senses.meaning_en: Powerful, mighty or influential; literary or archaic in tone.
senses.english_definition: Someone or something that is puissant has great power, strength or influence.
senses.collocation_en: a puissant ruler; a puissant army
senses.collocation_zh: 权势强大的统治者；强大的军队
senses.sentence_en: The prince sought an alliance with his more puissant neighbor.
senses.sentence_zh: 王子寻求与比自己更强大的邻国结盟。

etymology_story.zh: puissant 于中古英语时期借自盎格鲁法语及中古法语，原意为“有能力的、强大的”，最终可追溯至拉丁语 posse（能够、有能力）。其核心意义从“能够做到”自然延伸为“拥有强大力量或权势”。
etymology_story.en: Puissant entered Middle English from Anglo-French and Middle French with the meaning 'able or powerful,' ultimately tracing back to Latin posse, 'to be able.' The underlying idea of being able to act developed naturally into possessing great strength or authority.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 puissant 视为完整的借入形容词词干，不作 pu- 等人为拆分。词族包括 puissant + -ly → puissantly（强有力地），以及同源借入名词 puissance（力量、权势）；这两个词如今都带明显的文学或古雅色彩。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats puissant as a complete borrowed adjective stem, without an artificial division such as pu- plus a remainder. Its family includes puissantly, formed with -ly, and the related borrowed noun puissance, meaning power or might; both the adjective and noun now have a distinctly literary or archaic flavor.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: powerful（强大的）最通用，可指力量、影响或效力；mighty（强大的、威猛的）更强调非凡力量，常有庄严或文学色彩；potent（强有力的、有效力的）更侧重产生显著效果，而 puissant 常突出人物、军队或政治势力的强大。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Powerful is the broad everyday term for strength, influence or effectiveness; mighty emphasizes exceptional strength and often sounds elevated or literary; potent focuses more on producing a strong effect, whereas puissant often describes the might of rulers, armies or political powers.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从历史核心“能够”记起：不只做得到，而且有力量做到——puissant 就是“强大的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the historical idea 'able': having the strength to make things happen leads to puissant, 'powerful.'

meaning: 由多个国家联合而成的超国家
forms: 可数名词；复数 superstates。
family: state 国家；supergovernment 超国家政府。
usage_note: 本课学多个国家组成、由共同政府统辖的政治体；不把任何国际组织都叫 superstate，也不单凭词形推断它实行极权统治。
sentence: The proposal would unite the countries into a single superstate.
translation: 这项提案将把这些国家联合为一个超国家。
collocation:
form a superstate 组成超国家（政治联合方案）
a fictional superstate 虚构的超国家（小说设定）
context_hint: Notice several countries joining under one political authority.
scenario: 讨论一个把数国纳入共同政府的政治联合方案。
aliases: 由多个国家联合而成的超国家
hint: Notice several countries joining under one political authority.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 super-；state 读 /steɪt/。

morphology.text: super-（在……之上）+ state（国家）→ superstate（凌驾于成员国之上的联合政治体）。

etymology.text: 现代英语以拉丁语来源的 super- 和 state 合成这个政治词，把国家之上的共同政权形象地称为“超国家”。

teaching.sentence: The novel imagines a superstate with one parliament for five nations.

fields.wrong_reason: 这里的多个国家归于一个共同政治体，有共同议会；不是仍完全各自独立的松散群体。

senses.meaning_zh: 超国家政治实体；尤指由多个国家组成、对成员国行使共同最高权力的国家体制
senses.meaning_en: A political entity formed from several states, with overarching authority over its constituent members.
senses.english_definition: A superstate is a political organization in which several countries are joined under a government or authority that exercises power over them.
senses.collocation_en: a European superstate; a federal superstate
senses.collocation_zh: 欧洲超国家政治实体；联邦式超国家政治实体
senses.sentence_en: Critics feared that closer integration would create a superstate with powers over national governments.
senses.sentence_zh: 批评者担心，更紧密的一体化会形成一个对各国政府拥有管辖权的超国家政治实体。

etymology_story.zh: superstate 是英语用 super-（在……之上、超越）与 state（国家）组合而成的政治词汇。其构词意象是“国家之上的国家”，用于描述或设想统合多个国家并拥有更高层级权力的政治实体。
etymology_story.en: Superstate was formed in English from super-, 'above or beyond,' and state. Its image of a 'state above states' describes or envisages a political entity that unites several countries under a higher level of authority.

morphology_enriched.zh: super-（在……之上、超越）+ state（国家）→ superstate；复数为 superstates。该词本身没有常用的进一步派生词；词基 state 的常见相关词有 statehood（国家地位）、stateless（无国籍的）和 interstate（国家之间的；美国州际的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Superstate consists of super-, 'above or beyond,' plus state; its plural is superstates. It has no widely used further derivatives of its own; common relatives of the base state include statehood, stateless and interstate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: federation（联邦）强调中央与成员单位之间的宪制分权，成员未必原是独立国家；political union（政治联盟或联合体）范围较宽，不一定形成最高共同政权；supranational union（超国家联盟）强调部分权力高于成员国，但不一定达到 superstate 所暗示的国家化程度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Federation emphasizes a constitutional division of powers between a center and constituent units, which need not have been independent countries; political union is broader and need not establish a supreme common government; supranational union involves authority above member states in some areas without necessarily implying the degree of statehood suggested by superstate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: super- 是“在上面”：把多个 state 放在一个更高的共同政权下面，就是 superstate。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Super- means 'above': place several states beneath one overarching authority to picture a superstate.

forms: 化学物质名，通常作不可数名词。
family: toluol 甲苯的另一名称；toluic acid 甲基苯甲酸。
usage_note: 化学语境的物质名，可用作溶剂；与 benzene（苯）是不同物质。这里只辨认名称和用途，不涉及操作方法。
sentence: The label lists toluene as a solvent in the paint.
translation: 标签把甲苯列为这种油漆中的一种溶剂。
collocation:
toluene solvent 甲苯溶剂（涂料成分）

context_hint: Look for the named chemical used as a solvent.
scenario: 阅读油漆成分标签，找出列出的溶剂。
hint: Look for the named chemical used as a solvent.

pronunciation.note: 首音节重读；末尾 -ene 读 /iːn/。

morphology.text: tolu-（与托卢香脂名称相关）+ -ene（化学命名词尾）→ toluene（甲苯）；不要把 -ene 简单等同于某一种用途。

etymology.text: 借自法语 toluène，名字联系到托卢香脂；香脂名称又来自哥伦比亚的 Tolú 地名。记住这是从香脂名称走进化学的词。

senses.meaning_zh: 甲苯，一种无色、易燃的芳香烃液体
senses.meaning_en: A colorless, flammable aromatic hydrocarbon used as a solvent and chemical feedstock
senses.english_definition: Toluene is a colorless, flammable liquid with the formula C₇H₈ that is used as a solvent and to make other chemicals.
senses.collocation_en: toluene exposure; toluene solvent
senses.collocation_zh: 甲苯接触；甲苯溶剂
senses.sentence_en: The laboratory uses toluene as a solvent in this reaction.
senses.sentence_zh: 实验室在这一反应中使用甲苯作为溶剂。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 toluene 借自法语 toluène，其名称与曾用于制取相关物质的托卢香脂有关。香脂名称来自今哥伦比亚的 Tolú 地名，因此这个化学名称最终可以追溯到一个地名。
etymology_story.en: English toluene comes from French toluène, a name associated with balsam of Tolu, from which related chemical material had been obtained. The balsam takes its name from Tolú in present-day Colombia, so the chemical name ultimately traces back to a place.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中主要作为完整化学名称使用；历史命名结构可分析为 tolu-（联系托卢香脂的词干）+ -ene（化学命名后缀），不能据此把甲苯归为普通烯烃。主要相关形式包括 tolyl（甲苯基）、toluic acid（甲基苯甲酸）、toluate（甲基苯甲酸盐或酯），以及复合名称 nitrotoluene（硝基甲苯）、trinitrotoluene（TNT，三硝基甲苯）和 toluenesulfonic acid（甲苯磺酸）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, toluene functions mainly as a complete chemical name; its historical naming structure is tolu-, associated with balsam of Tolu, plus the chemical suffix -ene, which does not make toluene an ordinary alkene. Principal related forms include tolyl, toluic acid, and toluate, alongside compound names such as nitrotoluene, trinitrotoluene (TNT), and toluenesulfonic acid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: methylbenzene（甲基苯）与 toluene 指同一种物质，名称直接体现苯环连接一个甲基的结构；toluol（甲苯）也是同义名称，但较旧，更多见于历史或工业语境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Methylbenzene names exactly the same substance and explicitly describes a benzene ring bearing one methyl group; toluol is also an exact synonym, but is an older name encountered especially in historical or industrial contexts.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名称连到托卢香脂，结构记作“苯环＋一个甲基”：甲苯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the name to Tolu balsam and the structure to a benzene ring plus one methyl group.

forms: 通常作不可数名词，常见于 pledge / plight your troth。
family: trothless 不忠实的；betroth 使订婚。
usage_note: 古雅或文学用语，尤其见于婚姻誓词。pledge their troth 指许下忠贞誓约，不是随便提出一个计划。
sentence: Before the gathered guests, they pledged their troth.
translation: 在聚集的宾客面前，他们许下了忠贞誓约。
collocation:
pledge your troth 许下忠贞誓约（婚礼）
keep your troth 信守忠贞誓约（骑士歌谣）
context_hint: Think of a solemn promise made before wedding guests.
scenario: 传统婚礼上，新人在宾客面前宣誓。
hint: Think of a solemn promise made before wedding guests.

pronunciation.note: 末尾 /θ/ 要让舌尖轻触上齿，不能读成 /s/。

morphology.text: troth 作为独立词素记忆；troth + -less → trothless（不忠实的），-less 表示缺少。

etymology.text: 来自古英语 trēowth，经中古英语 trouth 延续下来，与 truth 同源。从真实、忠诚，便能联想到庄严许下的忠贞誓约。

cloze: Before the gathered guests, they pledged their _____.

teaching.contrast: 古雅或文学用语，尤其见于婚姻誓词。pledge their troth 指许下忠贞誓约，不是随便提出一个计划。

fields.wrong_reason: troth 是庄严的忠贞承诺，keep his troth 指信守誓约；不是对事情的猜测。

senses.meaning_zh: 忠贞誓约，尤指婚姻誓约；用于古雅或文学表达
senses.meaning_en: A solemn pledge of faithfulness, especially in marriage; archaic or literary
senses.english_definition: If you pledge your troth to someone, you solemnly promise to be faithful to them, especially as their husband or wife.
senses.collocation_en: pledge one's troth; plight one's troth
senses.collocation_zh: 许下忠贞誓言；立下婚姻誓约
senses.sentence_en: In the old wedding ceremony, each partner pledged their troth to the other.
senses.sentence_zh: 在旧式婚礼仪式中，双方各自向对方许下忠贞的誓言。

senses.meaning_zh: 忠实，忠贞；用于古雅或文学表达
senses.meaning_en: Faithfulness or loyalty; archaic or literary
senses.english_definition: A person's troth is the faithfulness they show to someone or to a promise they have made.
senses.collocation_en: keep one's troth; break one's troth
senses.collocation_zh: 恪守忠贞；背弃忠贞誓约
senses.sentence_en: Though they spent years apart, she kept her troth.
senses.sentence_zh: 尽管两人分离多年，她仍坚守忠贞。

etymology_story.zh: troth 经中古英语延续自古英语表示“真实、信实、忠诚”的词，与 truth 和 true 有共同的历史来源。它后来尤其用于表示郑重承诺的忠贞，因此保留在婚姻誓约等古雅表达中。
etymology_story.en: Troth developed through Middle English from an Old English word expressing truth, good faith, and loyalty, and shares its historical origin with truth and true. It became especially associated with solemnly promised faithfulness and survives in traditional expressions concerning marriage vows.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 troth 是不可再按常用前后缀拆解的独立词。相关词族包括 trothless（不忠的，罕用）、betroth（使订婚）、betrothed（已订婚的；未婚夫或未婚妻）和 betrothal（订婚）；true、truly、truth、truthful 等属于历史同源词族，并非由现代 troth 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, troth is a simple word without a productive internal affix division. Its related family includes the rare adjective trothless, betroth, betrothed, and betrothal; true, truly, truth, and truthful belong to its historical family rather than being direct modern derivatives of troth.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vow（誓言）强调庄严承诺，适用范围比 troth 广；pledge（郑重承诺）也可用于公开或正式保证；fidelity（忠贞）强调持续保持忠实的状态，而不是许诺这一行为。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vow emphasizes a solemn promise and has a wider range than troth; pledge can describe a public or formal commitment; fidelity emphasizes continuing faithfulness rather than the act of making a promise.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 truth 同源：把“真实可信”落实为“忠贞守誓”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of its connection with truth: being true becomes remaining faithful to a solemn promise.

forms: 指鱼时可数，复数可用 turbot 或 turbots；指鱼肉时通常不可数。
family: flatfish 鲽形鱼类，是类别词而非同词根派生词。
usage_note: 本课学鱼的名称，也常见于菜单，表示这种鱼做的菜。不是 tuna（金枪鱼），也不是所有扁鱼的统称。
sentence: The fisherman lifted a large turbot from the net.
translation: 渔民从网里提起一条大菱鲆。
collocation:
catch a turbot 捕到一条大菱鲆（海上捕捞）
grilled turbot 烤大菱鲆（餐厅点菜）
context_hint: The sentence names a flat-bodied sea fish.
scenario: 渔船收网后，辨认网中的一条扁平海鱼。
hint: The sentence names a flat-bodied sea fish.

pronunciation.note: 首音节重读；结尾 -ot 在这里读 /ət/。

morphology.text: turbot 作为独立词素记忆；turbot + -like → turbot-like（像大菱鲆的），-like 表示形状或特征相似。

etymology.text: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语 turbut 借入这个鱼名。把扁平、近菱形的身体和这个整词一起记住，比硬拆字母更直观。

etymology_story.zh: turbot 在中古英语时期从盎格鲁法语的鱼名 turbut 等形式借入。这个名称更早的来源并不确定，不宜依据现代英语中的相似字母强行拆解。
etymology_story.en: Turbot entered Middle English from Anglo-French fish names such as turbut. Its earlier origin is uncertain, so similarities to parts of modern English words do not provide a reliable historical analysis.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 turbot 是不可进一步拆分的鱼名，没有常用的派生词族。表示多条鱼时复数可用 turbot 或 turbots；表示鱼肉时通常不可数；turbot-like（像大菱鲆的）是可以临时构成的描述性复合词，并非常用固定派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, turbot is an unanalyzable fish name with no established common family of derivatives. Its fish plural can be turbot or turbots, while the food sense is normally uncountable; turbot-like is a possible descriptive compound rather than a common established derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: European turbot（欧洲大菱鲆）可用来明确指通常所说的大菱鲆；flatfish（比目鱼）是包含它的上位类别；brill（光滑菱鲆）是外形相近的另一种鱼，并非严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: European turbot can explicitly identify the fish ordinarily called turbot; flatfish is the broader category containing it; brill names a similar-looking but distinct fish and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词配图记忆：宽扁、近菱形的鱼身，就是大菱鲆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Attach the whole word to one image: a broad, flat, almost diamond-shaped fish.

forms: 可数名词；复数 twerps。另有较少见拼写 twirp。
family: twerpish 讨厌而愚蠢的；twerpishly 讨厌而愚蠢地。
usage_note: 非正式贬称，表达说话者觉得对方愚蠢、无足轻重或令人讨厌；直接称呼别人会冒犯。
sentence: She called him a twerp after he laughed at her mistake.
translation: 他嘲笑她的失误后，她骂他是个讨厌的蠢家伙。
collocation:
an annoying twerp 讨厌的蠢家伙（日常抱怨）
play a pompous twerp 扮演自大的蠢家伙（喜剧表演）
context_hint: Listen for the speaker expressing contempt for a person.
scenario: 有人嘲笑别人的失误，对方用一句不客气的话回击。
hint: Listen for the speaker expressing contempt for a person.

pronunciation.note: 单音节；英式 /ɜː/ 后接 /p/。

morphology.text: twerp 作为独立词素记忆；twerp + -ish → twerpish（像讨厌的蠢家伙的），-ish 构成描述特点的形容词。

etymology.text: 这是英语俚语，约1923年已有记录，更早的来源尚不明确。可联想一个自以为了不起、却只会惹人烦的小人物，记住它的轻蔑语气。

senses.meaning_en: A foolish, annoying, or insignificant person; an informal insult
senses.english_definition: If you call someone a twerp, you mean that you think they are foolish, annoying, or unimportant.
senses.collocation_en: a little twerp; an annoying twerp
senses.collocation_zh: 讨厌的小蠢货；惹人烦的蠢家伙
senses.sentence_en: Stop being such a twerp and give her phone back.
senses.sentence_zh: 别这么讨厌了，把她的手机还给她。

etymology_story.zh: twerp 在二十世纪早期作为英语俚语出现，更早的来源尚不确定。它形成了对愚蠢、惹人烦或自以为是的小人物的轻蔑称呼。
etymology_story.en: Twerp emerged as English slang in the early twentieth century, and its earlier origin is uncertain. It became a dismissive label for someone regarded as foolish, irritating, or self-important.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 twerp 是独立词根，复数为 twerps。可见的非正式派生形式包括 twerp + -ish → twerpish（像蠢家伙的）和 twerp + -y → twerpy（愚蠢讨厌的），但这些形容词远不如名词常见。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, twerp is a simple base, with the plural twerps. Informal derivatives include twerp + -ish → twerpish and twerp + -y → twerpy, both describing foolish or irritating behavior, though these adjectives are much less common than the noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: twit（傻瓜）侧重愚蠢，常带较轻的嘲弄；jerk（讨厌鬼）更侧重粗鲁、自私或不体贴；pipsqueak（无足轻重的小人物）侧重渺小或缺乏影响力，未必表示愚蠢。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Twit emphasizes foolishness and often sounds mildly mocking; jerk focuses more on rude, selfish, or inconsiderate behavior; pipsqueak emphasizes smallness or lack of importance without necessarily implying stupidity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把它想成一声短促的嫌弃：“这个讨厌的小蠢货！”这是语气联想，不是词源拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear it as a short burst of irritation: 'That annoying little fool!' This is a tone-based memory cue, not an etymological analysis.

forms: 可数名词；德语式复数 Weltanschauungen，也见英语式 Weltanschauungs。
family: Welt 德语“世界”；Anschauung 德语“看法”。
usage_note: 哲学、思想史用语；保留德语写法时通常首字母大写，也见小写 weltanschauung。这里指整套世界观，不是一时意见。
sentence: Her Weltanschauung shaped the way she wrote about justice.
translation: 她的世界观影响了她书写正义的方式。
collocation:
a personal Weltanschauung 个人世界观（人生思想）
the Weltanschauung of a movement 一场运动的世界观（思想史研究）
context_hint: Think of an overall view that shapes beliefs about life.
scenario: 读作家评论时，讨论她对世界和人生的整体理解。
hint: Think of an overall view that shapes beliefs about life.

pronunciation.note: w 按德语来源读 /v/；sch 读 /ʃ/；末尾 ng 为 /ŋ/。

morphology.text: 德语 Welt（世界）+ Anschauung（看法）→ Weltanschauung（世界观）；英语中通常把这个借词整体使用。

etymology.text: 十九世纪从德语借入英语，字面就是“对世界的看法”。它把一个人理解人生、社会与世界的整套观点收在一个词里。

fields.wrong_reason: Weltanschauung 指理解世界的整体观念体系；影响一场运动的思想框架不是临时意见。

senses.meaning_zh: 世界观；理解世界与人生的整体观念体系，属于正式或学术用语
senses.meaning_en: A comprehensive view of the world and human life; a formal or academic term
senses.english_definition: Someone's Weltanschauung is the overall set of beliefs and ideas through which they understand the world and their place in it.
senses.collocation_en: a religious Weltanschauung; a philosophical Weltanschauung
senses.collocation_zh: 宗教世界观；哲学世界观
senses.sentence_en: Her religious upbringing shaped her Weltanschauung.
senses.sentence_zh: 她所受的宗教教育塑造了她的世界观。

etymology_story.zh: Weltanschauung 在十九世纪从德语进入英语，由 Welt（世界）和 Anschauung（观看、理解或观念）组成。它从字面上的“观看世界的方式”发展为理解现实、人生与价值的整体思想框架。
etymology_story.en: Weltanschauung entered English from German in the nineteenth century, combining Welt, 'world,' with Anschauung, 'contemplation, perception, or conception.' From the literal idea of viewing the world, it developed the sense of a comprehensive framework for understanding reality, life, and values.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中通常作为整体借词使用，没有常用的英语派生词族。德语内部结构为 Welt（世界）+ Anschauung（观念、直观），其中 Anschauung 来自 anschauen（观看、审视）+ 名词后缀 -ung；英语中可见保留的德语复数 Weltanschauungen，也可见英语化复数 Weltanschauungs，词首亦可小写。
morphology_enriched.en: English normally treats this as a complete loanword, without a common English family of derivatives. Its German structure is Welt, 'world,' plus Anschauung, 'conception or perception'; Anschauung derives from anschauen, 'to look at or contemplate,' with the noun-forming suffix -ung. English uses both the retained German plural Weltanschauungen and the anglicized Weltanschauungs, and lowercase spelling also occurs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: worldview（世界观）是最直接、最通俗的对应词；outlook（人生观、看法）常侧重个人态度或看待生活的方式，未必构成完整体系；ideology（意识形态）更强调组织化的社会或政治信念。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Worldview is the closest and most accessible equivalent; outlook often emphasizes a person's attitude or approach to life without implying a complete system; ideology more strongly suggests an organized set of social or political beliefs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Welt＝世界，Anschauung＝看法：把看世界的整套“镜片”合成一个词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Welt means world and Anschauung means conception: imagine the complete set of lenses through which you view the world.

forms: 形容词；比较程度通常用 more / most antediluvian。
family: diluvian 洪水的；antediluvians 大洪水前的人（名词复数）。
usage_note: 本课学带幽默或批评色彩的“古老过时的”；原本的宗教历史义“大洪水前的”只作来历提示。
sentence: We finally replaced the antediluvian computer in the office.
translation: 我们终于换掉了办公室那台古老过时的电脑。
collocation:
antediluvian equipment 古老过时的设备（办公室更新）
antediluvian attitudes 过时的观念（社会讨论）
context_hint: The machine is so old that replacing it feels overdue.
scenario: 办公室终于决定淘汰一台用了多年的老电脑。
hint: The machine is so old that replacing it feels overdue.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 /luː/；不要漏掉结尾 /viən/。

morphology.text: ante-（在……之前）+ diluvi-（洪水）+ -an（……的）→ antediluvian（大洪水以前的），引申为古老过时的。

etymology.text: 借自新拉丁语 antediluvianus，由拉丁语“在前”和“洪水”构成；原指《圣经》大洪水以前，后来夸张地形容老得跟不上时代。

teaching.contrast: 本课学带幽默或批评色彩的“古老过时的”；原本的宗教历史义“大洪水前的”只作来历提示。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（古老过时的／新潮先进的）
fields.wrong_reason: antediluvian 在这里夸张地说东西或观念十分陈旧；不是先进新潮。

senses.meaning_zh: 极其陈旧的；过时守旧的，常含幽默或贬义
senses.meaning_en: Extremely old or old-fashioned, often humorously or disapprovingly.
senses.english_definition: If you describe something as antediluvian, you mean that it seems extremely old or belongs to a way of thinking that is no longer acceptable.
senses.collocation_en: antediluvian attitudes; antediluvian technology
senses.collocation_zh: 陈腐的态度；老掉牙的技术
senses.sentence_en: The company still relies on an antediluvian system for tracking orders.
senses.sentence_zh: 这家公司仍然依靠一套老掉牙的系统来跟踪订单。

senses.meaning_zh: 《圣经》所述大洪水以前的
senses.meaning_en: Of or belonging to the time before the Flood described in the Bible.
senses.english_definition: Antediluvian people or events belong to the period before the great flood described in the Bible.
senses.collocation_en: the antediluvian world; antediluvian patriarchs
senses.collocation_zh: 大洪水以前的世界；大洪水以前的族长
senses.sentence_en: The chapter discusses the long lives of the antediluvian patriarchs.
senses.sentence_zh: 这一章讨论了大洪水以前诸位族长的长寿。

senses.meaning_zh: 极守旧的人；老古董；原指大洪水以前的人，名词用法较少见
senses.meaning_en: An extremely old-fashioned person; originally, a person living before the biblical Flood. The noun is uncommon.
senses.english_definition: An antediluvian is someone whose ideas seem extremely old-fashioned, or, in biblical discussion, someone who lived before the Flood.
senses.collocation_en: a political antediluvian; an old antediluvian (uncommon noun combinations)
senses.collocation_zh: 政治上的老顽固；老古董，均为较少见的名词搭配
senses.sentence_en: He jokingly calls himself an antediluvian because he still writes every letter by hand.
senses.sentence_zh: 他开玩笑地称自己是个老古董，因为他仍然每封信都用手写。

etymology_story.zh: 该词以拉丁语 ante（在……以前）和 diluvium（洪水）为基础，17世纪用于指《圣经》大洪水以前的时代。到18世纪初，它也被夸张地用于形容极其古老的人或事物，进而产生“陈旧守旧”的含义。[词源与用法：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/antediluvian)
etymology_story.en: Built from Latin ante, meaning 'before,' and diluvium, meaning 'flood,' the word was used in seventeenth-century English for the period before the biblical Flood. By the early eighteenth century, it also humorously described extremely old people or things, developing its familiar sense of being hopelessly outdated. [History and usage: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/antediluvian)

morphology_enriched.zh: 学习性构词分析：ante-（在……以前）+ diluvi-（洪水词干）+ -an（……的）；diluvi- 不是现代英语中的独立单词。同形词 antediluvian 可作形容词或名词，名词复数为 antediluvians；相关词有 diluvial、diluvian（洪水的）和 postdiluvian（大洪水以后的），它们属于相关构词系列，并非都由 antediluvian 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful structural analysis is ante- ('before') + diluvi- (the stem associated with 'flood') + -an ('relating to'); diluvi- is not an independent modern English word. Antediluvian functions as both adjective and noun, with the plural antediluvians; related formations include diluvial and diluvian ('relating to a flood') and postdiluvian ('after the biblical Flood'), rather than direct derivatives of antediluvian.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: archaic（古旧的）强调属于早期时代，尤其用于语言或形式；outdated（过时的）强调已不适合当前情况；obsolete（已淘汰的）强调已被替代或不再使用。antediluvian 的夸张和嘲讽色彩通常更强，形容观念时尤其突出守旧。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Archaic emphasizes an earlier historical period, especially in language or form; outdated means no longer suited to present conditions; obsolete suggests replacement or discontinued use. Antediluvian is usually more exaggerated and mocking, particularly when describing conservative attitudes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “洪水以前的”→ 老得像远古遗物 → 老古董、老观念。
mnemonic_anchor.en: 'Before the Flood' → unimaginably old → ancient equipment or outdated thinking.

forms: 形容词；不作规则复数或动词时态变化。
family: atherosclerosis 动脉粥样硬化；atheroma 动脉粥样斑块。
usage_note: 医学描述词，常修饰 plaque、lesion、artery；与泛指动脉硬化的 arteriosclerotic 相关但不完全等同。本课只识别词义。
sentence: The scan showed an atherosclerotic plaque in the artery.
translation: 扫描显示动脉内有一处粥样硬化斑块。
collocation:
atherosclerotic plaque 粥样硬化斑块（影像报告）
atherosclerotic artery 动脉粥样硬化的血管（医学教学）
context_hint: Focus on the adjective describing the plaque in an artery.
scenario: 在医学英语阅读中辨认扫描报告里的病变描述。
hint: Focus on the adjective describing the plaque in an artery.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 /rɒt/；开头 th 读 /θ/。

morphology.text: athero-（粥样斑块）+ sclerot-（硬化）+ -ic（……的）→ atherosclerotic（动脉粥样硬化的）。

etymology.text: 来自新拉丁语医学名称 atherosclerosis 的形容词形式；名称采用希腊语“粥状物”和“硬化”的成分，形象地描写血管内壁的粥样沉积与变硬。

senses.meaning_zh: 动脉粥样硬化的；与动脉壁粥样斑块形成有关的
senses.meaning_en: Affected by or relating to the buildup of fatty plaques within artery walls.
senses.english_definition: Atherosclerotic changes or conditions involve fatty material building up within artery walls, causing them to thicken and harden.
senses.collocation_en: atherosclerotic plaque; atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
senses.collocation_zh: 动脉粥样硬化斑块；动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病
senses.sentence_en: The scan revealed atherosclerotic plaque in the carotid artery.
senses.sentence_zh: 扫描显示颈动脉内存在动脉粥样硬化斑块。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是新拉丁语医学名称 atherosclerosis（动脉粥样硬化）的形容词形式，其希腊语构词成分分别表示“粥状物”和“硬化”。这个名称用粥状物比喻斑块中的软性物质，并与动脉壁的硬化相联系。[词条与词源：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/atherosclerotic)
etymology_story.en: The adjective belongs to the medical term atherosclerosis, a New Latin formation using Greek elements for 'gruel' and 'hardening.' The imagery connects the soft, gruel-like material in plaques with the hardening of artery walls. [Entry and word history: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/atherosclerotic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词：athero-（粥样物；粥样斑块）+ sclerot-（硬化）+ -ic（……的）；与名词 atherosclerosis 的 -osis（病理状态）形成词尾交替，而不是直接在整个名词后加 -ic。词族包括 atherosclerosis（动脉粥样硬化）、atherosclerotic（动脉粥样硬化的）、atherosclerotically（以动脉粥样硬化方式，少用）和 antiatherosclerotic（抗动脉粥样硬化的）；相关词根词有 atheroma（粥样斑块）、atheromatous（粥样斑块的）、sclerosis（硬化）和 sclerotic（硬化的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Medical formation: athero- ('gruel-like material; atheromatous plaque') + sclerot- ('hardening') + -ic ('relating to'). The ending alternates with -osis ('pathological condition') in atherosclerosis, rather than simply attaching -ic to the entire noun. The family includes atherosclerosis, atherosclerotic, the uncommon adverb atherosclerotically, and antiatherosclerotic; related root-family words include atheroma, atheromatous, sclerosis, and sclerotic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: arteriosclerotic（动脉硬化的）范围更广，不一定涉及粥样斑块；atheromatous（粥样斑块的）突出斑块本身；sclerotic（硬化的）泛指组织硬化。三者均不能在所有语境中与 atherosclerotic 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Arteriosclerotic is broader and need not involve atheromatous plaques; atheromatous emphasizes the plaques themselves; sclerotic describes tissue hardening generally. None is interchangeable with atherosclerotic in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: athero- 粥样斑块 + sclerot- 硬化：动脉壁里积了“粥”，血管壁随之变厚变硬。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Athero- supplies the 'gruel-like plaque'; sclerot- supplies the hardening: plaque builds within an artery wall.

forms: 可数名词；复数 braggarts。本课不用作动词。
family: brag 吹牛；bragging 吹嘘。
usage_note: 贬义可数名词，指总爱夸耀自己的人。自信 confident 不等于爱吹牛；本课学人物名词义。
sentence: Nobody believed the braggart when he claimed to own three castles.
translation: 那个吹牛者说自己有三座城堡时，谁也不相信。
collocation:
an unbearable braggart 令人受不了的吹牛者（社交场合）
a comic braggart 喜剧中的吹牛人物（戏剧评论）
context_hint: The person makes grand claims about his possessions.
scenario: 聚会上有人夸口说自己拥有好几座城堡，大家都不信。
hint: The person makes grand claims about his possessions.

pronunciation.note: 首音节 /bræɡ/ 重读；结尾弱读 /ət/。

morphology.text: brag（吹牛）+ -art（带贬义的人员后缀）→ braggart（吹牛者）；拼写中 g 双写。

etymology.text: 一方面与英语 brag 加 -art 有关，另一方面受中古法语 bragard（过分自负的）影响。记住它把“吹牛”变成了“爱吹牛的人”。

senses.meaning_en: A person who boasts arrogantly about personal qualities, possessions, or achievements.

senses.collocation_zh: 令人难以忍受的吹牛者；出了名的吹牛大王
senses.sentence_en: He was such a braggart that every conversation turned into a story about his success.
senses.sentence_zh: 他太爱自吹自擂了，每次聊天都会变成他讲述自己成功经历的独角戏。

senses.meaning_zh: 自吹自擂的；夸夸其谈的，较少见，多见于文学表达
senses.meaning_en: Boastful or arrogantly self-praising; less common and often literary.
senses.english_definition: Braggart talk or behavior shows that someone is trying to impress others by praising themselves too much.
senses.collocation_en: braggart talk; a braggart soldier (less common, often literary)
senses.collocation_zh: 夸夸其谈；爱吹牛的士兵，均较少见，常用于文学表达
senses.sentence_en: His braggart manner concealed a deep fear of failure.
senses.sentence_zh: 他自吹自擂的姿态掩盖着内心对失败的深深恐惧。

etymology_story.zh: braggart 的形成既与英语 brag（吹牛）加人员后缀 -art 有关，也受到中古法语 bragard（过分自负的）的影响。它在16世纪已用于指傲慢地夸耀自己的人，后来也用作表示这种性格或行为的形容词。[词源与词性：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/braggart)
etymology_story.en: Braggart arose partly from English brag with the personal suffix -art and partly through borrowing from Middle French bragard, meaning 'excessively proud.' Recorded in the sixteenth century for an arrogant boaster, it also functions as an adjective describing boastful people or behavior. [History and parts of speech: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/braggart)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习分析：brag（吹牛）+ -art（带贬义的人称后缀）→ braggart，拼写中 g 双写；-art 不能理解成独立名词 art（艺术）。核心词族有 brag（吹牛；夸耀）、brags、bragged、bragging（动词屈折形式，bragging 也可作名词）、bragger（吹牛者）、braggart（名词兼形容词）和 braggarts（名词复数）；braggartism（自夸行为）较少见，braggadocio（狂妄自夸）是相关词，并非直接由 braggart 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning: brag ('boast') + -art (a disparaging personal suffix) → braggart, with doubled g; the ending is unrelated to the independent noun art. The core family includes brag, its inflections brags, bragged, and bragging, the noun use of bragging, bragger, braggart as noun and adjective, and plural braggarts. Braggartism is an uncommon noun for boastfulness; braggadocio is related rather than a direct derivative of braggart.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boaster（自夸者）意义最接近，表达较一般；blowhard（夸夸其谈的人）更口语化，突出说大话、令人厌烦；boastful（爱自夸的）是对应的常用形容词。braggart 通常带有鲜明的贬义，强调自负和反复炫耀。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boaster is the closest general noun; blowhard is more informal and emphasizes loud, irritating talk; boastful is the usual adjective for the same tendency. Braggart strongly disapproves of arrogant, repeated self-promotion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: brag 是“吹牛”；braggart 就是把“吹牛”活成人设的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Brag names the action; a braggart makes bragging a habit.

senses.meaning_zh: 女像柱；用作建筑支撑的女性雕像
senses.meaning_en: A sculpted female figure serving as an architectural support.
senses.english_definition: A caryatid is a statue of a woman that supports part of a building in place of a column.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经拉丁语复数 caryatides 借自希腊语 karyatides，该词与拉科尼亚地区卡律艾城的阿耳忒弥斯女祭司有关。建筑术语沿用这个名称，指以女性形象代替普通柱子承托上部结构的雕像。[词源与释义：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/caryatid)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the term through Latin caryatides from Greek karyatides, associated with priestesses of Artemis at Caryae in Laconia. In architecture, the name designates a female sculptural figure that supports an upper structure in place of an ordinary column. [History and definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/caryatid)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 caryatid 作为完整的借入词基学习，不拆成 carry 等英语词。词形与派生包括 caryatids（规则复数）、caryatides（古典复数）、caryatidal（女像柱的）和 caryatic（女像柱的，较少见）；其中 caryatidal 可分析为 caryatid + -al。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, caryatid is best treated as a complete borrowed base, not divided into English words such as carry. Its forms and derivatives include the regular plural caryatids, the classical plural caryatides, caryatidal ('relating to caryatids'), and the less common adjective caryatic; caryatidal is transparently caryatid + -al.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: female figure support（女性人像支撑）是解释性近义表达；column（柱）范围更广，通常没有人形；telamon（男像柱）是男性人像支撑，属于对应建筑构件。caryatid 专指女性人像支撑，没有常用的完全等义单词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Female figure support is an explanatory equivalent; column is broader and usually lacks a human form; telamon denotes the corresponding male figure support. Caryatid specifically identifies a female architectural support and has no common exact one-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一位石雕女子用头顶托住屋檐：女性雕像兼作柱子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a stone woman carrying the roof on her head: a female statue doing a column's job.

forms: 药物名称，通常作不可数名词。
family: quinoline 喹啉，是名称中的相关化学成分。
usage_note: 药物名，属于抗疟药；本课只辨认药名。antibiotic 是抗生素的类别词，不能当作它的同义词。

morphology.text: chloro-（氯）+ quinoline（喹啉，缩合）→ chloroquine（氯喹）；这是化学名称的缩合，不是把普通词强行切开。

etymology.text: 英语药名由表示氯的 chlor- 和 quinoline（喹啉）缩合而来，二十世纪已有使用记录。名字把它的含氯喹啉结构留了下来。

senses.meaning_zh: 氯喹，一种合成抗疟药
senses.meaning_en: A synthetic antimalarial drug.
senses.english_definition: Chloroquine is a drug used to prevent or treat malaria caused by parasites that are sensitive to it.
senses.collocation_en: chloroquine phosphate; chloroquine resistance
senses.collocation_zh: 磷酸氯喹；氯喹耐药性

etymology_story.zh: chloroquine 是由 chlor-（氯）与 quinoline（喹啉）的缩合成分构成的20世纪药名，英语使用记录可追溯至1946年。这个名称体现了药物所含的氯取代喹啉结构。[词源与释义：Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chloroquine)
etymology_story.en: Chloroquine is a twentieth-century drug name formed from chlor- ('chlorine') and a shortened form of quinoline, with English use recorded from 1946. Its name reflects the drug's chlorine-substituted quinoline structure. [History and definition: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chloroquine)

morphology_enriched.zh: 药名构词：chlor-（氯）+ quinoline（喹啉）的缩合形式 → chloroquine；这是化学命名中的缩合，不能机械地把每个字母片段当成普通英语词缀。相关名称有 hydroxychloroquine（羟氯喹，相关但不同的药物）和 desethylchloroquine（去乙基氯喹，一种代谢产物）；chloroquine-resistant（耐氯喹的）与 chloroquine-sensitive（对氯喹敏感的）是复合形容词，chloroquine phosphate（磷酸氯喹）是盐形式名称。
morphology_enriched.en: Drug-name formation: chlor- ('chlorine') + a contracted form of quinoline → chloroquine; this is chemical-name contraction rather than a sequence of ordinary English affixes. Related names include hydroxychloroquine, a related but different drug, and desethylchloroquine, a metabolite. Chloroquine-resistant and chloroquine-sensitive are compound adjectives; chloroquine phosphate names a salt form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该药名没有可随意替换的常用同义词。antimalarial（抗疟药）是上位类别；hydroxychloroquine（羟氯喹）是相关但不同的药物；quinine（奎宁）是另一种抗疟药，不能因名称相似而视作氯喹的别名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The drug name has no common freely interchangeable synonym. Antimalarial names the broader drug class; hydroxychloroquine is a related but different drug; quinine is another antimalarial and is not an alternative name for chloroquine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chlor- 提示“氯”，quinoline 提示“喹啉”：含氯的喹啉类药物 → 氯喹。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chlor- signals chlorine; quinoline supplies the chemical framework: a chlorine-containing quinoline drug.

forms: 法律拉丁语借词；本课按抽象名词使用。
family: culpable 有过失的；culpability 过失责任。
usage_note: 罕见法律用词，常与故意欺诈 dolus 对举；本课只学词义“过失”，不据此推断具体法律责任。

collocation:

mea culpa 我的过错（承认错误的表达）

scenario: 阅读法律拉丁语术语表，区分疏忽和故意行为。
hint: Notice the contrast between negligence and deliberate fraud.

pronunciation.note: 首音节重读；末尾 a 弱读为 /ə/。

morphology.text: 拉丁语 culp-（过失）+ -able（可归责的）→ culpable（有过失的）；culpa 在英语中作为独立法律借词记忆。

etymology.text: 直接借自拉丁语 culpa（过错、罪责）。熟悉 mea culpa（我的过错）就容易记住：核心是承认或归属的过失。

senses.pos: n. 名词（拉丁语借词，主要见于法律术语及固定表达）
senses.meaning_zh: 过错；过失；罪责
senses.meaning_en: fault, negligence, or blame
senses.english_definition: Culpa is fault or blame for something wrong, especially in legal language or the expression mea culpa.
senses.chinese_definition: culpa 指应为错误承担的过错或责任，主要用于法律语言或 mea culpa 这一固定表达。
senses.collocation_en: mea culpa
senses.collocation_zh: 我的过错；认错，自责的表示
senses.sentence_en: He offered a public mea culpa for the error.
senses.sentence_zh: 他为这个错误公开认错。

etymology_story.zh: 直接借自拉丁语 culpa，意为“过错、过失、罪责”。它在英语中主要保留于法律术语和 mea culpa（字面意为“我的过错”）等表达中，后者也可指一次认错或道歉。
etymology_story.en: Culpa was borrowed directly from Latin culpa, meaning fault, negligence, or blame. In English it survives chiefly in legal terminology and expressions such as mea culpa, literally “my fault,” which can also denote an acknowledgment of fault or an apology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 culpa 视为不可再作常规拆分的拉丁语借词；不能把词尾 -a 当作英语能产后缀。同源词族包括 culpable（应受责备的）、culpably（应受责备地）、culpability／culpableness（可责性）、exculpate（证明无罪或无责）、exculpation（开脱）、exculpatory（开脱罪责的）、inculpate（归罪于）、inculpation（归罪）和 inculpatory（归罪的）；这些是同源词，并非都由英语 culpa 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, culpa is an unanalyzed Latin loan; its final -a is not a productive English suffix. Its etymological family includes culpable, culpably, culpability, culpableness, exculpate, exculpation, exculpatory, inculpate, inculpation, and inculpatory; these are related formations rather than direct English derivatives of culpa.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fault（过错）最通用；blame（责备、责任）强调责任的归属；negligence（疏忽、过失）强调未尽应有注意。culpa 带明显的拉丁语或法律语体色彩，具体含义取决于所在表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fault is the broad everyday term; blame emphasizes the attribution of responsibility; negligence specifically concerns a failure to take proper care. Culpa has a distinctly Latin or legal register, and its precise meaning depends on the expression.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mea culpa＝“我的过错”：用固定表达锁定 culpa 的“过错、责任”核心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mea culpa means “my fault”: anchor culpa to fault and responsibility.

comprehension_check.wrong_reason: dib 指让鱼饵轻轻浮沉、点触水面；不是固定放在水底。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（轻提鱼饵使其浮沉垂钓／把鱼饵固定沉在水底垂钓）
answers: 轻提鱼饵使其浮沉垂钓
fields.wrong_reason: dib 指让鱼饵轻轻浮沉、点触水面；不是固定放在水底。

senses.pos: v. 动词（不及物；罕用钓鱼术语）
senses.meaning_zh: 轻点或轻提鱼饵，使其在水面浮沉以诱鱼
senses.meaning_en: to fish by lightly dipping or moving bait at the water's surface
senses.english_definition: If you dib, you fish by letting the bait touch or move lightly on the surface of the water.
senses.chinese_definition: dib 指让鱼饵轻触水面或在水面轻轻浮动，以这种方式钓鱼。
senses.collocation_en: dib for trout; dib with a natural fly
senses.collocation_zh: 用轻点水面的钓法钓鳟鱼；用真蝇作饵轻点水面垂钓
senses.sentence_en: He dibbed for trout beneath the overhanging branches.
senses.sentence_zh: 他在伸向水面的树枝下轻点鱼饵，垂钓鳟鱼。

etymology_story.zh: dib 是一个较早的英语动词，曾表示轻点、轻蘸等动作，可能与 dab 的变体有关，但具体来源并不确定。其钓鱼义把这种轻触动作用于鱼饵接触水面的过程。
etymology_story.en: Dib is an older English verb associated with light tapping or dipping, possibly a variant of dab, though its precise origin is uncertain. Its fishing sense applies that light movement to bait touching the water.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dib 为基本词干；dib + -s → dibs，dib + -ed → dibbed，dib + -ing → dibbing；加元音开头的词尾时双写 b。dibbing 也可作动名词，表示这种钓法；常见口语表达 have dibs on（对……有优先权）应另作词条处理，不能据此把“优先权”直接列为 dib 的常用单数义。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern morphology: dib is the base; dib + -s gives dibs, dib + -ed gives dibbed, and dib + -ing gives dibbing, with b doubled before a vowel-initial ending. Dibbing can also name the fishing technique; the familiar expression have dibs on belongs under the separate entry dibs and does not establish a common singular dib meaning a priority claim.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dap（轻点水面垂钓）是此义最接近的钓鱼术语；dip（轻蘸、浸入）仅描述动作；angle（垂钓）泛指用钩线钓鱼。dib 特指鱼饵在水面附近轻点浮动的方式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dap is the closest fishing synonym; dip describes the movement without necessarily implying fishing; angle broadly means to fish with a hook and line. Dib specifies a light bait movement at or near the surface.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 鱼饵“点一下水”：轻点动作连接到这种钓法。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the bait giving the water a tiny tap: the light movement explains the fishing sense.

forms: 可数名词；复数 disquisitions。
family: disquisitional 专题论述的；disquisitive 探究性的。
usage_note: 正式书面语，指详尽、有分析性的论述，可书面也可口头；有时略带嫌其冗长的语气。
sentence: Her essay became a disquisition on the meaning of freedom.
translation: 她的文章写成了一篇讨论自由含义的专题论述。
collocation:
a philosophical disquisition 哲学专题论述（论文写作）
launch into a disquisition 开始长篇论述（餐桌谈话）
context_hint: Think of a detailed discussion that examines one subject.
scenario: 读到一篇细致讨论自由含义的长文章。
hint: Think of a detailed discussion that examines one subject.

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 /zɪ/；qu 读 /kw/。

morphology.text: dis-（分开、逐一）+ quisit-（探求）+ -ion（名词后缀）→ disquisition（深入探讨的论述）；这是拉丁语词干的构词线索。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 disquisitio，源于 disquirere（调查、探究）；其中 quaerere 表示寻求。把一个问题逐层查清，再讲成一篇专题论述。

fields.label: 句中目标词表示（专题论述／简短的闲聊）
fields.wrong_reason: disquisition 是详尽分析一个主题的论述；不是随意而简短的闲聊。

senses.meaning_zh: 专题论述；长篇而详尽的探讨
senses.meaning_en: a long, detailed discussion or examination of a subject
senses.english_definition: A disquisition is a long and detailed discussion of a particular subject, especially in speech or writing.
senses.chinese_definition: disquisition 指针对某一专题展开的长篇、详尽的口头或书面论述。
senses.collocation_en: a lengthy disquisition; a disquisition on a subject
senses.collocation_zh: 长篇论述；关于某一主题的专题论述
senses.sentence_en: What began as a simple question led to a lengthy disquisition on the nature of justice.
senses.sentence_zh: 一个简单的问题引出了一番关于正义本质的长篇论述。

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 disquisitio（调查、探究），对应动词 disquirere（仔细探查），后者与 quaerere（寻求、询问）有关。词义由探究过程发展为详尽呈现探究内容的论述。
etymology_story.en: Disquisition comes from Latin disquisitio, an investigation or inquiry, associated with disquirere, to investigate thoroughly, and ultimately quaerere, to seek or ask. Its meaning developed from the act of inquiry to a detailed discussion presenting that inquiry.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以完整词干 disquisition 为基础，复数为 disquisitions；教学上可借历史词干 disquisit- + 名词后缀 -ion 理解，但不能把 quisit 当作独立英语词。直接词族包括较罕见的 disquisitional、disquisitionary（专题论述的）；inquisition（调查、审讯）、acquisition（获得）和 requisition（正式征用、要求）属于更远的拉丁语同源词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, disquisition functions as a complete stem, with the plural disquisitions; the historical stem disquisit- plus the noun suffix -ion provides a learning aid, but quisit is not an independent English word. Direct family members include the uncommon adjectives disquisitional and disquisitionary; inquisition, acquisition, and requisition are more distant Latin relatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: treatise（专论）强调系统、正式的书面著作；discourse（论述）可指较广泛的口头或书面讨论；exposition（阐述）强调清楚解释。disquisition 突出详尽和篇幅较长，有时略带“讲得过长”的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A treatise is typically a systematic formal written work; discourse covers a broader range of spoken or written discussion; exposition emphasizes explanation. Disquisition stresses detail and length and can sometimes suggest excessive elaboration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “追问到底，再详细讲透”：探究发展成长篇专题论述。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Investigate thoroughly, then explain at length: inquiry becomes a detailed discussion.

forms: 形容词；名词复数 fungibles 指可互换物，本课不考名词义。
family: fungibility 可互换性。
usage_note: 常用于货币、标准化商品；同类等量单位可以替换。只说两件物品都能使用，并不能说明它们 fungible。
sentence: Standard gold bars are fungible when their weight and purity match.
translation: 重量和纯度一致的标准金条可以互相替代。
collocation:
fungible gold bars 可互换的金条（标准商品）
fungible game tokens 可互换的游戏代币（游戏计分）
context_hint: Each unit can replace another unit of the same kind and value.
scenario: 比较规格一致的标准金条，理解同类物品的互换性。
hint: Each unit can replace another unit of the same kind and value.

pronunciation.note: g 读 /dʒ/；词尾 -ible 弱读 /ɪbəl/。

morphology.text: fung-（履行，拉丁语词干）+ -ible（能够……的）→ fungible（可由同类替代履行义务的）；与 fungus 没有这种构词关系。

etymology.text: 来自新拉丁语 fungibilis，更早联系拉丁语 fungi（履行）。原来强调能用同类物品履行交付义务，后来概括为可互换。

cloze: Standard gold bars are _____ when their weight and purity match.

teaching.contrast: 常用于货币、标准化商品；同类等量单位可以替换。只说两件物品都能使用，并不能说明它们 fungible。
teaching.sentence: The game uses fungible tokens, each worth exactly one point.
