etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学英语将 immuno-“免疫”与 compromised“功能受损的”组合而成的词。immuno- 与 immune 同源，最终可追溯到拉丁语 immunis“免除义务的”，其意义后来转向免受疾病侵害。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical formation joins immuno-, meaning “immune,” to compromised in the sense of impaired functioning. Immuno- belongs to the family of immune, ultimately from Latin immunis, meaning “exempt from obligations,” a meaning later extended to protection from disease.

morphology_enriched.zh: immuno-（免疫）+ compromised（受损的，源自 compromise + -ed）→ immunocompromised，整体作为形容词使用。相关形式有较少见的 immunocompromise（免疫损害）；常见相关词族包括 immune（免疫的）、immunity（免疫力）、immunodeficiency（免疫缺陷）和 immunosuppression（免疫抑制），后两者并非该词的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Immuno- + compromised, from compromise + -ed, forms the adjective immunocompromised. The less common related form immunocompromise names immune impairment; the wider family includes immune, immunity, immunodeficiency, and immunosuppression, although the last two are not direct derivatives of immunocompromised.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: immune-impaired（免疫功能受损的）是接近的描述性表达；immunodeficient（免疫缺陷的）强调免疫系统某些成分或功能不足；immunosuppressed（免疫受抑制的）强调免疫活动受到抑制，常与药物治疗有关。immunocompromised 是涵盖多种原因的宽泛用语。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Immune-impaired is a close descriptive equivalent. Immunodeficient emphasizes a deficiency in immune components or function; immunosuppressed emphasizes suppression of immune activity, often associated with treatment. Immunocompromised is a broad term covering impairment from various causes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: immune 是防御系统；compromised 是功能打了折扣：身体防线变弱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Immune names the defense system; compromised means its effectiveness is reduced: the body's defenses are weakened.

etymology_story.en: Lanyard comes from French lanière, meaning “strap” or “thong,” with early English forms including lanyer. It developed nautical uses for securing lines, acquired a spelling influenced by yard, and later extended to badge straps and safety tethers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 lanyard 视为完整词干，不拆成 lan + yard。常用形式为复数 lanyards；主要通过复合词扩展，如 badge lanyard（证件挂绳）、safety lanyard（安全系索）、tool lanyard（工具防坠系绳）；没有常用的标准派生动词或副词。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语借入后期拉丁语 ligatura，最终源于拉丁语 ligare“捆、系”。从“用于捆绑的东西”发展出结扎线、连接音符的符号和连字等含义，核心都是“连接或束紧”。参见 [Collins 词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ligature)。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed Late Latin ligatura, ultimately from Latin ligare, meaning 'to bind'. The idea of binding developed into surgical ties, joined musical notation, and joined letters. See [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/ligature).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整词处理，不宜把历史词干当作自由构词成分。屈折形式：ligatures（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、ligatured（过去式及过去分词）、ligaturing（现在分词）；同根词族包括 ligate（结扎）、ligation（结扎；连接）、ligament（韧带）和 ligamentous（韧带的），这些并非都由 ligature 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ligature is normally treated as a whole lexical base rather than a productive root-and-suffix combination. Inflections are ligatures, ligatured, and ligaturing; the wider root family includes ligate, ligation, ligament, and ligamentous, which are not all direct derivatives of ligature.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tie（系带；捆扎物）含义最宽；suture（缝线；缝合）主要用于连接组织，ligature 则侧重扎住结构；ligate（结扎）是医学动词中比 ligature 更常见的表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tie is a broad term for something used in binding; a suture primarily joins tissue, whereas a ligature ties off a structure; ligate is the more usual medical verb for the action expressed by the verb ligature.

etymology_story.zh: oxytocin 是以 oxytocic“催产的”的词干加物质名称后缀 -in 构成的现代科学名称。其希腊语来源包含 oxys“快的”和 tokos“分娩”，名称突出了促进分娩的作用。参见 [Collins：oxytocin](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/oxytocin) 和 [Collins：oxytocic](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/oxytocic)。
etymology_story.en: Oxytocin is a modern scientific name formed from the stem of oxytocic with the substance suffix -in. Its Greek ancestry includes oxys, 'quick', and tokos, 'childbirth', highlighting its role in promoting childbirth. See [Collins: oxytocin](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/oxytocin) and [Collins: oxytocic](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/oxytocic).

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词分析：oxytoc-（催产相关词干，见 oxytocic）+ -in（物质后缀）→ oxytocin。专业词族包括 oxytocic（催产的；催产药）、oxytocinase（催产素酶，分解催产素的酶）、oxytocinergic（与催产素信号传递有关的）；oxytocin receptor（催产素受体）是复合术语，其中 oxytocic 是相关基础词，并非由 oxytocin 直接加后缀而成。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific formation: oxytoc-, the stem associated with oxytocic, + the substance suffix -in → oxytocin. The specialist family includes oxytocic, promoting childbirth or an agent that does so; oxytocinase, an enzyme that breaks down oxytocin; and oxytocinergic, relating to oxytocin signalling. Oxytocin receptor is a compound term; oxytocic is a related source word rather than a direct suffixal derivative of oxytocin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义普通名词：oxytocic（催产药）和 uterotonic（宫缩剂）都是更宽的药理类别；hormone（激素）是上位概念。oxytocin 指特定分子及其制剂，不能与这些类别名称任意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact generic synonym: oxytocic and uterotonic name broader categories of agents, while hormone is a broader biological category. Oxytocin identifies a particular molecule and its medicinal preparation, so these terms are not freely interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名称里的逻辑是“快＋分娩＋物质”：先记催产，再连到乳汁排出。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read the naming logic as 'quick + childbirth + substance': remember contractions first, then connect the hormone with milk release.

The ground-level idea underlies both the patterned garden area and the theatre's lower audience area. See [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/parterre).

morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats parterre as a complete French loanword; its regular plural is parterres. Parterred, furnished with parterres, is a rare adjective rather than a common family member; parterre garden is a compound expression. French par + terre explains the historical source, not a productive modern English prefix-and-root structure.

etymology_story.zh: 这是19世纪形成的科学词汇，由源自希腊语 seismos（震动；地震）的 seismo- 与表示记录仪器的 -graph 构成。名称直指其功能：把地面震动记录下来。
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century scientific term combines seismo-, from Greek seismos meaning shaking or earthquake, with -graph, denoting a recording instrument. Its name directly describes its function: recording ground motion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：seismo-（地震）+ -graph（记录仪器）。直接词族包括 seismography（地震记录术）、seismographic / seismographical（地震记录的）、seismographically（通过地震记录方法）；相关构词包括 seismogram（地震记录图）、seismometer（地震计）、seismometry（地震测量）和 seismology（地震学）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: seismo- (earthquake) + -graph (recording instrument). The direct family includes seismography, seismographic, seismographical, and seismographically; related formations include seismogram (the recorded trace), seismometer (the measuring instrument), seismometry, and seismology.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关表达：seismometer（地震计）侧重感测和测量震动，seismograph 侧重包含记录功能的仪器或系统，但两者在实际使用中常有重叠；seismic recorder（地震记录器）是强调记录功能的描述性名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Near equivalents are seismometer and seismic recorder. Seismometer emphasizes sensing and measuring motion, whereas seismograph emphasizes the recording instrument or system, although usage often overlaps; seismic recorder is a descriptive term emphasizing recording.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: seismo- 是地震，-graph 是记录：把地面震动“画”下来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Seismo- means earthquake and -graph means recorder: it draws a record of the shaking.

meaning: 系统论述某领域的大全；总结性论著

etymology_story.zh: 借自拉丁语 summa（总数；总和），它原是 summus（最高的）的阴性形式。在中世纪拉丁语中，summa 成为系统汇总某一领域知识的论著名称，尤其常见于神学和哲学。
etymology_story.en: Summa comes from Latin summa, meaning a total or sum, originally the feminine form of summus, meaning highest. In medieval Latin it became a name for a systematic compendium of knowledge, especially in theology and philosophy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再按常用词缀拆分的借词：summa。复数为 summae 或 summas；没有常用的直接派生词。sum（总和）、summary（总结）和 summation（总计；总结）与它在历史上同源，但不是由英语 summa 派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, summa is an unanalyzed loanword. Its plurals are summae and summas, and it has no common direct derivatives. Sum, summary, and summation are historically related words, rather than derivatives of the English noun summa.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: compendium（知识汇编）强调以较紧凑的形式汇集信息；treatise（专论）强调对某一主题作严谨、深入的论述；synthesis（综合论述）强调把不同思想整合成整体。summa 则突出全面、系统且具有总结性的知识总汇。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A compendium collects information in a relatively compact form; a treatise develops a subject in depth; a synthesis integrates different ideas into a whole. A summa particularly suggests a comprehensive, systematic culmination of knowledge.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 sum“总和”同源：把一门学问加总，成为一部大全。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with its relative sum: a summa adds a whole field of knowledge together.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语经法语借入，源自中世纪拉丁语 suppositorium，最终可追溯至拉丁语 supponere（放在下面），由 sub-（在下面）和 ponere（放置）构成。它的医学含义由这种药物的置入方式发展而来。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 suppository 作为完整的医学名词学习；历史构形可分析为 supposit-（放在下面）+ -ory（构成相关事物名称的词尾）。复数为 suppositories，没有常用的直接派生词；不能按现代 suppose（猜想）+ 词尾来理解。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats suppository as a complete medical noun; historically, it contains supposit- (placed underneath) and the noun-forming ending -ory. synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common single-word synonym covering every use. Rectal suppository specifies the insertion site; pessary can mean a vaginal suppository in some varieties of English, but can also mean a support device; an enema is usually liquid and is a related dosage form, not a synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自俄语 тайга（taiga），该俄语词通常被认为来自突厥语。它原用于描述西伯利亚的森林地带，后来在英语中扩展为横跨欧亚大陆和北美洲的北方森林生态带名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed taiga from Russian тайга, a word generally traced to Turkic. Originally associated with Siberian forest country, it came to name the northern forest biome extending across Eurasia and North America.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：taiga 是不可再拆分的借词，没有常用的词缀派生词。通常作不可数名词表示生态带，特指多个区域或类型时也可用 taigas；taiga forest（泰加林）和 taiga biome（泰加林生物群系）是名词修饰名词的组合，不构成独立的形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: taiga is an unanalyzed loanword with no common affixal derivatives. It is usually uncountable when naming the biome, though taigas can refer to distinct regions or types; taiga forest and taiga biome use the noun attributively and do not establish a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: boreal forest（北方森林）是最接近的常用对应表达；northern coniferous forest（北方针叶林）强调地理位置与优势树种；subarctic forest（亚寒带森林）强调气候区域，其范围与 taiga 并不总是完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Boreal forest is the closest common equivalent; northern coniferous forest emphasizes location and dominant tree types; subarctic forest emphasizes the climatic zone and does not always have exactly the same scope as taiga.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture one landscape: a vast, cold belt of conifers south of the tundra.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 tannic 与法语 tannique 相对应，源自 tannin（单宁），其名称又与 tan（鞣革；鞣革用树皮）相关。这个化学形容词后来也用于品评茶和葡萄酒，描述单宁造成的收敛涩感。
etymology_story.en: English tannic corresponds to French tannique and derives from tannin, whose name is connected with tan, referring to tanning and the bark used in it. The chemical adjective also came to describe the astringency produced by tannins in tea and wine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 tann-（见 tannin，单宁）+ -ic（……的）；不能机械地把 tannin 与 -ic 直接拼接。相关词族包括 tannin（单宁）、tannins（各类单宁）、tannate（鞣酸盐或酯）和 tannase（单宁酶）；更广的历史相关词包括 tan（鞣制）、tanning（鞣制）、tanner（鞣革工）和 tannery（制革厂）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation can be analyzed as tann- (the base associated with tannin) + -ic (relating to), rather than simply attaching -ic to the unchanged word tannin. Related vocabulary includes tannin, tannins, tannate, and tannase; the wider historical family includes tan, tanning, tanner, and tannery.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: astringent（收敛性的；涩的）强调口腔发紧、发干的感觉，不限定由单宁造成；tannin-rich（富含单宁的）直接说明成分含量；bitter（苦的）描述苦味，常与 tannic 并存，但苦味和涩感是不同感觉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Astringent emphasizes a drying, puckering sensation without specifying tannins as its cause; tannin-rich directly describes composition. Bitter describes bitterness, which can accompany tannic astringency but is a different sensation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 单宁既能鞣皮，也能让口腔发紧：tannic 就是“单宁相关、涩感明显”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tannins tan hides and make your mouth feel dry: tannic connects the substance with its astringent effect.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 travertin 和意大利语 travertino 传入英语，最终源于拉丁语 lapis Tiburtinus，意为“提布尔的石头”。提布尔即今天罗马附近的蒂沃利，当地出产的这种石材使地名逐渐成为石材名称。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French travertin and Italian travertino, ultimately from Latin lapis Tiburtinus, meaning 'stone of Tibur.' Tibur, now Tivoli near Rome, supplied this building stone, so its place-name became the name of the material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 travertine 是整体借入的名词，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀。表示石材时通常不可数；travertines 可用于不同种类或不同产地的石灰华。常见组合有 travertine tile（洞石瓷砖）和 travertine-like（类似石灰华的）；没有常用的独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, travertine is a borrowed noun rather than a productive combination of English roots and affixes. It is normally uncountable as a material; travertines can refer to different varieties or occurrences. Common combinations include travertine tile and travertine-like; there is no established family of common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: limestone（石灰岩）是上位词，范围比 travertine 广；tufa（钙华）与其含义有重叠，但通常指较疏松、多孔的淡水碳酸钙沉积物；calcareous sinter（钙质泉华）强调由水沉积形成的碳酸钙结壳。这些名称的使用范围有时重叠，并非处处可以互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Limestone is the broader rock category; tufa overlaps with travertine but usually denotes softer, more porous freshwater calcium-carbonate deposits; calcareous sinter emphasizes calcium-carbonate crusts deposited by water. These terms overlap in use but are not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“蒂沃利的石头”记住石材名称，再联想泉水层层沉积形成的白色阶地。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember 'stone from Tivoli,' then picture spring water building pale stone terraces layer by layer.

etymology_story.en: Uppercut is an English boxing compound formed from upper and cut, recorded in the nineteenth century. Cut uses an older sense meaning a stroke or blow, and the compound describes the fist's upward movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: upper（上方的）+ cut（击打）→ uppercut；名词通过零派生兼作动词。常用形式：uppercuts（名词复数、动词第三人称单数）、uppercutting（现在分词）；过去式和过去分词通常仍为 uppercut。
morphology_enriched.en: Upper + cut, with cut meaning a blow, forms uppercut; the noun also functions as a verb through conversion. Common forms are uppercuts for the plural noun and third-person singular verb, uppercutting for the present participle, and usually uppercut for both the past tense and past participle.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: upward punch（向上击出的拳）是最接近的释义性表达；hook（钩拳）通常沿侧向弧线击出；jab（刺拳）是快速的直拳。后两者是相关拳法，不能作为 uppercut 的精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Upward punch is the closest explanatory equivalent; a hook usually follows a sideways curved path; a jab is a quick straight punch. Hook and jab name related punches rather than exact synonyms of uppercut.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Upper gives the upward direction, and cut supplies the blow: picture a fist rising toward the chin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中，vaquero 是整体借词，复数为 vaqueros。其西班牙语内部构成为 vaca（牛）去掉词尾 -a，再加 -ero（从业者）；c 在 e 前改写为 qu，以保留 /k/ 音。相关形式有 vaquera（女性牧牛人）和 buckaroo（同源借词）；两者均不是英语后缀派生词。

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cowboy is the closest and most widely used equivalent; cowhand emphasizes the work of tending cattle; buckaroo has a regional western US flavor. Vaquero particularly evokes the cattle-handling and riding traditions of Spanish-speaking cultures.

etymology_story.zh: adipose 源于拉丁语 adiposus，意为“多脂肪的”，由 adeps“脂肪”的词干 adip- 与表示“富含”的后缀 -osus 构成。英语中它主要用于解剖学和生物学，名词用法也可视为 adipose tissue 的省略。
etymology_story.en: Adipose comes from Latin adiposus, meaning 'fatty,' formed from adip-, the stem of adeps 'fat,' and -osus 'full of.' In English it is chiefly anatomical and biological, and its noun use can also be understood as a shortening of adipose tissue.

morphology_enriched.zh: adip-（脂肪）+ -ose（具有……性质的、富含……的）→ adipose；名词用法通过词类转换或省略 tissue 形成。常用相关词包括 adiposity（脂肪含量；肥胖程度）、adipocyte（脂肪细胞）、adipogenesis（脂肪细胞形成）和 adipogenic（促进脂肪细胞形成的）；后几项共享 adip-，并非都直接由 adipose 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Adip- 'fat' + -ose 'having the nature of or full of' forms adipose; the noun arises through conversion or omission of tissue. Common related terms include adiposity, the amount or degree of body fat; adipocyte, a fat cell; adipogenesis, fat-cell formation; and adipogenic, promoting fat-cell formation. These terms share adip-, but are not all direct derivatives of adipose.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fatty（含脂肪的）适用范围更广，也可描述食物；fat（脂肪）作名词时更日常，可指身体脂肪或脂肪物质；adipose tissue（脂肪组织）是 adipose 名词用法更明确的完整表达。adipose 强调生物体内的脂肪或储脂组织。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fatty is broader and can also describe food; fat is the everyday noun for body fat or fatty material; adipose tissue is the more explicit equivalent of the noun adipose. Adipose chiefly refers to fat or fat-storing tissue in an organism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: adip- 抓住“脂肪”，-ose 表示“富含”：富含脂肪的组织就是 adipose tissue。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor adip- to fat and -ose to 'full of': adipose tissue is tissue filled with fat-storing cells.

etymology_story.zh: alfresco 借自意大利语短语 al fresco，字面意为“在清凉处”，其中 al 是 a 与定冠词 il 的合并形式。英语将其固定用于“在户外”的意思，尤其常见于露天用餐的语境。
etymology_story.en: Alfresco comes from the Italian phrase al fresco, literally 'in the cool,' with al combining a and the definite article il. English established the meaning 'in the open air,' particularly in descriptions of outdoor dining.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中 alfresco 是整体使用的借词，可兼作副词和形容词；al fresco 是常见的分写形式。在来源语言中可分析为 al（a + il，表示“在……处”）+ fresco（清凉）。该词没有常用的屈折变化或独立派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: English treats alfresco as a borrowed unit used as both an adverb and an adjective; al fresco is a common two-word spelling. In Italian it consists of al, from a + il, meaning 'in the,' and fresco, referring to coolness. It has no usual inflected forms or established family of common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: outdoors（在户外）是适用范围最广的副词；outdoor（户外的）是普通形容词；open-air（露天的）常强调场所没有屋顶。alfresco 尤其常修饰用餐，容易让人联想到轻松舒适的户外环境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Outdoors is the broad everyday adverb; outdoor is the general adjective; open-air often emphasizes a setting without a roof. Alfresco is especially associated with meals and often suggests a pleasant, relaxed outdoor setting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“到清凉处”联想到把餐桌搬到室外：alfresco 就是露天吃、户外享用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move 'into the cool' by taking the table outside: alfresco brings the meal into the open air.

etymology_story.zh: 由 bipedal（双足的）加 -ism 构成；bipedal 最终源于拉丁语 bipes（双足的），其中 bi- 表示“二”，ped- 表示“脚”。这个词把“双足的”这一特征转化为一种运动方式，常用于讨论人类演化。
etymology_story.en: Bipedalism combines bipedal with -ism; bipedal ultimately derives from Latin bipes, meaning 'two-footed,' with bi- meaning 'two' and ped- meaning 'foot.' The noun names a mode of locomotion and is especially associated with human evolution.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bipedal（双足的）+ -ism（状态或行为方式）→ bipedalism。主要词族：biped（两足动物）、bipedal（双足的）、bipedally（以双足方式）、bipedality（双足性）；历史词根为 bi-（二）和 ped-（脚）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bipedal + -ism, denoting a condition or mode of behavior. The principal word family includes biped, bipedal, bipedally, bipedality, and bipedalism; its historical elements are bi- 'two' and ped- 'foot.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bipedality（双足性）侧重具有双足运动这一特征；bipedal locomotion（双足运动）明确指运动方式，可包括行走和奔跑；upright walking（直立行走）强调姿态及行走行为，范围比 bipedalism 窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bipedality emphasizes the condition or characteristic; bipedal locomotion explicitly describes movement, including walking and running; upright walking emphasizes posture and walking specifically, so it is narrower than bipedalism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bi-＝二，ped-＝脚：把“两只脚移动”看成一种运动方式，就是 bipedalism。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bi- means two and ped- means foot: bipedalism names the two-footed way of moving.

etymology_story.en: The word is based on the botanical genus name Bromelia, which honors the Swedish botanist Olof Bromelius, whose first name is also written Olaf. In English, bromeliad denotes a member of the entire pineapple family, not just the genus Bromelia.

morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Bromeli-, from Bromelia, + -ad, a noun suffix identifying a member of a group. The plural is bromeliads; related taxonomic names are Bromelia and Bromeliaceae, and the uncommon adjective bromeliaceous means 'belonging to the pineapple family.'

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bromeliaceous plant is a more technical equivalent, while pineapple-family plant is a plain-language paraphrase. Pineapple names one particular member of the family and cannot replace bromeliad generally.

etymology_story.en: Catechetical derives through catechetic from ecclesiastical Latin catecheticus and related Greek words concerned with oral instruction. Closely associated with teaching Christian doctrine, it also came to describe question-and-answer instruction more generally.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：catechetic（教理教学的）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ catechetical；catechetical + -ly → catechetically（以教理教学或问答教学方式）。主要相关词族：catechesis（教理讲授）、catechism（教理问答书；问答式纲要）、catechist（教理教师）、catechize／catechise（讲授教理；逐项盘问）、catechetic（教理教学的）。这些词共享历史词干，但并非都由 catechetical 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: catechetic + the adjective suffix -al → catechetical; adding -ly gives catechetically. The principal related family includes catechesis, catechism, catechist, catechize or catechise, and catechetic. These share a historical stem rather than all being direct derivatives of catechetical.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Question-and-answer describes the format without implying religion; doctrinal emphasizes the beliefs being taught; instructional is broader and specifies neither religious content nor a particular teaching method.

etymology_story.zh: commutate 由 commutation 逆构而来，后者最终源于拉丁语 commutare（改变、交换），包含 com- 和 mutare（改变）。其电学含义将一般的“改变、交换”具体化为电流方向或通路的切换。
etymology_story.en: Commutate was back-formed from commutation, which ultimately comes from Latin commutare, 'to change or exchange,' containing com- and mutare, 'to change.' Its electrical use specializes this idea as switching the direction or path of a current.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系：commutation（换向）→ 逆构动词 commutate；commutat- + -or → commutator（换向器）。主要词族和形式：commutates、commutated、commutating、commutation、commutator；commute（通勤；交换；减刑）与之历史同源，commutative（可交换的）和 commutativity（交换性）主要用于数学语境。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern relationship: commutation → the back-formed verb commutate; commutat- + -or → commutator. Principal family members and forms include commutates, commutated, commutating, commutation, and commutator. Commute is historically related, while commutative and commutativity occur chiefly in mathematics.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: switch（切换）含义最广，可指改变开关状态或电路通路；reverse（反转）只强调方向相反；rectify（整流）特指把交流变为直流，某些换向过程可以实现整流，但不等同于所有 commutation。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Switch broadly covers changes in circuit state or current path; reverse specifically emphasizes a change to the opposite direction; rectify means converting alternating current into direct current, which some commutation processes accomplish but which is not equivalent to all commutation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 mut- 的“改变”：在电路里，改变的是电流方向或流经的通路。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor mut- to change: in a circuit, commutating changes the current's direction or route.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 coulis；它与古法语表示“过滤”的动词有关，最终可追溯到拉丁语 colare（过滤）和 colum（滤器）。其历史含义涉及滤过的浓汤或汁液，现代通常指细滑的果蔬酱汁。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed coulis from French; the word is related to an Old French verb meaning 'to strain' and ultimately to Latin colare, 'to strain,' and colum, 'a sieve.' Earlier uses involved strained broths or juices, while modern use usually refers to smooth fruit or vegetable sauces.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 coulis 是整体借入的单纯词，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀；词尾 s 属于原词拼写，并非英语复数词尾。单复数均可写作 coulis，没有常用的固定派生词；raspberry coulis（覆盆子酱汁）等属于修饰词加名词的组合。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, coulis is an unanalyzed loanword rather than a combination of English roots and affixes; its final s belongs to the borrowed spelling. Both singular and plural can be written coulis, and there are no established common derivatives; raspberry coulis and similar expressions are modifier-plus-noun combinations.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: purée（果蔬泥）强调打碎后的泥状食物，不一定经过滤或用作酱汁；sauce（酱汁）是范围更广的上位词；compote（糖煮水果）通常保留果块，与 coulis 的细滑质地不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Purée emphasizes food reduced to a soft mass and need not be strained or served as a sauce; sauce is the broader category; compote usually contains pieces of cooked fruit, unlike the smooth texture of a coulis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住词源中的“过滤”：果蔬打泥再滤细，成为能淋在食物上的 coulis。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical idea of straining: purée fruit or vegetables, strain them smooth, and spoon on the coulis.

etymology_story.zh: crankcase 由 crank（曲柄）与 case（外壳）复合而成，是按照机械部件的结构和用途命名的词。这里的 crank 指向曲柄机构，全词指包围并保护曲轴的壳体。
etymology_story.en: Crankcase combines crank with case, naming a mechanical component by its structure and function. Crank refers to the crank mechanism, and the compound denotes the housing surrounding and protecting the crankshaft.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：crank（曲柄）+ case（外壳）→ crankcase（曲轴箱）；复数为 crankcases。相关复合词有 crankshaft（曲轴）、crankpin（曲柄销）和 crankcase breather（曲轴箱通气装置）；本词没有常用的派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: crank + case → crankcase; plural: crankcases. Related compounds include crankshaft, crankpin, and crankcase breather; crankcase has no commonly used derived verb or adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无严格通用的单词近义词。相关词 engine block（发动机缸体）指发动机的主要结构体，可能与曲轴箱上部一体成形；sump（油底壳，英式用语）和 oil pan（油底壳，主要用于美式英语）通常指位于下方的储油部分，均不等于完整的曲轴箱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact general single-word synonym. Engine block denotes the engine's main structural body and may incorporate the upper crankcase; sump, in British usage, and oil pan, chiefly in American usage, usually denote the lower oil reservoir rather than the complete crankcase.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: crank 是曲柄，case 是外壳：曲轴住在 crankcase 里。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Crank + case: the crankshaft lives inside its protective case.

senses.english_definition: If someone douches, they wash inside a body cavity, especially the vagina, with a stream of liquid.

etymology_story.zh: douche 借自法语 douche（淋浴、冲洗），法语词来自意大利语 doccia（水管、淋水装置）。英语中该词形成了医疗灌洗的名词和动词用法；粗俗的人身辱称则与 douchebag 的贬义用法有关。
etymology_story.en: Douche was borrowed from French douche, meaning 'shower' or 'washing,' from Italian doccia, a water conduit or shower. In English it developed medical noun and verb uses for irrigation; its vulgar use for a person is associated with the insulting use of douchebag.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：douche 是完整借入的词基，可兼作名词和动词。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 douches，过去式和过去分词为 douched，现在分词为 douching；douche + bag → douchebag（灌洗袋；粗俗用语：混蛋），另有非正式形容词 douchey／douchy（令人讨厌的、混蛋似的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: douche is a borrowed base used as both a noun and a verb. Its noun plural and third-person singular verb form are douches, its past tense and past participle are douched, and its present participle is douching; douche + bag forms douchebag, literally an irrigation bag and figuratively a vulgar insult, while informal douchey or douchy means obnoxious.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: irrigation（灌洗、冲洗）是范围更广、语体较正式的医疗用词；lavage（灌洗）通常指医疗程序中的冲洗；jerk（讨厌鬼、混蛋）只对应辱称义，通常比 douche 粗俗程度低。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Irrigation is a broader, more formal medical term for washing with fluid; lavage usually denotes washing performed as a medical procedure; jerk matches only the insulting sense and is generally less vulgar than douche.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a stream of liquid washing something: the word can name the washing, its equipment, or the action; remember the vulgar insult separately.

etymology_story.zh: ductal 由英语 duct（导管）加形容词后缀 -al 构成。duct 源自拉丁语 ductus（引导、输送；通道），与 ducere（引导）有关，因此保留了“引导液体流动的通道”这一概念。
etymology_story.en: Ductal was formed from English duct and the adjective suffix -al. Duct comes from Latin ductus, referring to leading, conveying, or a channel, and is related to ducere, 'to lead,' preserving the idea of a passage that directs a flow.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：duct（导管）+ -al（与……有关的）→ ductal。相关词族包括 ducts（导管，复数）、ductule（小导管）、ductular（小导管的）；加前缀可形成 intraductal（导管内的）、periductal（导管周围的）和 interductal（导管之间的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: duct + -al, 'relating to,' → ductal. The related family includes ducts, ductule, meaning a small duct, and ductular, meaning relating to small ducts; prefixed forms include intraductal, within a duct, periductal, around a duct, and interductal, between ducts.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ductular（小导管的）特别指较小的导管；tubular（管状的）侧重形状或管状结构，不一定涉及导管；canalicular（小管的）用于特定的微小通道。三者都是相关术语，不能在所有语境中替代 ductal。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ductular specifically concerns small ducts; tubular describes a tube shape or tubular structure without necessarily referring to a duct; canalicular concerns particular small channels. These are related terms rather than universally interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: duct 是输送通道，-al 表示“……的”：ductal 就是“导管的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A duct carries a flow; -al means 'relating to': ductal means 'relating to a duct.'

senses.meaning_zh: 弹性蛋白；使组织具有伸展和回弹能力的结构蛋白
senses.meaning_en: a structural protein that allows tissues to stretch and spring back

senses.sentence_zh: 血液流经动脉时，弹性蛋白帮助动脉壁伸展并回弹。

etymology_story.zh: elastin 是以 elastic（有弹性的）为基础、配合科学物质名后缀 -in 形成的术语。它按照这种蛋白质的主要性质命名：使结缔组织能够伸展后恢复形状。
etymology_story.en: Elastin is a scientific formation based on elastic with the substance-name suffix -in. Its name reflects the protein's characteristic role in allowing connective tissues to stretch and recover their shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：elast-（与弹性有关的词干）+ -in（用于某些蛋白质及其他物质名称的后缀）→ elastin，通常为不可数名词。相关词有 elastic（有弹性的）、elastically（有弹性地）和 elasticity（弹性）；专门术语包括 tropoelastin（原弹性蛋白，可溶性前体）、elastase（弹性蛋白酶，能分解弹性蛋白的酶）和 elastogenesis（弹性纤维的形成）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: elast-, a stem associated with elasticity, + -in, a suffix used in some protein and other substance names, → elastin, normally an uncountable noun. Related words include elastic, elastically, and elasticity; specialist terms include tropoelastin, its soluble precursor, elastase, an enzyme that breaks down elastin, and elastogenesis, the formation of elastic fibers.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无严格的常用近义词。相关词 collagen（胶原蛋白）主要提供抗拉强度和结构支撑；keratin（角蛋白）主要构成毛发、指甲等坚韧结构；elastic fiber（弹性纤维）是以弹性蛋白为主要成分的组织结构，并不等于单独的弹性蛋白。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact common synonym. Collagen mainly provides tensile strength and structural support; keratin forms tough structures such as hair and nails; an elastic fiber is a tissue structure containing elastin as a major component, rather than the protein alone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: elastic（有弹性的）→ elastin（弹性蛋白）：想象组织里的回弹橡皮筋。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect elastic with elastin: picture the protein as the springy rubber band in a tissue.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 Elysius（极乐世界的），最终可追溯至希腊语 Ēlysion，即神话中的极乐原野。英语由这一幸福来世的意象，引申出“天堂般美好安宁的”之义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin Elysius, ultimately from Greek Ēlysion, the mythical Elysian Fields. The image of a blessed afterlife developed into the broader English meaning of heavenly beauty and happiness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 Elysi-（与 Elysium“极乐世界”对应的词干）+ -an（……的）；词干发生调整，不能机械地将完整的 Elysium 与 -an 相加。核心词族为 Elysium（极乐世界）和 Elysian/elysian（极乐世界的；天堂般的），没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is Elysi-, the stem corresponding to Elysium, + -an, meaning 'relating to'; the stem changes rather than simply retaining the whole word Elysium. The core family is Elysium and Elysian/elysian, with no common verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heavenly（天堂般的）适用范围更广，也可口语化地表示“美妙极了”；idyllic（田园诗般的）侧重宁静、纯朴的理想生活或景色；paradisiacal（乐园般的）强调如同天堂的环境。elysian 更具文学色彩，并带有古典神话联想。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heavenly is broader and can informally mean extremely pleasant; idyllic emphasizes peaceful, simple perfection; paradisiacal describes conditions resembling paradise. Elysian is especially literary and carries an association with classical mythology.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Elysium is a blessed paradise: elysian means beautiful or peaceful enough to belong there.

etymology_story.zh: fentanyl 是二十世纪药物命名中创造的通用药名，随后作为这种合成阿片类药物的名称进入英语。它不是由普通英语词根和词缀透明构成的词，不宜将与化学名称的相似之处当作已经确定的完整词源。
etymology_story.en: Fentanyl was coined as a generic pharmaceutical name in the twentieth century and entered English as the name of this synthetic opioid. It is not transparently formed from ordinary English roots and affixes, so similarities to chemical terms should not be treated as a fully established derivation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 fentanyl 作为整体药名处理，通常为不可数名词；fentanyl + -like → fentanyl-like（类似芬太尼的）。常见复合表达有 fentanyl-based（以芬太尼为基础的）和 fentanyl-containing（含芬太尼的）；alfentanil（阿芬太尼）、sufentanil（舒芬太尼）、remifentanil（瑞芬太尼）是相关药名，不是通过普通英语词缀规则形成的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, fentanyl is treated as a whole drug name and is normally uncountable; fentanyl + -like forms fentanyl-like. Common compounds include fentanyl-based and fentanyl-containing; alfentanil, sufentanil, and remifentanil are related drug names rather than derivatives formed by ordinary English affixation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: opioid（阿片类药物）是包含芬太尼在内的上位词；analgesic（镇痛药）按缓解疼痛的作用分类，范围更广；narcotic（麻醉性药物、毒品）含义随医学、法律及日常语境变化。三者都不是 fentanyl 的精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Opioid names the broader drug class containing fentanyl; analgesic describes any pain-relieving medicine; narcotic has meanings that vary across medical, legal, and everyday contexts. None is an exact synonym for fentanyl.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经意第绪语借入 goy，源头是希伯来语 gōy，原义为“民族、国家”。该词后来在犹太人的语言使用中专指非犹太民族或其中的个人，进入英语后也保留了这一文化语境。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed goy through Yiddish from Hebrew gōy, originally meaning 'nation' or 'people.' In Jewish usage it came to refer specifically to non-Jewish peoples or individuals, a cultural association retained in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: goy 是借入的单纯词，现代英语中不再拆分；复数有 goyim（沿用希伯来语复数形式）和 goys（英语规则复数）。goy + -ish → goyish（非犹太人的；具有非犹太人特点的）；另见借自意第绪语的形容词变体 goyische，语体与褒贬色彩依语境而定。
morphology_enriched.en: Goy is a borrowed simple word with no productive internal division in English; its plurals are goyim, retaining the Hebrew plural, and the regular English goys. Goy + -ish forms goyish; the Yiddish-derived adjective variant goyische also occurs, with register and tone depending on context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: non-Jew（非犹太人）最直接、通常也最中性；gentile（非犹太人）较正式，常见于宗教或历史语境。goy 更具有犹太文化内部口语色彩，可能亲昵、诙谐，也可能带轻蔑意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Non-Jew is explicit and usually neutral; gentile is more formal and common in religious or historical contexts. Goy has a stronger association with informal Jewish speech and may be affectionate, humorous, or contemptuous.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“民族”到“其他民族的人”：记住 goy 指犹太文化语境中的非犹太人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'a people' becoming 'someone from another people': in Jewish usage, a goy is a non-Jew.

senses.meaning_en: A painting technique using shades of gray to create form and shading.
senses.english_definition: Grisaille is a way of painting in shades of gray, often to make the subject look like sculpture or to prepare a layer beneath colored paint.

senses.meaning_zh: 用灰色单色画法完成的画作或装饰画
senses.meaning_en: A painting or decorative image executed in shades of gray.
senses.english_definition: A grisaille is a picture painted in shades of gray rather than in a range of colors.
senses.collocation_en: a grisaille painting; a grisaille panel
senses.collocation_zh: 一幅灰色单色画；一块灰色单色画板

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 grisaille，其基础是 gris，意为“灰色”。这个名称由灰色色调转指使用这些色调的绘画技法，也指以这种技法完成的作品。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed grisaille from French, where it is based on gris, meaning 'gray.' The name came to denote both painting in gray tones and a work produced using that technique.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中，grisaille 通常作为完整的法语借词处理；其法语内部结构为 gris（灰色）+ -aille（名词后缀），不是英语中的能产构词公式。表示技法时通常不可数，表示作品时可数，复数为 grisailles；相关固定表达有 en grisaille（以灰色单色画法），无常用英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats grisaille as a whole French loanword; its French structure is gris, 'gray,' + the noun suffix -aille, rather than a productive English formation. It is normally uncountable for the technique and countable for an artwork, with plural grisailles; the related phrase en grisaille means 'in gray monochrome,' and there is no common English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: monochrome（单色画、单色表现）可使用任何一种色相；gray monochrome（灰色单色画）与 grisaille 含义接近，但不一定强调传统绘画技法；underpainting（底画）指绘画的底层，可采用灰色或其他颜色。grisaille 特指灰色调绘画或其技法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monochrome can use any single hue; gray monochrome closely describes grisaille without necessarily suggesting a traditional painting technique; underpainting refers to a preliminary paint layer, which may use gray or other colors. Grisaille specifically identifies painting in gray tones.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gris＝灰色：只靠灰的深浅，也能画出立体感。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Gris means gray: shades of gray alone can create the illusion of three-dimensional form.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自阿拉伯语 ḥadīth，意为“话语、谈话、报告”，其所属词根与“发生、成为新的”等概念相关。在伊斯兰教语境中，它专指关于先知穆罕默德言行及默许的传述，也用于统称这些传述。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Arabic ḥadīth, meaning 'speech,' 'conversation,' or 'report,' from a root associated with happening or becoming new. In Islamic usage it denotes reports of the Prophet Muhammad's words, actions, and tacit approval, both individually and collectively.

morphology_enriched.zh: hadith 在现代英语中是不可继续拆分的借词；可数复数为 hadiths，也见沿用阿拉伯语复数的 ahadith，统称时通常不可数。hadith + -ic → hadithic（圣训的，专业用语）；常见复合表达有 hadith studies（圣训研究）、hadith scholar（圣训学者），阿拉伯语词根不能当作英语前后缀拆解。
morphology_enriched.en: Hadith is an unanalyzed loanword in modern English; countable plurals include hadiths and the Arabic plural ahadith, while collective use is normally uncountable. Hadith + -ic forms the specialist adjective hadithic; common compounds include hadith studies and hadith scholar, and the Arabic root should not be presented as English affixes.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: report（传述、报告）是描述单则圣训的宽泛词；tradition（传承、传述）在伊斯兰教研究中可指圣训，但日常含义更广；Sunnah（圣行）指先知的规范性榜样与实践，圣训是认识圣行的重要文献依据，二者不完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Report is a broad description of an individual hadith; tradition can mean a hadith in Islamic scholarship but has wider everyday meanings; Sunnah refers to the Prophet's normative example and practice, for which hadith provides important documentary evidence, rather than being an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“一则传下来的话语或报告”记住 hadith：圣训是关于先知言行的传述。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'a transmitted report': a hadith preserves an account of the Prophet's words or conduct.

etymology_story.zh: hydroplane 由表示“水”的希腊语来源构词成分 hydro- 与 plane 结合而成，早期用于描述在水面滑行的艇，后来也用于水上飞机。车辆“发生水滑”的动词义延续了在水层上滑行的意象。
etymology_story.en: Hydroplane combines hydro-, a combining form of Greek origin meaning 'water,' with plane; early uses concerned boats that skimmed over water, and the word was later also applied to seaplanes. The vehicle-related verb extends the image of gliding over a layer of water.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hydro-（水）+ plane（与平面及滑行有关）。常用词形及派生：hydroplanes（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、hydroplaned（过去式及过去分词）、hydroplaning（现在分词；也可作名词，表示水滑现象）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hydro- ('water') + plane, associated with a flat surface and gliding. Common family forms are hydroplanes, hydroplaned, and hydroplaning; hydroplaning also functions as a noun for the loss of tire contact on a wet road.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: seaplane 是“水上飞机”的常用名称；aquaplane 与车辆发生水滑的动词义基本相同，在英式英语中更常见；skid 泛指打滑，不限定由水膜造成。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Seaplane is the usual term for the aircraft. Aquaplane means essentially the same as the vehicle-related verb and is more usual in British English. Skid describes sliding more generally, without specifying a layer of water as the cause.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“水上滑行”：艇在水面滑，飞机在水面起降，轮胎在水膜上滑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to gliding on water: a boat skims, an aircraft lands, and a tire slides on a water film.

etymology_story.zh: lobotomy 是医学构词，由表示“脑叶”的 lobo- 与表示“切开”的 -tomy 组成，两者最终都源于希腊语。该名称描述切断脑叶相关连接的手术，并不表示把整个脑叶切除。
etymology_story.en: Lobotomy is a medical formation combining lobo-, meaning 'lobe,' with -tomy, meaning 'cutting'; both elements ultimately come from Greek. The name refers to cutting connections associated with a brain lobe, rather than removing the entire lobe.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：lob-（叶）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -tomy（切开术）。词族包括 lobotomies（复数）、lobotomize／lobotomise（施行脑叶切断术）、lobotomized／lobotomised（过去式、过去分词及分词形容词）、lobotomizing／lobotomising（现在分词）、lobotomization／lobotomisation（施行脑叶切断术）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: lob- ('lobe') + linking -o- + -tomy ('surgical cutting'). The family includes lobotomies, lobotomize or lobotomise, lobotomized or lobotomised, lobotomizing or lobotomising, and lobotomization or lobotomisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: leucotomy（亦拼 leukotomy，白质切断术）强调切断脑白质，常与 lobotomy 指同类手术；prefrontal lobotomy 专指前额叶相关手术；lobectomy 则是脑叶或其他器官叶的切除术，不能与 lobotomy 混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Leucotomy, also spelled leukotomy, emphasizes cutting white matter and often refers to the same kind of operation. Prefrontal lobotomy specifies the frontal region involved. Lobectomy means removal of a lobe and is not interchangeable with lobotomy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lobe 是“叶”，-tomy 是“切开”：切断脑叶连接，不是切除整个脑叶。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'lobe + cutting': cutting a lobe's connections, rather than removing the lobe.

etymology_story.zh: macaroon 借自法语 macaron，后者来自意大利语方言中的 maccarone 或 macarone，与 macaroni 有历史联系。这个名称逐渐用于杏仁蛋白甜饼，而现代英语中的 macaroon 也常指椰丝蛋白甜饼。
etymology_story.en: Macaroon came through French macaron from Italian dialect forms such as maccarone or macarone, historically related to macaroni. The name became associated with almond cookies, while modern English also commonly uses macaroon for the coconut variety.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 macaroon 是不可再作实用拆分的借入词；复数为 macaroons。常见组合有 almond macaroon（杏仁蛋白小甜饼）和 coconut macaroon（椰丝蛋白小甜饼）；没有常用的同根派生动词或形容词，macaron 是相关借词而非其英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, macaroon is a borrowed word without a useful productive internal breakdown; its plural is macaroons. Common combinations include almond macaroon and coconut macaroon. It has no common derived verb or adjective; macaron is a related borrowing, not an English derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cookie 是美式英语中范围更广的“甜饼”；almond biscuit 可泛指杏仁饼，不一定采用蛋白甜饼的配方；macaron 通常指两片杏仁蛋白饼夹馅的法式马卡龙，现代英语中一般与 macaroon 区分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cookie is the broader American term. Almond biscuit can describe various almond cookies without specifying a macaroon recipe. Macaron usually denotes a French sandwich confection with almond shells and a filling, and modern English generally distinguishes it from macaroon.

etymology_story.zh: macrocosm 经法语及中世纪拉丁语传入英语，其构词成分最终来自希腊语 makros（大）和 kosmos（秩序、世界）。它最初把整个宇宙与作为“小宇宙”的人相对照，后来也泛指任何包含较小体系的整体世界。
etymology_story.en: Macrocosm reached English through French and medieval Latin, with elements ultimately derived from Greek makros ('large') and kosmos ('order' or 'world'). It contrasted the whole universe with the human being as a microcosm, later extending to other large systems containing smaller ones.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：macro-（大、宏观）+ -cosm（世界、宇宙，黏着词根）。词族包括 macrocosms（复数）、macrocosmic（大宇宙的；整体世界的）、macrocosmically（从大宇宙或整体层面看）；microcosm（小宇宙；缩影）是结构对应的对比词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: macro- ('large' or 'large-scale') + -cosm, a bound element meaning 'world' or 'universe.' The family includes macrocosms, macrocosmic, and macrocosmically. Microcosm is its structurally parallel contrasting term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: universe 通常指全部时空及其中的事物；cosmos 常强调宇宙作为有秩序的整体；world 可指人类社会或某个活动领域。macrocosm 特别突出“大整体与较小对应体系”的关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Universe usually means all space, time, and their contents; cosmos often presents the universe as an ordered whole; world can mean human society or a particular sphere of activity. Macrocosm especially emphasizes a larger whole in relation to a smaller corresponding system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: macro 是“大”，cosm 是“世界”：把镜头拉远，看到包含局部的整体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Macro means 'large' and cosm means 'world': zoom out from a small part to the encompassing whole.

etymology_story.zh: microsurgery 是现代医学构词，由源自希腊语 mikros（小）的 micro- 加 surgery（外科手术）组成。其含义发展为借助显微镜处理微小组织结构的手术技术，而非仅指切口很小的手术。
etymology_story.en: Microsurgery is a modern medical formation combining micro-, from Greek mikros ('small'), with surgery. It came to denote operations on tiny structures under microscopic magnification, rather than simply operations with small incisions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：micro-（微小；此处也关联显微技术）+ surgery（外科手术）。词族包括 microsurgeon（显微外科医生）、microsurgeons（医生复数）、microsurgical（显微外科的）、microsurgically（通过显微外科技术）；microsurgery 通常作不可数名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: micro- ('small,' here also associated with microscopy) + surgery. The family includes microsurgeon, microsurgeons, microsurgical, and microsurgically. Microsurgery is normally an uncountable noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: microscopic surgery 是解释性的近义表达，强调显微镜辅助；reconstructive surgery 指重建形态或功能的手术，其中一部分采用显微技术；minimally invasive surgery 强调减少切口和组织损伤，与 microsurgery 并不等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Microscopic surgery is a descriptive near-equivalent emphasizing microscope assistance. Reconstructive surgery restores form or function and may use microsurgical techniques. Minimally invasive surgery emphasizes limiting incisions and tissue disruption and is not equivalent to microsurgery.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Micro + surgery: magnify the view to operate on tiny vessels and nerves.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 moire 借自法语 moire，法语词又源于英语 mohair，最初与毛织物有关，后来用于表面经过加工而呈水波纹的织物。织物名称进一步用于指重复图案叠加时出现的类似波纹；英语也常保留法语拼写 moiré。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed moire from French moire, which came from English mohair; the name shifted from a type of cloth to fabric finished with a watered appearance. It later also named similar interference patterns created by overlapping repeating designs, and the French-style spelling moiré remains common in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 moire／moiré 是借入的完整词基，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀；名词与形容词同形。词形及相关形式：复数 moires／moirés（多种波纹织物或纹样）；moired／moiréed（经过波纹加工的）；moiré pattern（摩尔纹图案）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, moire/moiré is a borrowed whole base, without a useful English root-and-affix division; its noun and adjective forms are identical. Forms and related expressions include plural moires/moirés, meaning types of fabric or patterns; moired/moiréed, meaning given a watered finish; and moiré pattern.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: watered silk（波纹绸）专指具有水波纹外观的丝织物；interference pattern（干涉图样）是范围更广的技术术语；wavy（波浪状的）只描述形状，不说明织物加工或图案叠加的成因。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Watered silk specifically names silk with a rippled appearance; interference pattern is a broader technical term; wavy describes shape without identifying a textile finish or overlapping-pattern mechanism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住同一个视觉核心：绸面像水波，图案叠加也会显出“水波”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep one visual anchor: watered silk looks rippled, and overlapping patterns can create similar ripples.

forms: 可数名词；复数 phantasmagorias。
family: phantasmagoric 梦幻般变幻的；phantasm 幻象

morphology.text: phantasmagoria 整词作为独立词素记忆；phantasmagor-（去掉 -ia 的词干）+ -ic → phantasmagoric（梦幻般变幻的）。

etymology.text: 借自法语 phantasmogorie，后来写作 fantasmagorie，原指在暗处用幻灯制造鬼影的表演；由此发展出“一连串变幻幻象”的意思。

usage_note: 文学性较强，强调真实或想象中的影像纷繁变化，不只是一个静止的幻影。

senses.meaning_zh: 变幻不定的梦幻景象；纷繁怪诞的幻象
senses.meaning_en: a rapidly changing, dreamlike succession of strange images
senses.english_definition: A phantasmagoria is a strange mixture or sequence of images that seem unreal and change like scenes in a dream.
senses.collocation_en: a phantasmagoria of images; a surreal phantasmagoria
senses.collocation_zh: 一连串变幻的幻象；超现实的梦幻景象
senses.sentence_en: The film unfolds as a phantasmagoria of childhood memories and imagined disasters.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部电影将童年记忆与想象中的灾难交织成一连串变幻不定的梦幻景象。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词借自法语，最初用于十八世纪末利用幻灯投射鬼怪影像的表演，其前部与希腊语 phantasma（幻象、幽灵）有关。词义后来从具体的幻灯鬼影表演扩展为任何纷繁、怪异且不断变幻的景象。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French, the word originally named late-eighteenth-century shows that projected ghostly images with magic lanterns; its first element is related to Greek phantasma, meaning an apparition. It later broadened to any bewildering succession of strange, shifting images.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 phantasmagoria 作为整体词基；理解时可联系 phantasm（幻象），但不宜把整个词硬拆成规则的现代英语构词公式。词族：phantasmagorias（复数）；phantasmagoric、phantasmagorical（幻象般变幻的）；phantasmagorically（如变幻幻象般地）；相关词有 phantasm（幻象）、phantasmal（幻影般的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats phantasmagoria as a whole base; phantasm provides a useful semantic connection, but the full word is not a transparent modern English formation. Its family includes plural phantasmagorias, adjectives phantasmagoric and phantasmagorical, and adverb phantasmagorically; related words include phantasm, an apparition, and phantasmal, resembling an apparition.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kaleidoscope（万花筒般的变化）强调色彩丰富、组合不断改变，不一定怪异；dreamscape（梦境般的场景）强调整体环境，不一定连续变换；幻觉义的 hallucination（幻觉）强调没有相应外部刺激的感知，而 phantasmagoria 也可描述真实艺术作品呈现的效果。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kaleidoscope emphasizes colorful, changing combinations without necessarily suggesting strangeness; dreamscape emphasizes a dreamlike setting rather than a sequence; hallucination denotes perception without a corresponding external stimulus, whereas a phantasmagoria can be an effect created by an actual artwork.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从历史画面记：幻灯里的鬼影接连变换，便是一场 phantasmagoria。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the historical show: ghostly lantern images changing one after another form a phantasmagoria.

senses.meaning_zh: 照片；图片（非正式用语）
senses.meaning_en: photographs or pictures, informally
senses.english_definition: Pix are photographs or pictures, especially when you refer to them in informal writing.

senses.collocation_zh: 度假照片；发布照片
senses.sentence_en: She posted a few pix from her weekend trip.
senses.sentence_zh: 她发布了几张周末旅行的照片。

etymology_story.zh: pix 是 pics 的按音改写形式，而 pics 是 pic（picture 的缩略形式）的复数。字母 x 表示 /ks/，这种简短拼写在二十世纪的非正式文字和新闻用语中流行，后来也常见于网络交流。
etymology_story.en: Pix is a respelling of pics, the plural of pic, which is a shortening of picture. The letter x represents /ks/; this compact spelling became established in twentieth-century informal and journalistic writing and later appeared widely online.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词路径：picture（图片）→ pic（截短形式）→ pic + -s → pics → pix（把 /ks/ 改写成 x）。pix 本身已是复数，通常不再加 -s；单数用 pic 或 picture。相关词族：picture、pictures、pictured（描绘了的；图示的）、picturing（描绘；想象）、pictorial（图画的）、pictorially（用图画地）、picturesque（风景如画的）、picturesquely（如画般地）、picturesqueness（如画之美）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: picture → clipped form pic → pic + plural -s → pics → respelled pix, with x representing /ks/. Pix is already plural and normally takes no additional -s; use pic or picture for the singular. Related family members include picture, pictures, pictured, picturing, pictorial, pictorially, picturesque, picturesquely, and picturesqueness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pics（照片、图片）与 pix 基本同义，是更直接体现复数结构的拼写；photos（照片）明确指摄影图像；pictures（图片、照片）范围更广，也可包括绘画等非摄影图像。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pics has essentially the same meaning as pix and displays the plural ending more transparently; photos specifically means photographic images; pictures is broader and can also include drawings and paintings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pic 加 s 读 /pɪks/，把末尾的 /ks/ 写成 x，就是 pix。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pic plus s sounds like /pɪks/: write the final /ks/ as x to get pix.

senses.meaning_zh: 前列腺切除术：切除部分或全部前列腺的手术
senses.meaning_en: surgical removal of part or all of the prostate
senses.english_definition: A prostatectomy is an operation in which a surgeon removes part or all of the prostate gland.
senses.collocation_en: undergo a prostatectomy; radical prostatectomy
senses.collocation_zh: 接受前列腺切除术；根治性前列腺切除术
senses.sentence_en: He underwent a prostatectomy after discussing the treatment options with his surgeon.
senses.sentence_zh: 他与外科医生讨论治疗方案后，接受了前列腺切除术。

etymology_story.zh: 这个现代医学词由 prostate（前列腺）和源自希腊语的 -ectomy（切除术）构成；prostate 的词源与希腊语 prostatēs（站在前面者）有关。手术名称直接表达“切除前列腺”，具体切除范围由术式限定。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term combines prostate with the Greek-derived surgical element -ectomy, meaning excision; prostate ultimately relates to Greek prostatēs, meaning one who stands in front. The name directly identifies removal of prostate tissue, with the particular procedure determining its extent.

morphology_enriched.zh: prostat-（prostate 的词干，前列腺）+ -ectomy（切除术）→ prostatectomy。词形：prostatectomies（复数）；prostatectomized／prostatectomised（已接受前列腺切除术的，专业用语）。相关医学词族：prostate（前列腺）、prostatic（前列腺的）、prostatitis（前列腺炎）；其中 prostatitis 并非由 prostatectomy 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Prostat-, the stem of prostate, + -ectomy, surgical removal, → prostatectomy. Forms include plural prostatectomies and the specialist adjective prostatectomized/prostatectomised, meaning having undergone the operation. Related medical terms include prostate, prostatic, and prostatitis, inflammation of the prostate; prostatitis is not derived from prostatectomy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prostate removal（前列腺切除）是通俗说法，需结合语境明确范围；prostate resection（前列腺切除术）强调切除组织，常用于部分切除的语境；radical prostatectomy（根治性前列腺切除术）是一种具体术式，通常切除整个前列腺及精囊，不能与所有 prostatectomy 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prostate removal is a plain-language equivalent whose extent depends on context; prostate resection emphasizes cutting away tissue and often occurs in discussions of partial removal; radical prostatectomy is a specific procedure generally removing the entire prostate and seminal vesicles, so it is not interchangeable with every prostatectomy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 认器官，再认手术：prostat- 指前列腺，-ectomy 指切除。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Identify the organ, then the operation: prostat- means prostate, and -ectomy means surgical removal.

etymology_story.zh: puffball 是 puff（一小团喷出的气体或粉末）与 ball（球）的复合词，名称描绘了球状菌体受扰时喷出孢子的现象。后来这个名称也用于下摆蓬起、轮廓圆鼓的裙装。
etymology_story.en: Puffball combines puff, a small burst or cloud, with ball, describing a rounded fungus that emits spores when disturbed. The name was later also applied to skirts and dresses with a full, rounded outline.

morphology_enriched.zh: puff（喷出一团；鼓起）+ ball（球）→ puffball；复数为 puffballs。在 puffball skirt 等搭配中，puffball 可作名词定语。词族及构词成分的相关形式：puff（名词、动词）、puffs、puffed（鼓起的；喷出了）、puffing（喷出；喘气）、puffy（膨起的）、puffiness（浮肿；蓬松）、ball（球）、balls（复数）。
morphology_enriched.en: Puff, suggesting a burst or swelling, + ball → puffball; the plural is puffballs. In expressions such as puffball skirt, puffball can function as a noun modifier. Family members and forms of its components include puff as noun and verb, puffs, puffed, puffing, puffy, puffiness, ball, and balls.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fungus（真菌）是范围更广的上位词；mushroom（蘑菇）常让人联想到有菌盖和菌柄的形态，不能准确替代所有 puffball；bubble skirt（泡泡裙）与服装义的 puffball skirt 接近，突出蓬起且向内收拢的下摆。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fungus is the broader biological category; mushroom often suggests a cap-and-stem form and is not an exact substitute for every puffball; bubble skirt closely matches the clothing sense of puffball skirt, emphasizing a full shape with a tucked-under hem.

mnemonic_anchor.en: A ball that gives a puff of spores is a puffball; a skirt puffed into a rounded shape shares the name.

etymology_story.zh: 这个词由表示“五”的拉丁语来源成分 quin- 与 centenary（百周年；百周年的）组合而成，背后的拉丁语词根分别是 quinque（五）和 centum（一百）。它既表示五百周年这一时间节点，也表示相关纪念活动。
etymology_story.en: The word combines the Latin-derived element quin-, meaning 'five', with centenary, ultimately drawing on Latin quinque, 'five', and centum, 'hundred'. It denotes both a five-hundredth anniversary and the celebrations associated with it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：quin-（五）＋ centenary（百周年；百周年的）→ quincentenary；同形兼作名词和形容词。名词复数为 quincentenaries；相关词有 centenary（百周年）和近义词 quincentennial（五百周年；五百周年的），后者不是由 quincentenary 直接派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: quin- ('five') + centenary ('a hundredth anniversary; relating to one') → quincentenary, used as both noun and adjective. The noun plural is quincentenaries. Related vocabulary includes centenary and the equivalent quincentennial; quincentennial is a parallel formation rather than a direct derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: quincentennial（五百周年；五百周年的）与本词基本同义；anniversary（周年纪念）不限定周年数；commemoration（纪念活动）强调纪念行为，也不一定在周年举行。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Quincentennial is essentially equivalent. Anniversary does not specify the number of years, while commemoration emphasizes an act of remembrance and need not take place on an anniversary.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: quin- 表示五，centenary 表示百周年：五个一百年，就是五百周年。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Five hundreds: quin- supplies five, and centenary supplies the hundred-year anniversary.

etymology_story.en: Rawhide is an English compound of raw and hide, both words with Old English ancestry. Here raw chiefly means 'untanned', rather than necessarily untouched by cleaning or drying.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：raw（未加工的）＋ hide（兽皮）→ rawhide。材料名词通常不可数；表示多张生皮时可用复数 rawhides。形容词与名词同形，置于名词前的材料用法也常分析为名词作定语；常见复合表达有 rawhide-covered（覆有生皮的）和 rawhide-bound（用生皮捆扎的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: raw ('unprocessed') + hide ('animal skin') → rawhide. The material noun is usually uncountable; rawhides can refer to individual skins. The adjective has the same form, and material uses before another noun are also often analyzed as attributive noun uses. Compounds include rawhide-covered and rawhide-bound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hide（兽皮）是较宽泛的名称，不限定是否鞣制；untanned hide（未鞣制兽皮）最接近 rawhide；leather（皮革）通常指经过鞣制的材料，与 rawhide 在加工方式和性能上有区别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hide is broader and does not itself specify tanning status. Untanned hide is the closest equivalent. Leather normally refers to tanned material and therefore differs from rawhide in processing and properties.

etymology_story.zh: rechecked 来自 recheck，由表示“再次”的拉丁语来源前缀 re- 加 check 构成，再加过去式或过去分词词尾 -ed。check 的检查义是在其更早的“阻止、约束”等意义基础上发展起来的；其词源可追溯到国际象棋中的“将军”。
etymology_story.en: Rechecked is formed from recheck, which combines the Latin-derived prefix re-, meaning 'again', with check, followed by the past-tense or past-participle ending -ed. The examination sense of check developed from earlier senses involving restraint or control; the word ultimately traces back to the chess expression 'check'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：re-（再次）＋ check（检查）＋ -ed（过去式或过去分词）→ rechecked；check 以清辅音 /k/ 结尾，因此 -ed 读 /t/。核心屈折词族：recheck、rechecks、rechecking、rechecked；基础词族包括 check、checks、checked、checking、checker（检查者；检查工具）、checkable（可核查的）和 unchecked（未经检查的；未受控制的）。rechecked 本身通常是动词形式，不另立常用独立形容词义。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: re- ('again') + check ('examine') + -ed (past tense or past participle) → rechecked. Because check ends in the voiceless consonant /k/, -ed is pronounced /t/. Core inflected forms are recheck, rechecks, rechecking, and rechecked. The base family includes check, checks, checked, checking, checker, checkable, and unchecked. Rechecked is normally a verb form rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: double-checked（再次仔细核对了）强调为确保无误而多查一遍；reviewed（复查了；审阅了）范围更广，可包括重新评价；verified（核实了）强调确认真实性或准确性，但不一定表示此前已检查过。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Double-checked emphasizes an additional careful check for reassurance. Reviewed is broader and can include reconsideration or evaluation. Verified emphasizes establishing truth or accuracy without necessarily implying an earlier check.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: re- 是“再来一次”：check 一遍之后又 check，已经做完就是 rechecked。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Check, then check again: re- repeats the action, and -ed places it in the past or marks a participle.

etymology_story.zh: regolith 由希腊语 rhēgos（毯子；覆盖物）和 lithos（石头）组合造出，字面意象是“盖在岩石上的毯子”。这个地质学术语后来也广泛用于月球等天体表面的松散覆盖层，不限于地球上由风化产生的物质。
etymology_story.en: Regolith was coined from Greek rhēgos, 'blanket or covering', and lithos, 'stone', giving the image of a blanket over rock. The geological term also came to be widely used for loose surface material on bodies such as the Moon, rather than only material produced by weathering on Earth.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：rego-（覆盖物，源自希腊语）＋ -lith（石）→ regolith；这属于学术合成词，而不是普通英语自由词的组合。材料名词通常不可数，比较不同覆盖层时可用 regoliths；相关形容词为 regolithic（风化层的）。含相同石义成分的词有 lithology（岩性；岩石学）和 lithosphere（岩石圈），它们不是 regolith 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: rego- ('covering', from Greek) + -lith ('stone') → regolith, a learned compound rather than a combination of ordinary independent English words. It is usually an uncountable material noun; regoliths can distinguish different deposits or types. The related adjective is regolithic. Lithology and lithosphere share the stone-related element but are not direct derivatives of regolith.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: soil（土壤）通常指具有特定形成过程和性质的表层物质，只是风化覆盖层的一部分；unconsolidated material（未固结物质）强调松散状态，不限定位置；overburden（覆盖层）强调盖在某个地层或矿体之上的材料，也可能包含坚硬岩层。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Soil usually denotes surface material with particular formation processes and properties and is only part of the broader category of regolith. Unconsolidated material emphasizes looseness without specifying location. Overburden emphasizes material above a deposit or formation and may include solid rock.

etymology_story.zh: spritzer 借自德语 Spritzer，与 spritzen（喷；溅）同源，保留了液体飞溅的意象。在英语中，它主要指葡萄酒兑气泡水的饮料，后来也扩展用于类似的果汁气泡饮料。
etymology_story.en: Spritzer was borrowed from German Spritzer, related to spritzen, 'to spray or splash', retaining an image of splashing liquid. In English it chiefly names wine mixed with sparkling water and has also extended to similar fizzy juice drinks.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在德语中可分析为 spritz-（喷、溅的动词词干）＋ -er（名词后缀）；英语主要把 spritzer 作为整体借词使用。复数为 spritzers；相关英语词有 spritz（喷洒；少量喷出的液体）、spritzes、spritzed 和 spritzing，但不能简单把英语饮料义 spritzer 理解为“喷洒的人”。
morphology_enriched.en: In German, the word can be analyzed as spritz-, a verb stem meaning 'spray or splash', plus the noun-forming suffix -er. English primarily uses spritzer as an established borrowing, with the plural spritzers. Related English forms include spritz, spritzes, spritzed, and spritzing, but the drink name does not simply mean 'a person who spritzes'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wine and soda（葡萄酒兑苏打水）直接说明经典配方；wine cooler（葡萄酒调饮）通常也含果味或甜味成分，不完全等同于 spritzer；spritz（斯普利茨鸡尾酒）在饮料语境中常指含起泡酒、苦味开胃酒和苏打水的一类鸡尾酒，配方更具体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wine and soda directly describes the classic mixture. A wine cooler commonly includes fruit flavoring or sweet ingredients and is not an exact equivalent. In drink terminology, a spritz often denotes a cocktail combining sparkling wine, a bitter aperitif, and soda water, making its recipe more specific.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住 spritz 的“喷、溅”：给葡萄酒添一股气泡水，就得到 spritzer。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect spritz with a splash: add a splash of sparkling water to wine to make a spritzer.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 tiki 借自毛利语及相关波利尼西亚语言，与一些传统中名为 Tiki 的始祖或造人者有关，后来用于称呼相应的人形雕刻。20世纪，美国商业娱乐文化又将这个词用于受波利尼西亚意象启发的酒吧、饮品与装饰风格。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed tiki from Māori and related Polynesian languages, connecting it with Tiki, an ancestral or creator figure in some traditions, and with associated human-shaped carvings. In the twentieth century, American commercial entertainment culture extended the word to bars, drinks, and decoration inspired by Polynesian imagery.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tiki 是不可再分析的借入词，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀。复数为 tikis（多个提基像）；常见复合表达有 tiki bar（提基酒吧）、tiki culture（提基文化）；tiki-like（像提基像的）是可按规则临时构成的形容词，并非固定的核心派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tiki is an unanalyzable loanword rather than a combination of English roots and affixes. Its plural is tikis; common compounds include tiki bar and tiki culture. Tiki-like is a possible productive adjective, rather than an established core derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的通用近义词：carving（雕刻品）强调制作方式，范围更广；figurine（小雕像）强调体积小；idol（神像）强调宗教崇拜功能，不能据此认定所有 tiki 都是供奉对象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact general synonym: carving emphasizes how an object is made and is broader; figurine emphasizes a small sculpted figure; idol implies a religious object of worship, a function that should not be assumed for every tiki.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“Tiki 人物”联想到“人形雕刻”，再联想到使用这类意象的提基装饰风格。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the figure Tiki with human-shaped carvings, then with the decorative style that uses this imagery.

etymology_story.zh: 这是由希腊语来源的医学构词成分组成的词：tracheo- 指气管，-stomy 源于表示“口、开口”的 stoma。trachea 的名称最终与希腊语“粗糙的”有关，原指气管软骨环造成的粗糙外观。
etymology_story.en: This medical formation combines Greek-derived tracheo-, meaning the windpipe, with -stomy, from stoma, meaning a mouth or opening. Trachea ultimately comes from a Greek adjective meaning rough, referring to the windpipe's cartilaginous rings.

morphology_enriched.zh: trache/o（气管，o 为连接元音）+ -stomy（外科造口术）→ tracheostomy。复数：tracheostomies；相关构词：tracheostomal（气管造口的）、tracheostomize（施行气管造口术，专业用语）、tracheostomized（已接受气管造口术的）；同根术语 tracheotomy（气管切开术）采用表示“切开”的 -tomy。
morphology_enriched.en: Trache/o, meaning windpipe and containing the linking vowel o, + -stomy, meaning surgical creation of an opening, forms tracheostomy. Related forms include the plural tracheostomies, tracheostomal, the specialist verb tracheostomize, and tracheostomized. The related term tracheotomy uses -tomy, meaning incision.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关术语并非完全等义：tracheotomy（气管切开术）强调切开气管，临床用语中有时与 tracheostomy 重叠；stoma（造口）可指身体多种部位的人工开口；surgical airway（外科气道）是更广的上位表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms are not exact synonyms: tracheotomy emphasizes the incision into the windpipe, although clinical usage sometimes overlaps with tracheostomy; stoma can describe an artificial opening at various body sites; surgical airway is a broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tracheo- 是“气管”，-stomy 是“造一个口”：给气管建立开口。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tracheo- means windpipe; -stomy means making an opening: create an opening into the windpipe.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 tutelarius，意为“保护的、监护的”，其基础是 tutela（保护、监护），最终与 tueri（看护、守护）有关。英语沿用了这种守护含义，尤其常用于保护特定人物或地方的神灵。
etymology_story.en: Tutelary comes from Latin tutelarius, meaning protective or relating to guardianship, based on tutela, protection or guardianship, and ultimately tueri, to watch over. English retained this protective meaning, particularly for deities or spirits associated with particular people or places.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按学术词干 tutel-（保护、监护）+ -ary（具有……性质的）理解，但它在历史上是整体借入的词。相关词有 tutelar（守护的，较少用）、tutelage（监护；指导）、tutor（导师；辅导）；tutorship（导师职位或职责）和 tutorial（辅导的；辅导课）属于 tutor 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be understood as the learned stem tutel-, protection or guardianship, + -ary, relating to, although historically it was borrowed as a whole. Related words include the less common tutelar, tutelage, and tutor; tutorship and tutorial are derivatives of tutor.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: protective（保护的）最通用，强调防止伤害；guardian（守护的，如 guardian spirit）强调持续看护；patron（庇护的，如 patron deity）强调神灵与特定群体、职业或地方的庇护关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Protective is the broadest term and emphasizes preventing harm; guardian, as in guardian spirit, emphasizes continuing watchfulness; patron, as in patron deity, emphasizes a protective association with a particular group, occupation, or place.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 与 tutor、tutelage 联系：从“照看和指导”记住“守护”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link it with tutor and tutelage: watching over and guiding someone leads to the idea of guardianship.

senses.meaning_zh: 发出高亢悠长的呼号声；发出颤动的长声
senses.meaning_en: To make a long, high, wavering cry, especially in grief or celebration.
senses.english_definition: If someone ululates, they make a long, high sound with their voice, often expressing grief or celebration.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 ululare（嚎叫、哀号），通过其分词词干 ululat- 进入英语。拉丁词本身具有拟声性质，模仿悠长的呼号；英语中的用法既可表达悲痛，也可表达欢庆。
etymology_story.en: Ululate comes from Latin ululare, to howl or wail, through its participial stem ululat-. The Latin verb is imitative of a prolonged cry, and English usage includes both mourning and celebration.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 ululate 是借入的动词词基，不宜硬拆为有独立意义的 ulu- + -late。屈折形式：ululates、ululated、ululating；派生词：ululate 去掉词尾 e + -ion → ululation（高亢的呼号；颤声）；另有较少用的 ululator（发出这种呼号的人）和 ululatory（呼号的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ululate is a borrowed verb base, not a meaningful combination of ulu- and -late. Its inflected forms are ululates, ululated, and ululating. Dropping the final e and adding -ion gives ululation; less common derivatives include ululator and ululatory.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: howl（嚎叫）强调响亮而拖长的声音，也常用于动物；wail（哀号）通常突出悲伤或痛苦；trill（发颤音）突出声音快速颤动，但不一定是呼号或表达强烈情绪。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Howl emphasizes a loud, prolonged cry and is also common for animals; wail usually foregrounds grief or distress; trill emphasizes rapid vocal vibration without necessarily implying a cry or strong emotion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 ulu 的反复声音联想成“呜——噜——”的长颤声；这是拟声联想，不是英语词素拆分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear the repeated ulu sounds as a long, wavering cry; this is a sound association, not an English morpheme breakdown.

usage_note: 包括蜘蛛、蝎子、螨和蜱等。蛛形纲动物通常有四对足，不能把这个词直接等同于 insect。

senses.meaning_en: An arthropod belonging to the class that includes spiders, scorpions, ticks, and mites.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自法语 arachnide，其基础是希腊语 arakhnē，意为“蜘蛛”。这一名称被用于整个蛛形纲，因此含义不限于蜘蛛，也包括蝎子、蜱和螨等动物。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed arachnid from French arachnide, based on Greek arakhnē, meaning spider. The name was applied to the whole zoological class, extending beyond spiders to animals such as scorpions, ticks, and mites.

morphology_enriched.zh: arachn-（蜘蛛）+ -id（类群成员）→ arachnid；复数为 arachnids，形容词形式同形。相关学术构词包括 arachnology（蛛形动物学）、arachnologist（蛛形动物学家）、arachnological（蛛形动物学的）、arachnophobia（蜘蛛恐惧症）、arachnophobic（恐惧蜘蛛的）和 arachnoid（蛛网状的；蛛网膜），这些词共享 arachn- / arachno-，并非都直接由 arachnid 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Arachn-, meaning spider, + -id, indicating a member of a group, forms arachnid; the plural is arachnids, and the adjective has the same form. Related learned formations include arachnology, arachnologist, arachnological, arachnophobia, arachnophobic, and arachnoid. These share arachn- or arachno- rather than all deriving directly from arachnid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的常用近义词：arachnidan 是较少用的同义名词；spider（蜘蛛）只指其中一类，范围更窄；arthropod（节肢动物）范围更广，也包括昆虫和甲壳类动物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym: arachnidan is a less common equivalent noun; spider denotes only one subgroup and is narrower; arthropod is broader and also includes insects and crustaceans.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: arachn- 联想“蜘蛛”，-id 联想“这一类的成员”：蛛形纲包括蜘蛛和它的同纲动物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link arachn- with spider and -id with group membership: arachnids include spiders and the other animals in their class.

usage_note: 常修饰 economy、policy、state，强调经济上减少或摆脱对进口的依赖；不是 autocratic（专制的）。

senses.meaning_zh: 经济上自给自足的；实行经济自给政策的
senses.meaning_en: Economically self-sufficient or pursuing economic self-sufficiency.
senses.english_definition: An autarkic country or economy produces what it needs itself and seeks to avoid dependence on foreign trade.
senses.definition_zh: 一个自给自足的国家或经济体自行生产所需物资，并力求避免依赖对外贸易。
senses.collocation_en: an autarkic economy; autarkic policies

etymology_story.zh: 由 autarky 的词干 autark- 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成；autarky 源自希腊语 autarkeia，意为“自足”，其基础成分是 autos（自己）和 arkein（足够、满足需要）。英语中的这一形容词尤其用于描述国家或经济体追求经济自给的状态。
etymology_story.en: Autarkic combines the stem autark- from autarky with the adjective suffix -ic; autarky ultimately comes from Greek autarkeia, meaning self-sufficiency, based on autos, meaning self, and arkein, meaning to suffice. The English adjective is especially associated with countries or economies pursuing economic self-sufficiency.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：autark-（autarky 的词干）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ autarkic。词族包括 autarky（经济自给；自给政策）、autarkically（以经济自给的方式）、autarkist（经济自给主义者；经济自给主义的）和 autarkistic（经济自给主义的，较少见）；autarkical 是较少见的形容词变体。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: autark-, the stem of autarky, + -ic, an adjective suffix → autarkic. The family includes autarky, economic self-sufficiency or its pursuit; autarkically, in an autarkic manner; autarkist, an advocate of autarky or relating to autarky; and the less common adjective autarkistic. Autarkical is a less common adjective variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: self-sufficient（自给自足的）适用范围最广，可描述个人、家庭或国家；self-sustaining（能够自我维持的）强调持续运转而无须外部支持；economically independent（经济独立的）强调不受外部经济力量支配，但不排斥贸易。autarkic 更突出经济自给及减少对外贸易依赖。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Self-sufficient broadly describes people, households, or countries that meet their own needs; self-sustaining emphasizes continued operation without outside support; economically independent emphasizes freedom from external economic control without necessarily avoiding trade. Autarkic more specifically emphasizes economic self-sufficiency and reduced reliance on foreign trade.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: auto- 表示“自己”，历史成分 ark- 表示“足够”：自己生产就够用 → 经济自给的。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Auto- means self, and the historical element ark- conveys sufficiency: enough from your own production → economically self-sufficient.

usage_note: 负责监督甲板工作、绳索等事务的船员职务；不是掌握全船指挥权的船长。常用读音接近 bosun。

senses.meaning_en: A ship's crew member responsible for deck equipment and supervising deck work.
senses.english_definition: A boatswain is a member of a ship's crew who looks after its deck equipment and supervises the sailors doing deck work.

etymology_story.zh: 来自中古英语中由“船”和“侍从、仆役”构成的复合词；后一成分 swain 源自古诺尔斯语 sveinn，意为“男孩、侍从”。这个船上职称后来专指负责甲板设备并组织水手作业的水手长。
etymology_story.en: Boatswain comes from a Middle English compound meaning boat plus attendant or servant; its second element, swain, derives from Old Norse sveinn, meaning boy or attendant. The shipboard title came to designate the crew member responsible for deck equipment and the sailors' deck work.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可分析为 boat（船）+ swain（古义：侍从），但通常整体记忆，读音不按两个成分逐一拼读。复数为 boatswains；bosun、bo'sun 和 bos'n 是反映其读音的拼写变体；boatswain's mate（水手长助手；某些海军中的相关职衔）是复合表达，无常用的派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form can be analyzed as boat + swain, an archaic word for an attendant, but it is normally learned as a whole because its pronunciation does not follow the two written components separately. The plural is boatswains; bosun, bo'sun, and bos'n are pronunciation-based spelling variants. Boatswain's mate is a compound title for an assistant or a related naval position; there are no common derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bosun（水手长）与 boatswain 指同一职务，只是拼写不同；petty officer（海军军士）是更宽泛的军衔类别；deck supervisor（甲板作业主管）是描述职责的泛称，不一定是正式的水手长职称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bosun names exactly the same position as boatswain and differs only in spelling; petty officer is a broader naval rank category; deck supervisor is a descriptive expression for someone overseeing deck work and does not necessarily denote the formal boatswain position.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: boat（船）+ swain（侍从）：船上的资深管事 → 水手长；读音近似“BOH-sun”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Boat + swain, an attendant: the experienced person overseeing shipboard deck work → boatswain, pronounced approximately BOH-sun.

senses.english_definition: You describe someone or their behavior as cheapskate when they avoid spending money in a way that you think is unreasonable.

etymology_story.zh: 这是十九世纪末已有记录的英语复合词，由 cheap（此处指小气的）和旧俚语 skate（家伙，常带轻蔑意味）构成。这里的 skate 不是“溜冰”，这个组合用来贬称不肯花钱的人。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in the late nineteenth century, cheapskate combines cheap in its stingy sense with the older slang word skate, meaning a fellow, often contemptuously. Skate here does not refer to skating; the compound became a disparaging name for someone unwilling to spend money.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cheap（小气的）+ skate（旧俚语：家伙）→ cheapskate；名词复数为 cheapskates，同形词也作形容词。相关 cheap 词族包括 cheaper、cheapest、cheaply（便宜地；低劣地）、cheapness（便宜；低劣）和 cheapen（使贬值；使显得低俗），但这些词并不都保留“吝啬”的含义。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cheap, meaning stingy, + skate, an older slang term for a fellow → cheapskate; the noun plural is cheapskates, and the same form also functions as an adjective. The related cheap family includes cheaper, cheapest, cheaply, cheapness, and cheapen, although these words do not all retain the meaning of stinginess.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: miser（守财奴）强调积攒钱财且极不愿花钱；tightwad（吝啬鬼）同样口语化，突出把钱攥得很紧；penny-pincher（锱铢必较的人）突出连小钱也要计较。cheapskate 常用于批评具体消费场景中的小气行为。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Miser emphasizes accumulating money and strongly resisting spending it; tightwad is similarly informal and stresses holding tightly onto money; penny-pincher emphasizes excessive attention to even tiny expenses. Cheapskate often criticizes stinginess in a particular spending situation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cheap 在这里是“小气”，skate 是“家伙”：一个小气的家伙 → 吝啬鬼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cheap here means stingy, and skate means fellow: a stingy fellow → a cheapskate.

etymology_story.zh: 来自中古英语 chiteren，属于模仿短促、尖细声音的拟声词。其核心声音意象延续至今，常用来描写小动物或鸟类接连发出的细小叫声。
etymology_story.en: Chitter comes from Middle English chiteren and is an imitative word suggesting short, high-pitched sounds. That sound image survives in its use for the repeated small calls of animals and birds.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 chitter 视为整体词干，不宜把它硬拆成具有独立现代词义的 chit + -er。屈折形式为 chitters、chittered、chittering；chittering 也可作名词，表示连续的吱吱声；chitter 本身有较少见的名词用法。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chitter is best treated as a whole stem rather than forced into chit + -er with separate modern meanings. Its inflected forms are chitters, chittered, and chittering; chittering can also function as a noun for repeated high-pitched calls, while chitter itself has an uncommon noun use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chirp（啁啾；短促鸣叫）常指清脆而较分明的一声；twitter（啾啾叫）强调连续、轻快的鸟鸣；squeak（吱吱叫）强调尖细声，也可用于物体发声。chitter 尤其适合描写小动物接连发出的短促细声。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chirp often suggests a clear, relatively distinct short call; twitter emphasizes a light succession of bird calls; squeak emphasizes a thin, high sound and can also describe objects. Chitter is especially suited to a succession of short, fine sounds made by small animals.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 chitter 听成连续的“吱、吱、吱”：短促尖细的声音就是词义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear chitter as a repeated chit-chit-chit: the short, high sound directly suggests its meaning.

senses.meaning_zh: 时空体：叙事中相互联系并共同塑造事件的时间与空间结构

senses.english_definition: A chronotope is the way time and space are connected in a story and together shape its events and characters.

etymology_story.zh: 这一术语经俄语 khronotop 进入英语，其组成成分源自希腊语 khronos（时间）和 topos（地方）。巴赫金将其引入文学研究，用来讨论叙事中时间与空间不可分割的联系，而非仅仅指故事发生的地点。
etymology_story.en: The term entered English through Russian khronotop and is built from elements originating in Greek khronos, meaning time, and topos, meaning place. Bakhtin introduced it into literary study to discuss the inseparable relationship between narrative time and space, rather than location alone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：chrono-（时间）+ -tope（地方、空间）→ chronotope；复数为 chronotopes。主要派生词包括 chronotopic（时空体的）、chronotopical（时空体的，较少见）和 chronotopically（从时空体角度；以时空体方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: chrono-, meaning time, + -tope, meaning place or space → chronotope; the plural is chronotopes. Principal derivatives include chronotopic, relating to a chronotope; the less common adjective chronotopical; and chronotopically, from a chronotopic perspective or in a chronotopic manner.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: setting（故事背景）通常指故事发生的时间、地点及环境；spatiotemporal framework（时空框架）是描述时间与空间组织的一般表达。两者都不是严格同义词：chronotope 更强调时空关系如何塑造叙事事件、人物和体裁。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Setting usually denotes a story's time, place, and surrounding conditions; spatiotemporal framework is a general expression for the organization of time and space. Neither is an exact synonym: chronotope emphasizes how relationships between time and space shape narrative events, characters, and genres.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chrono- 是时间，-tope 是地方：把“何时”和“何地”编织成推动故事的整体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chrono- is time and -tope is place: weave when and where into one structure that shapes the story.
